## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/demos/notebooks/4_tpch.ipynb
````
   1: {
   2:  "cells": [
   3:   {
   4:    "cell_type": "markdown",
   5:    "id": "ff83342c-3b61-4475-ae5e-519daaf6923e",
   6:    "metadata": {},
   7:    "source": [
   8:     "# PyDough TPC-H\n",
   9:     "\n",
  10:     "This notebook provides PyDough translations for 19 out of the 22 TPC-H benchmark queries. For each query we will reproduce the business context, borrowing from the defintion provided in the specification, the corresponding SQL query, and finally a valid PyDough implementation. The underlying schema of this data matches this example image from [TPC Benchmark H Standard Specification](https://www.tpc.org/tpc_documents_current_versions/pdf/tpc-h_v2.17.1.pdf).\n",
  11:     "\n",
  12:     "![TPC-H schema from the Specification Document as of December 12, 2024](../images/tpc_h_schema.png)\n",
  13:     "\n",
  14:     "In several places we have updated the names in our metadata to be more human readable. It should also be noted that the TPC-H benchmark does not necessarily constitute the \"simplest\" way to express the SQL for each of these statements, but this comparison is still useful for understanding how to construct PyDough statements.\n",
  15:     "\n",
  16:     "In addition, since the demo consists of running the PyDough statements on SQLite, an OLTP database, some of these statements are significantly slower to complete than they would be if run instead on an OLAP database."
  17:    ]
  18:   },
  19:   {
  20:    "cell_type": "code",
  21:    "execution_count": null,
  22:    "id": "ec6b6ac7-e59a-41aa-b46a-0ff43f55369c",
  23:    "metadata": {},
  24:    "outputs": [],
  25:    "source": [
  26:     "%load_ext pydough.jupyter_extensions"
  27:    ]
  28:   },
  29:   {
  30:    "cell_type": "code",
  31:    "execution_count": null,
  32:    "id": "539536e2-21b0-412d-9114-9ef9a1a277f4",
  33:    "metadata": {},
  34:    "outputs": [],
  35:    "source": [
  36:     "import pydough\n",
  37:     "import datetime\n",
  38:     "import pandas as pd"
  39:    ]
  40:   },
  41:   {
  42:    "cell_type": "code",
  43:    "execution_count": null,
  44:    "id": "a8a35558-ba91-445b-8141-2ad0e72029dd",
  45:    "metadata": {},
  46:    "outputs": [],
  47:    "source": [
  48:     "# Setup demo metadata\n",
  49:     "pydough.active_session.load_metadata_graph(\"../metadata/tpch_demo_graph.json\", \"TPCH\");\n",
  50:     "pydough.active_session.connect_database(\"sqlite\", database=\"../../tpch.db\");\n",
  51:     "# Avoid scientific notation\n",
  52:     "pd.options.display.float_format = '{:.6f}'.format"
  53:    ]
  54:   },
  55:   {
  56:    "cell_type": "markdown",
  57:    "id": "18f1c949-5e3c-4bbf-9d3d-2f1c12ec3195",
  58:    "metadata": {},
  59:    "source": [
  60:     "## Query 1\n",
  61:     "\n",
  62:     "This query seeks to determine **the amount of business that was billed, shipped, and returned**. More specifically, it provides a summary pricing report for all line items shipped as of a given date. The date is within 90 days of the greatest ship date contained in the database.\n",
  63:     "\n",
  64:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
  65:     "\n",
  66:     "```SQL\n",
  67:     "select\n",
  68:     "\tl_returnflag,\n",
  69:     "\tl_linestatus,\n",
  70:     "\tsum(l_quantity) as sum_qty,\n",
  71:     "\tsum(l_extendedprice) as sum_base_price,\n",
  72:     "\tsum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as sum_disc_price,\n",
  73:     "\tsum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) * (1 + l_tax)) as sum_charge,\n",
  74:     "\tavg(l_quantity) as avg_qty,\n",
  75:     "\tavg(l_extendedprice) as avg_price,\n",
  76:     "\tavg(l_discount) as avg_disc,\n",
  77:     "\tcount(*) as count_order\n",
  78:     "from\n",
  79:     "\tlineitem\n",
  80:     "where\n",
  81:     "\tl_shipdate <= date '1998-12-01' - interval '90' day\n",
  82:     "group by\n",
  83:     "\tl_returnflag,\n",
  84:     "\tl_linestatus\n",
  85:     "order by\n",
  86:     "\tl_returnflag,\n",
  87:     "\tl_linestatus\n",
  88:     "```"
  89:    ]
  90:   },
  91:   {
  92:    "cell_type": "code",
  93:    "execution_count": null,
  94:    "id": "59d6e822-f77e-4dc2-b7d8-5cbb41ddf9b6",
  95:    "metadata": {},
  96:    "outputs": [],
  97:    "source": [
  98:     "%%pydough\n",
  99:     "\n",
 100:     "disc_price = lines.extended_price * (1 - lines.discount)\n",
 101:     "charge = disc_price * (1 + lines.tax)\n",
 102:     "selected_lines = lines.WHERE((ship_date <= datetime.date(1998, 9, 2)))\n",
 103:     "partitioned_lines = selected_lines.PARTITION(name=\"groups\", by=(return_flag, status))\n",
 104:     "output = partitioned_lines.CALCULATE(\n",
 105:     "    L_RETURNFLAG=return_flag,\n",
 106:     "    L_LINESTATUS=status,\n",
 107:     "    SUM_QTY=SUM(lines.quantity),\n",
 108:     "    SUM_BASE_PRICE=SUM(lines.extended_price),\n",
 109:     "    SUM_DISC_PRICE=SUM(disc_price),\n",
 110:     "    SUM_CHARGE=SUM(charge),\n",
 111:     "    AVG_QTY=AVG(lines.quantity),\n",
 112:     "    AVG_PRICE=AVG(lines.extended_price),\n",
 113:     "    AVG_DISC=AVG(lines.discount),\n",
 114:     "    COUNT_ORDER=COUNT(lines),\n",
 115:     ").ORDER_BY(return_flag.ASC(), status.ASC())\n",
 116:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 117:    ]
 118:   },
 119:   {
 120:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 121:    "id": "419981b5-0159-47b2-bc7f-da4e44707f7c",
 122:    "metadata": {},
 123:    "source": [
 124:     "## Query 2\n",
 125:     "\n",
 126:     "This question seeks to determine **which supplier should be selected to place an order for a given part in a given region**. More verbosely, it finds, in a given region, for each part of a certain type and size, the supplier who can supply it at minimum cost. If several suppliers in that region offer the desired part type and size at the same (minimum) cost, the query lists the parts from suppliers with the 100 highest account balances. For each supplier, the query lists the supplier's account balance, name and nation; the part's number and manufacturer; the supplier's address, phone number and comment information. The chosen region, part type, and size are Europe, brass parts, and 15, respectively.\n",
 127:     "\n",
 128:     "\n",
 129:     "\n",
 130:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 131:     "\n",
 132:     "```SQL\n",
 133:     "SELECT\n",
 134:     "    S_ACCTBAL,\n",
 135:     "    S_NAME,\n",
 136:     "    N_NAME,\n",
 137:     "    P_PARTKEY,\n",
 138:     "    P_MFGR,\n",
 139:     "    S_ADDRESS,\n",
 140:     "    S_PHONE,\n",
 141:     "    S_COMMENT\n",
 142:     "FROM\n",
 143:     "    PART,\n",
 144:     "    SUPPLIER,\n",
 145:     "    PARTSUPP,\n",
 146:     "    NATION,\n",
 147:     "    REGION\n",
 148:     "WHERE\n",
 149:     "    P_PARTKEY = PS_PARTKEY\n",
 150:     "    AND S_SUPPKEY = PS_SUPPKEY\n",
 151:     "    AND P_SIZE = 15\n",
 152:     "    AND P_TYPE LIKE '%BRASS'\n",
 153:     "    AND S_NATIONKEY = N_NATIONKEY\n",
 154:     "    AND N_REGIONKEY = R_REGIONKEY\n",
 155:     "    AND R_NAME = 'EUROPE'\n",
 156:     "    AND PS_SUPPLYCOST = (\n",
 157:     "        SELECT MIN(PS_SUPPLYCOST)\n",
 158:     "        FROM PARTSUPP, SUPPLIER, NATION, REGION\n",
 159:     "        WHERE P_PARTKEY = PS_PARTKEY\n",
 160:     "          AND S_SUPPKEY = PS_SUPPKEY\n",
 161:     "          AND S_NATIONKEY = N_NATIONKEY\n",
 162:     "          AND N_REGIONKEY = R_REGIONKEY\n",
 163:     "          AND R_NAME = 'EUROPE'\n",
 164:     "    )\n",
 165:     "ORDER BY\n",
 166:     "    S_ACCTBAL DESC,\n",
 167:     "    N_NAME,\n",
 168:     "    S_NAME,\n",
 169:     "    P_PARTKEY\n",
 170:     "LIMIT 100;\n",
 171:     "```\n",
 172:     "\n",
 173:     "Notice the use of a correlated subqueries to determine the `PS_SUPPLYCOST` criteria. In PyDough this is handled naturally by simply first peforming the partition, applying the filter, and then navigating back to `selected_parts` in question, which avoids fully stepping out of the query. "
 174:    ]
 175:   },
 176:   {
 177:    "cell_type": "code",
 178:    "execution_count": null,
 179:    "id": "27365f94-32a0-48f1-9589-711d57cf145b",
 180:    "metadata": {},
 181:    "outputs": [],
 182:    "source": [
 183:     "%%pydough\n",
 184:     "\n",
 185:     "selected_parts = (\n",
 186:     "        nations.CALCULATE(n_name=name)\n",
 187:     "        .WHERE(region.name == \"EUROPE\")\n",
 188:     "        .suppliers.CALCULATE(\n",
 189:     "            s_acctbal=account_balance,\n",
 190:     "            s_name=name,\n",
 191:     "            s_address=address,\n",
 192:     "            s_phone=phone,\n",
 193:     "            s_comment=comment,\n",
 194:     "        )\n",
 195:     "        .supply_records.CALCULATE(\n",
 196:     "            supplycost=supplycost,\n",
 197:     "        )\n",
 198:     "        .part.WHERE(ENDSWITH(part_type, \"BRASS\") & (size == 15))\n",
 199:     "    )\n",
 200:     "part_groups = selected_parts.PARTITION(name=\"groups\", by=key).CALCULATE(\n",
 201:     "    best_cost=MIN(part.supplycost)\n",
 202:     ")\n",
 203:     "output = part_groups.part.WHERE(\n",
 204:     "    (supplycost == best_cost)\n",
 205:     "    & ENDSWITH(part_type, \"BRASS\")\n",
 206:     "    & (size == 15)\n",
 207:     ").CALCULATE(\n",
 208:     "    S_ACCTBAL=s_acctbal,\n",
 209:     "    S_NAME=s_name,\n",
 210:     "    N_NAME=n_name,\n",
 211:     "    P_PARTKEY=key,\n",
 212:     "    P_MFGR=manufacturer,\n",
 213:     "    S_ADDRESS=s_address,\n",
 214:     "    S_PHONE=s_phone,\n",
 215:     "    S_COMMENT=s_comment,\n",
 216:     ").TOP_K(\n",
 217:     "    100,\n",
 218:     "    by=(S_ACCTBAL.DESC(), N_NAME.ASC(), S_NAME.ASC(), P_PARTKEY.ASC()),\n",
 219:     ")\n",
 220:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 221:    ]
 222:   },
 223:   {
 224:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 225:    "id": "c4979e37-388e-48df-9165-ecd3c71571c1",
 226:    "metadata": {},
 227:    "source": [
 228:     "## Query 3\n",
 229:     "\n",
 230:     "The question seeks to find **the 10 unshipped orders with the highest value**. More verbosely, it retrieves the shipping priority and potential revenue, defined as the sum of the extended price times one minus the discount, of the orders having the largest revenue among those that had not been shipped as of a given date. Orders are listed in decreasing order of revenue. If more than 10 unshipped orders exist, only the 10 orders with the largest revenue are listed.\n",
 231:     "\n",
 232:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 233:     "\n",
 234:     "```SQL\n",
 235:     "SELECT\n",
 236:     "    L_ORDERKEY,\n",
 237:     "    SUM(L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT)) AS REVENUE,\n",
 238:     "    O_ORDERDATE,\n",
 239:     "    O_SHIPPRIORITY\n",
 240:     "FROM\n",
 241:     "    CUSTOMER,\n",
 242:     "    ORDERS,\n",
 243:     "    LINEITEM\n",
 244:     "WHERE\n",
 245:     "    C_MKTSEGMENT = 'BUILDING'\n",
 246:     "    AND C_CUSTKEY = O_CUSTKEY\n",
 247:     "    AND L_ORDERKEY = O_ORDERKEY\n",
 248:     "    AND O_ORDERDATE < DATE '1995-03-15'\n",
 249:     "    AND L_SHIPDATE > DATE '1995-03-15'\n",
 250:     "GROUP BY\n",
 251:     "    L_ORDERKEY,\n",
 252:     "    O_ORDERDATE,\n",
 253:     "    O_SHIPPRIORITY\n",
 254:     "ORDER BY\n",
 255:     "    REVENUE DESC,\n",
 256:     "    O_ORDERDATE\n",
 257:     "LIMIT 10;\n",
 258:     "```\n",
 259:     "\n",
 260:     "PyDough allows us to first derive `selected_lines` as the data to be partitioned, before grouping it by certain partition keys to compute the aggregations."
 261:    ]
 262:   },
 263:   {
 264:    "cell_type": "code",
 265:    "execution_count": null,
 266:    "id": "95975cba-e8e2-4ac9-bbc2-874c0ab43418",
 267:    "metadata": {},
 268:    "outputs": [],
 269:    "source": [
 270:     "%%pydough\n",
 271:     "\n",
 272:     "cutoff_date = datetime.date(1995, 3, 15)\n",
 273:     "selected_orders = orders.CALCULATE(\n",
 274:     "    order_date, ship_priority\n",
 275:     ").WHERE(\n",
 276:     "    (customer.mktsegment == \"BUILDING\") & (order_date < cutoff_date)\n",
 277:     ")\n",
 278:     "selected_lines = selected_orders.lines.WHERE(ship_date > cutoff_date)\n",
 279:     "output = selected_lines.PARTITION(\n",
 280:     "    name=\"groups\", by=(order_key, order_date, ship_priority)\n",
 281:     ").CALCULATE(\n",
 282:     "    L_ORDERKEY=order_key,\n",
 283:     "    REVENUE=SUM(lines.extended_price * (1 - lines.discount)),\n",
 284:     "    O_ORDERDATE=order_date,\n",
 285:     "    O_SHIPPRIORITY=ship_priority,\n",
 286:     ").TOP_K(10, by=(REVENUE.DESC(), O_ORDERDATE.ASC(), L_ORDERKEY.ASC()))\n",
 287:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 288:    ]
 289:   },
 290:   {
 291:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 292:    "id": "a72bd083-12c7-402e-8b44-22d640308a7f",
 293:    "metadata": {},
 294:    "source": [
 295:     "## Query 4\n",
 296:     "\n",
 297:     "This question seeks to answer **how well the order priority system is working at ensuring that orders are delivered on time within a particular quarter**. It does this by counting the number of orders ordered in a given quarter of a given year in which at least one lineitem was received by the customer later than its committed date. The query lists the count of such orders for each order priority sorted in ascending priority order.\n",
 298:     "\n",
 299:     "\n",
 300:     "\n",
 301:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 302:     "\n",
 303:     "```SQL\n",
 304:     "SELECT\n",
 305:     "    O_ORDERPRIORITY,\n",
 306:     "    COUNT(*) AS ORDER_COUNT\n",
 307:     "FROM\n",
 308:     "    ORDERS\n",
 309:     "WHERE\n",
 310:     "    O_ORDERDATE >= DATE '1993-07-01'\n",
 311:     "    AND O_ORDERDATE < DATE '1993-10-01'\n",
 312:     "    AND EXISTS (\n",
 313:     "        SELECT 1\n",
 314:     "        FROM LINEITEM\n",
 315:     "        WHERE L_ORDERKEY = O_ORDERKEY\n",
 316:     "          AND L_COMMITDATE < L_RECEIPTDATE\n",
 317:     "    )\n",
 318:     "GROUP BY\n",
 319:     "    O_ORDERPRIORITY\n",
 320:     "ORDER BY\n",
 321:     "    O_ORDERPRIORITY;\n",
 322:     "```\n",
 323:     "\n",
 324:     "PyDough handles the `exists` functionality through its use of `HAS`, relying on the underlying relationship between collections to simplify the join/table logic."
 325:    ]
 326:   },
 327:   {
 328:    "cell_type": "code",
 329:    "execution_count": null,
 330:    "id": "e7525d29-7edc-4c41-9c48-c1313d6f07a4",
 331:    "metadata": {},
 332:    "outputs": [],
 333:    "source": [
 334:     "%%pydough\n",
 335:     "\n",
 336:     "selected_lines = lines.WHERE(commit_date < receipt_date)\n",
 337:     "selected_orders = orders.WHERE(\n",
 338:     "    (order_date >= datetime.date(1993, 7, 1))\n",
 339:     "    & (order_date < datetime.date(1993, 10, 1))\n",
 340:     "    & HAS(selected_lines)\n",
 341:     ")\n",
 342:     "output = selected_orders.PARTITION(name=\"priorities\", by=order_priority).CALCULATE(\n",
 343:     "    O_ORDERPRIORITY=order_priority,\n",
 344:     "    ORDER_COUNT=COUNT(orders),\n",
 345:     ").ORDER_BY(O_ORDERPRIORITY.ASC())\n",
 346:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 347:    ]
 348:   },
 349:   {
 350:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 351:    "id": "d6fee20d",
 352:    "metadata": {},
 353:    "source": [
 354:     "## Query 5\n",
 355:     "\n",
 356:     "This question seeks to learn about domestic revenue from suppliers in Asian countries. It does so by calculating, for each Asian country, the total revenue generated by suppliers in that nation shipping a part to a customer from the same nation, only considering shipments ordered in 1994. Revenue volume for all qualifying lineitems in a particular nation is defined as `sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount))`.\n",
 357:     "\n",
 358:     "\n",
 359:     "\n",
 360:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 361:     "\n",
 362:     "```SQL\n",
 363:     "select\n",
 364:     "    N_NAME,\n",
 365:     "    sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as REVENUE\n",
 366:     "from\n",
 367:     "    customer,\n",
 368:     "    orders,\n",
 369:     "    lineitem,\n",
 370:     "    supplier,\n",
 371:     "    nation,\n",
 372:     "    region\n",
 373:     "where\n",
 374:     "    c_custkey = o_custkey\n",
 375:     "    and l_orderkey = o_orderkey\n",
 376:     "    and l_suppkey = s_suppkey\n",
 377:     "    and c_nationkey = s_nationkey\n",
 378:     "    and s_nationkey = n_nationkey\n",
 379:     "    and n_regionkey = r_regionkey\n",
 380:     "    and r_name = 'ASIA'\n",
 381:     "    and o_orderdate >= '1994-01-01'\n",
 382:     "    and o_orderdate < '1995-01-01'\n",
 383:     "group by\n",
 384:     "    n_name\n",
 385:     "order by\n",
 386:     "    revenue desc\n",
 387:     "```"
 388:    ]
 389:   },
 390:   {
 391:    "cell_type": "code",
 392:    "execution_count": null,
 393:    "id": "4f8eb6d0",
 394:    "metadata": {},
 395:    "outputs": [],
 396:    "source": [
 397:     "%%pydough\n",
 398:     "\n",
 399:     "selected_lines = (\n",
 400:     "    customers.orders.WHERE(\n",
 401:     "        (order_date >= datetime.date(1994, 1, 1))\n",
 402:     "        & (order_date < datetime.date(1995, 1, 1))\n",
 403:     "    )\n",
 404:     "    .lines.WHERE(supplier.nation.name == nation_name)\n",
 405:     "    .CALCULATE(value=extended_price * (1 - discount))\n",
 406:     ")\n",
 407:     "output = (\n",
 408:     "    nations.CALCULATE(nation_name=name)\n",
 409:     "    .WHERE(region.name == \"ASIA\")\n",
 410:     "    .WHERE(HAS(selected_lines))\n",
 411:     "    .CALCULATE(N_NAME=name, REVENUE=SUM(selected_lines.value))\n",
 412:     "    .ORDER_BY(REVENUE.DESC())\n",
 413:     ")\n",
 414:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 415:    ]
 416:   },
 417:   {
 418:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 419:    "id": "c5c4d84b-b3c0-4b58-8635-b1d30ea2946a",
 420:    "metadata": {},
 421:    "source": [
 422:     "## Query 6\n",
 423:     "\n",
 424:     "This question formulated a sample \"what-if\" question, asking **how was revenue impacted over a previous year due to the presence of certain discounts** and potentially speculating on future revenue due to a change in that discount. It considers all the lineitems shipped in a given year with discounts in a certain value (in this case, 0.05 to 0.07). The query lists the amount by which the total revenue would have increased if these discounts had been eliminated for lineitems with l_quantity less than quantity. Note that the potential revenue increase is equal to the sum of the extended price times one minus the discount for all lineitems with discounts and quantities in the qualifying range. The chosen quantity range is quantity values below 24.\n",
 425:     "\n",
 426:     "\n",
 427:     "\n",
 428:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 429:     "\n",
 430:     "```SQL\n",
 431:     "SELECT\n",
 432:     "    SUM(L_EXTENDEDPRICE * L_DISCOUNT) AS REVENUE\n",
 433:     "FROM\n",
 434:     "    LINEITEM\n",
 435:     "WHERE\n",
 436:     "    L_SHIPDATE >= DATE '1994-01-01'\n",
 437:     "    AND L_SHIPDATE < DATE '1995-01-01'\n",
 438:     "    AND L_DISCOUNT BETWEEN 0.05 AND 0.07\n",
 439:     "    AND L_QUANTITY < 24;\n",
 440:     "```"
 441:    ]
 442:   },
 443:   {
 444:    "cell_type": "code",
 445:    "execution_count": null,
 446:    "id": "6e1edea5-63f0-4542-9bcc-16a3398abe22",
 447:    "metadata": {},
 448:    "outputs": [],
 449:    "source": [
 450:     "%%pydough\n",
 451:     "\n",
 452:     "selected_lines = lines.WHERE(\n",
 453:     "    (ship_date >= datetime.date(1994, 1, 1))\n",
 454:     "    & (ship_date < datetime.date(1995, 1, 1))\n",
 455:     "    & (0.05 <= discount)\n",
 456:     "    & (discount <= 0.07)\n",
 457:     "    & (quantity < 24)\n",
 458:     ").CALCULATE(amt=extended_price * discount)\n",
 459:     "output = TPCH.CALCULATE(REVENUE=SUM(selected_lines.amt))\n",
 460:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 461:    ]
 462:   },
 463:   {
 464:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 465:    "id": "3f4c5e4e-b038-4c83-b064-f730612378da",
 466:    "metadata": {},
 467:    "source": [
 468:     "## Query 7\n",
 469:     "\n",
 470:     "This question asks about **the value of goods shipped between certain nations within a particular year** as a representation for future contract negotiations. More specifically, it finds, for two given nations, the gross discounted revenues derived from lineitems in which parts were shipped from a supplier in either nation to a customer in the other nation during 1995 and 1996. The query lists the supplier nation, the customer nation, the year, and the revenue from shipments that took place in that year. The query orders the answer by Supplier nation, Customer nation, and year (all ascending). The two nations chosen are France and Germany.\n",
 471:     "\n",
 472:     "\n",
 473:     "\n",
 474:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 475:     "\n",
 476:     "```SQL\n",
 477:     "SELECT\n",
 478:     "    SUPP_NATION,\n",
 479:     "    CUST_NATION,\n",
 480:     "    L_YEAR,\n",
 481:     "    SUM(VOLUME) AS REVENUE\n",
 482:     "FROM (\n",
 483:     "    SELECT\n",
 484:     "        N1.N_NAME AS SUPP_NATION,\n",
 485:     "        N2.N_NAME AS CUST_NATION,\n",
 486:     "        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM L_SHIPDATE) AS L_YEAR,\n",
 487:     "        L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT) AS VOLUME\n",
 488:     "    FROM\n",
 489:     "        SUPPLIER,\n",
 490:     "        LINEITEM,\n",
 491:     "        ORDERS,\n",
 492:     "        CUSTOMER,\n",
 493:     "        NATION N1,\n",
 494:     "        NATION N2\n",
 495:     "    WHERE\n",
 496:     "        S_SUPPKEY = L_SUPPKEY\n",
 497:     "        AND O_ORDERKEY = L_ORDERKEY\n",
 498:     "        AND C_CUSTKEY = O_CUSTKEY\n",
 499:     "        AND S_NATIONKEY = N1.N_NATIONKEY\n",
 500:     "        AND C_NATIONKEY = N2.N_NATIONKEY\n",
 501:     "        AND (\n",
 502:     "            (N1.N_NAME = 'FRANCE' AND N2.N_NAME = 'GERMANY')\n",
 503:     "            OR (N1.N_NAME = 'GERMANY' AND N2.N_NAME = 'FRANCE')\n",
 504:     "        )\n",
 505:     "        AND L_SHIPDATE BETWEEN DATE '1995-01-01' AND DATE '1996-12-31'\n",
 506:     ") SHIPPING\n",
 507:     "GROUP BY\n",
 508:     "    SUPP_NATION,\n",
 509:     "    CUST_NATION,\n",
 510:     "    L_YEAR\n",
 511:     "ORDER BY\n",
 512:     "    SUPP_NATION,\n",
 513:     "    CUST_NATION,\n",
 514:     "    L_YEAR;\n",
 515:     "```"
 516:    ]
 517:   },

 538:     "    )\n",

 554:   {

 558:    "source": [
 559:     "## Query 8\n",
 560:     "\n",
 561:     "This question asks about **how the market share of a given nation within a given region has changed over two years for a given part type**. The market share for a given nation within a given region is defined as the fraction of the revenue, defined as the sum of the extended price times one minus the discount, from the products of a specified type in that region that was supplied by suppliers from the given nation. The query determines this for the years 1995 and 1996 presented in this order. The chosen nation, region, and product type are Brazil America, and `'ECONOMY ANODIZED STEEL'`, respectively.\n",
 562:     "\n",
 563:     "\n",
 564:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 565:     "\n",
 566:     "```SQL\n",
 567:     "SELECT\n",
 568:     "    O_YEAR,\n",
 569:     "    SUM(CASE\n",
 570:     "            WHEN NATION = 'BRAZIL' THEN VOLUME\n",
 571:     "            ELSE 0\n",
 572:     "        END) / SUM(VOLUME) AS MKT_SHARE\n",
 573:     "FROM (\n",
 574:     "    SELECT\n",
 575:     "        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM O_ORDERDATE) AS O_YEAR,\n",
 576:     "        L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT) AS VOLUME,\n",
 577:     "        N2.N_NAME AS NATION\n",
 578:     "    FROM\n",
 579:     "        PART,\n",
 580:     "        SUPPLIER,\n",
 581:     "        LINEITEM,\n",
 582:     "        ORDERS,\n",
 583:     "        CUSTOMER,\n",
 584:     "        NATION N1,\n",
 585:     "        NATION N2,\n",
 586:     "        REGION\n",
 587:     "    WHERE\n",
 588:     "        P_PARTKEY = L_PARTKEY\n",
 589:     "        AND S_SUPPKEY = L_SUPPKEY\n",
 590:     "        AND L_ORDERKEY = O_ORDERKEY\n",
 591:     "        AND O_CUSTKEY = C_CUSTKEY\n",
 592:     "        AND C_NATIONKEY = N1.N_NATIONKEY\n",
 593:     "        AND N1.N_REGIONKEY = R_REGIONKEY\n",
 594:     "        AND R_NAME = 'AMERICA'\n",
 595:     "        AND S_NATIONKEY = N2.N_NATIONKEY\n",
 596:     "        AND O_ORDERDATE BETWEEN DATE '1995-01-01' AND DATE '1996-12-31'\n",
 597:     "        AND P_TYPE = 'ECONOMY ANODIZED STEEL'\n",
 598:     ") ALL_NATIONS\n",
 599:     "GROUP BY\n",
 600:     "    O_YEAR\n",
 601:     "ORDER BY\n",
 602:     "    O_YEAR;\n",
 603:     "```"
 604:    ]
 605:   },
 606:   {
 607:    "cell_type": "code",
 608:    "execution_count": null,
 609:    "id": "b9339c6b-efa9-4460-a45b-d89196b21711",

 612:    "source": [
 613:     "%%pydough\n",
 614:     "\n",
 615:     "volume_data = (\n",
 616:     "    nations.CALCULATE(nation_name=name)\n",
 617:     "    .suppliers.supply_records.WHERE(part.part_type == \"ECONOMY ANODIZED STEEL\")\n",
 618:     "    .lines.CALCULATE(volume=extended_price * (1 - discount))\n",
 619:     "    .order.CALCULATE(\n",
 620:     "        o_year=YEAR(order_date),\n",
 621:     "        brazil_volume=IFF(nation_name == \"BRAZIL\", volume, 0),\n",
 622:     "    )\n",
 623:     "    .WHERE(\n",
 624:     "        (order_date >= datetime.date(1995, 1, 1))\n",
 625:     "        & (order_date <= datetime.date(1996, 12, 31))\n",
 626:     "        & (customer.nation.region.name == \"AMERICA\")\n",
 627:     "    )\n",
 628:     ")\n",
 629:     "\n",
 630:     "output = volume_data.PARTITION(name=\"years\", by=o_year).CALCULATE(\n",
 631:     "    O_YEAR=o_year,\n",
 632:     "    MKT_SHARE=SUM(order.brazil_volume) / SUM(order.volume),\n",
 633:     ")\n",
 634:     "\n",
 635:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 636:    ]
 637:   },

 641:    "metadata": {},
 642:    "source": [
 643:     "## Query 9\n",
 644:     "\n",
 645:     "This question asks about **the profit made for a particular line of parts looking at the supplying nation and particular year in question**. More specifically, it finds, for each nation and each year, the profit for all parts ordered in that year that contain a specified substring in their names and that were filled by a supplier in that nation. The profit is defined as the sum of the extended price times one minus the discount, minus the product of the supply cost and quantity, for all lineitems describing parts in the specified line. The query lists the nations in ascending alphabetical order and, for each nation, the year and profit in descending order by year (most recent first). The substring in question is `'green'`.\n",
 646:     "\n",
 647:     "\n",
 648:     "\n",
 649:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 650:     "\n",
 651:     "```SQL\n",
 652:     "SELECT\n",
 653:     "    NATION,\n",
 654:     "    O_YEAR,\n",
 655:     "    SUM(AMOUNT) AS SUM_PROFIT\n",
 656:     "FROM (\n",
 657:     "    SELECT\n",
 658:     "        N_NAME AS NATION,\n",
 659:     "        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM O_ORDERDATE) AS O_YEAR,\n",
 660:     "        L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT) - PS_SUPPLYCOST * L_QUANTITY AS AMOUNT\n",
 661:     "    FROM\n",
 662:     "        PART,\n",
 663:     "        SUPPLIER,\n",
 664:     "        LINEITEM,\n",
 665:     "        PARTSUPP,\n",
 666:     "        ORDERS,\n",
 667:     "        NATION\n",
 668:     "    WHERE\n",
 669:     "        S_SUPPKEY = L_SUPPKEY\n",
 670:     "        AND PS_SUPPKEY = L_SUPPKEY\n",
 671:     "        AND PS_PARTKEY = L_PARTKEY\n",
 672:     "        AND P_PARTKEY = L_PARTKEY\n",
 673:     "        AND O_ORDERKEY = L_ORDERKEY\n",
 674:     "        AND S_NATIONKEY = N_NATIONKEY\n",
 675:     "        AND P_NAME LIKE '%green%'\n",
 676:     ") PROFIT\n",
 677:     "GROUP BY\n",
 678:     "    NATION,\n",
 679:     "    O_YEAR\n",
 680:     "ORDER BY\n",
 681:     "    NATION,\n",
 682:     "    O_YEAR;\n",
 683:     "```"
 684:    ]
 685:   },
 686:   {
 687:    "cell_type": "code",
 688:    "execution_count": null,
 689:    "id": "3f2d470d-7bf4-4000-b049-9cac0c635ae2",

 691:    "outputs": [],
 692:    "source": [
 693:     "%%pydough\n",
 694:     "\n",
 695:     "selected_lines = (\n",
 696:     "    nations.CALCULATE(nation_name=name)\n",
 697:     "    .suppliers.supply_records.CALCULATE(supplycost)\n",
 698:     "    .WHERE(CONTAINS(part.name, \"green\"))\n",
 699:     "    .lines.CALCULATE(\n",
 700:     "        o_year=YEAR(order.order_date),\n",
 701:     "        value=extended_price * (1 - discount) - supplycost * quantity,\n",
 702:     "    )\n",
 703:     ")\n",
 704:     "output = (\n",
 705:     "    selected_lines.PARTITION(name=\"groups\", by=(nation_name, o_year))\n",
 706:     "    .CALCULATE(NATION=nation_name, O_YEAR=o_year, AMOUNT=SUM(lines.value))\n",
 707:     "    .TOP_K(10, by=(NATION.ASC(), O_YEAR.DESC()))\n",
 708:     ")\n",
 709:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 710:    ]
 711:   },
 712:   {
 713:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 714:    "id": "efe1a2f4-3198-4cd5-9807-3f054d0901e8",
 715:    "metadata": {},
 716:    "source": [
 717:     "## Query 10\n",
 718:     "\n",
 719:     "This question **determines the top 20 customers based on impact in revenue due to having returned parts within a particular quarter**. Revenue lost is defined as the sum of the extended price times one minus the discount for all qualifying lineitems. The chosen quarter is the last 3 months of 1993. The query lists the customer's name, address, nation, phone number, account balance, comment information and revenue lost.\n",
 720:     "\n",
 721:     "\n",
 722:     "\n",
 723:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 724:     "\n",
 725:     "```SQL\n",
 726:     "SELECT\n",
 727:     "    C_CUSTKEY,\n",
 728:     "    C_NAME,\n",
 729:     "    SUM(L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT)) AS REVENUE,\n",
 730:     "    C_ACCTBAL,\n",
 731:     "    N_NAME,\n",
 732:     "    C_ADDRESS,\n",
 733:     "    C_PHONE,\n",
 734:     "    C_COMMENT\n",
 735:     "FROM\n",
 736:     "    CUSTOMER,\n",
 737:     "    ORDERS,\n",
 738:     "    LINEITEM,\n",
 739:     "    NATION\n",
 740:     "WHERE\n",
 741:     "    C_CUSTKEY = O_CUSTKEY\n",
 742:     "    AND L_ORDERKEY = O_ORDERKEY\n",
 743:     "    AND O_ORDERDATE >= DATE '1993-10-01'\n",
 744:     "    AND O_ORDERDATE < DATE '1994-01-01'\n",
 745:     "    AND L_RETURNFLAG = 'R'\n",
 746:     "    AND C_NATIONKEY = N_NATIONKEY\n",
 747:     "GROUP BY\n",
 748:     "    C_CUSTKEY,\n",
 749:     "    C_NAME,\n",
 750:     "    C_ACCTBAL,\n",
 751:     "    C_PHONE,\n",
 752:     "    N_NAME,\n",
 753:     "    C_ADDRESS,\n",
 754:     "    C_COMMENT\n",
 755:     "ORDER BY\n",
 756:     "    REVENUE DESC\n",
 757:     "LIMIT 20;\n",
 758:     "```\n",
 759:     "\n",
 760:     "In the original query, a wide variety of columns need to be aggregated in the `GROUP BY` clause. PyDough greatly simplifies this if we phrase this question in the form of \"for each customer...\" since aggregating per-customer can be done implicitly without any manual partitioning."
 761:    ]
 762:   },
 763:   {
 764:    "cell_type": "code",

 766:    "id": "7d65be30-98fb-42af-aaff-8db79d8c981b",
 767:    "metadata": {},
 768:    "outputs": [],

 770:     "%%pydough\n",
 771:     "\n",

 774:     "    & (order_date < datetime.date(1994, 1, 1))\n",
 775:     ").lines.WHERE(return_flag == \"R\").CALCULATE(amt=extended_price * (1 - discount))\n",
 776:     "\n",
 777:     "output = customers.CALCULATE(\n",
 778:     "    C_CUSTKEY=key,\n",
 779:     "    C_NAME=name,\n",
 780:     "    REVENUE=SUM(selected_lines.amt),\n",
 781:     "    C_ACCTBAL=acctbal,\n",
 782:     "    N_NAME=nation.name,\n",
 783:     "    C_ADDRESS=address,\n",
 784:     "    C_PHONE=phone,\n",
 785:     "    C_COMMENT=comment,\n",
 786:     ").TOP_K(20, by=(REVENUE.DESC(), C_CUSTKEY.ASC()))\n",
 787:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 788:    ]
 789:   },
 790:   {
 791:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 792:    "id": "7e5efd87-7038-4725-b5ee-c3895668616d",
 793:    "metadata": {},
 794:    "source": [
 795:     "## Query 11\n",
 796:     "\n",
 797:     "The question seeks **to identify the most import subset of available part supplies from a particular nation**. It does so by finding, from scanning the available stock of suppliers in a given nation, all the parts that represent a significant percentage of the total value of all available parts. The query displays the part number and the value of those parts in descending order of value. A significant fraction is chosen to mean as at least 0.01%, and the chosen nation is Germany.\n",
 798:     "\n",
 799:     "\n",
 800:     "\n",
 801:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 802:     "\n",
 803:     "```SQL\n",
 804:     "SELECT\n",
 805:     "    PS_PARTKEY,\n",
 806:     "    SUM(PS_SUPPLYCOST * PS_AVAILQTY) AS VALUE\n",
 807:     "FROM\n",
 808:     "    PARTSUPP,\n",
 809:     "    SUPPLIER,\n",
 810:     "    NATION\n",
 811:     "WHERE\n",
 812:     "    PS_SUPPKEY = S_SUPPKEY\n",
 813:     "    AND S_NATIONKEY = N_NATIONKEY\n",
 814:     "    AND N_NAME = 'GERMANY'\n",
 815:     "GROUP BY\n",
 816:     "    PS_PARTKEY\n",
 817:     "HAVING\n",
 818:     "    SUM(PS_SUPPLYCOST * PS_AVAILQTY) > (\n",
 819:     "        SELECT\n",
 820:     "            SUM(PS_SUPPLYCOST * PS_AVAILQTY) * 0.0001\n",
 821:     "        FROM\n",
 822:     "            PARTSUPP,\n",
 823:     "            SUPPLIER,\n",
 824:     "            NATION\n",
 825:     "        WHERE\n",
 826:     "            PS_SUPPKEY = S_SUPPKEY\n",
 827:     "            AND S_NATIONKEY = N_NATIONKEY\n",
 828:     "            AND N_NAME = 'GERMANY'\n",
 829:     "    )\n",
 830:     "ORDER BY\n",
 831:     "    VALUE DESC;\n",
 832:     "```\n",
 833:     "\n",
 834:     "Notice that the SQL query requires a correlated subquery that leverages having to compute the corresponding SUM. PyDough uses a single filter to simplify this logic and ensure that through use of `BACK` the original results can be filtered."
 835:    ]
 836:   },
 837:   {
 838:    "cell_type": "code",
 839:    "execution_count": null,
 840:    "id": "ecbb5c84-4b48-4f5b-91f7-03a5e95ca0bd",
 841:    "metadata": {},
 842:    "outputs": [],
 843:    "source": [
 844:     "%%pydough\n",
 845:     "is_german_supplier = supplier.nation.name == \"GERMANY\"\n",
 846:     "selected_records = supply_records.WHERE(is_german_supplier).CALCULATE(metric=supplycost * availqty)\n",
 847:     "output = (\n",
 848:     "    TPCH\n",
 849:     "    .CALCULATE(min_market_share=SUM(selected_records.metric) * 0.0001)\n",
 850:     "    .supply_records\n",
 851:     "    .WHERE(is_german_supplier)\n",
 852:     "    .PARTITION(name=\"parts\", by=part_key)\n",
 853:     "    .CALCULATE(\n",
 854:     "        PS_PARTKEY=part_key,\n",
 855:     "        VALUE=SUM(supply_records.supplycost * supply_records.availqty)\n",
 856:     "    )\n",
 857:     "    .WHERE(VALUE > min_market_share)\n",
 858:     "    .ORDER_BY(VALUE.DESC())\n",
 859:     ")\n",
 860:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 861:    ]
 862:   },
 863:   {
 864:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 865:    "id": "158f76df-3abe-4721-924f-8e9597121b0f",
 866:    "metadata": {},
 867:    "source": [
 868:     "## Query 12\n",
 869:     "\n",
 870:     "This question seeks to determine **the impact of low cost shipping modes on delays for orders of varying priorities**. It does so by counting, by ship mode, for lineitems actually received by customers in a given year, the number of lineitems belonging to orders for which the receipt date exceeds the commit date for two different specified ship modes. Only lineitems that were actually shipped before the commit date are considered. The late lineitems are partitioned into two groups, those with priority `1-URGENT` or `2-HIGH`, and those with a priority other than `1-URGENT` or `2-HIGH`. The chosen year is 1994, and the two chosen ship modes are mail & ship.\n",
 871:     "\n",
 872:     "\n",
 873:     "\n",
 874:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 875:     "\n",
 876:     "```SQL\n",
 877:     "SELECT\n",
 878:     "    L_SHIPMODE,\n",
 879:     "    SUM(CASE\n",
 880:     "            WHEN O_ORDERPRIORITY = '1-URGENT'\n",
 881:     "              OR O_ORDERPRIORITY = '2-HIGH'\n",
 882:     "            THEN 1\n",
 883:     "            ELSE 0\n",
 884:     "        END) AS HIGH_LINE_COUNT,\n",
 885:     "    SUM(CASE\n",
 886:     "            WHEN O_ORDERPRIORITY <> '1-URGENT'\n",
 887:     "              AND O_ORDERPRIORITY <> '2-HIGH'\n",
 888:     "            THEN 1\n",
 889:     "            ELSE 0\n",
 890:     "        END) AS LOW_LINE_COUNT\n",
 891:     "FROM\n",
 892:     "    ORDERS,\n",
 893:     "    LINEITEM\n",
 894:     "WHERE\n",
 895:     "    O_ORDERKEY = L_ORDERKEY\n",
 896:     "    AND L_SHIPMODE IN ('MAIL', 'SHIP')\n",
 897:     "    AND L_COMMITDATE < L_RECEIPTDATE\n",
 898:     "    AND L_SHIPDATE < L_COMMITDATE\n",
 899:     "    AND L_RECEIPTDATE >= DATE '1994-01-01'\n",
 900:     "    AND L_RECEIPTDATE < DATE '1995-01-01'\n",
 901:     "GROUP BY\n",
 902:     "    L_SHIPMODE\n",
 903:     "ORDER BY\n",
 904:     "    L_SHIPMODE;\n",
 905:     "```"
 906:    ]
 907:   },
 908:   {
 909:    "cell_type": "code",
 910:    "execution_count": null,
 911:    "id": "7daa2e52-9afb-44dd-8d65-326011776532",
 912:    "metadata": {},
 913:    "outputs": [],
 914:    "source": [
 915:     "%%pydough\n",
 916:     "\n",
 917:     "selected_lines = lines.WHERE(\n",
 918:     "    ((ship_mode == \"MAIL\") | (ship_mode == \"SHIP\"))\n",
 919:     "    & (ship_date < commit_date)\n",
 920:     "    & (commit_date < receipt_date)\n",
 921:     "    & (receipt_date >= datetime.date(1994, 1, 1))\n",
 922:     "    & (receipt_date < datetime.date(1995, 1, 1))\n",
 923:     ").CALCULATE(\n",
 924:     "    is_high_priority=(order.order_priority == \"1-URGENT\")\n",
 925:     "    | (order.order_priority == \"2-HIGH\"),\n",
 926:     ")\n",
 927:     "output = selected_lines.PARTITION(\"modes\", by=ship_mode).CALCULATE(\n",
 928:     "    L_SHIPMODE=ship_mode,\n",
 929:     "    HIGH_LINE_COUNT=SUM(lines.is_high_priority),\n",
 930:     "    LOW_LINE_COUNT=SUM(~(lines.is_high_priority)),\n",
 931:     ").ORDER_BY(L_SHIPMODE.ASC())\n",
 932:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 933:    ]
 934:   },
 935:   {
 936:    "cell_type": "markdown",
 937:    "id": "f6f90a64-4a54-4790-bf80-d3b237f5b5a1",
 938:    "metadata": {},
 939:    "source": [
 940:     "## Query 13\n",
 941:     "\n",
 942:     "This question seeks to **understand the order count of each customer, including any customer who has not placed an order**. More specifically, it determines the distribution of customers by the number of orders they have made, including customers who have no record of orders, past or present. It counts and reports how many customers have no orders, how many have 1, 2, 3, etc. A check is made to ensure that the orders counted do not fall into one of several special categories of orders. Special categories are identified in the order comment column by looking for a particular pattern. The chosen pattern is comments that contain `'special'`, and later contain `'requests'`.\n",
 943:     "\n",
 944:     "\n",
 945:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
 946:     "\n",
 947:     "```SQL\n",
 948:     "SELECT\n",
 949:     "    C_COUNT,\n",
 950:     "    COUNT(*) AS CUSTDIST\n",
 951:     "FROM (\n",
 952:     "    SELECT\n",
 953:     "        C_CUSTKEY,\n",
 954:     "        COUNT(O_ORDERKEY) AS C_COUNT\n",
 955:     "    FROM\n",
 956:     "        CUSTOMER\n",
 957:     "        LEFT OUTER JOIN ORDERS ON C_CUSTKEY = O_CUSTKEY\n",
 958:     "        AND O_COMMENT NOT LIKE '%special%requests%'\n",
 959:     "    GROUP BY\n",
 960:     "        C_CUSTKEY\n",
 961:     ") C_ORDERS\n",
 962:     "GROUP BY\n",
 963:     "    C_COUNT\n",
 964:     "ORDER BY\n",
 965:     "    CUSTDIST DESC,\n",
 966:     "    C_COUNT DESC;\n",
 967:     "```"
 968:    ]
 969:   },
 970:   {
 971:    "cell_type": "code",
 972:    "execution_count": null,
 973:    "id": "522ee934-1e88-4c93-847b-d1757c372eeb",
 974:    "metadata": {},
 975:    "outputs": [],
 976:    "source": [
 977:     "%%pydough\n",
 978:     "\n",
 979:     "selected_orders = orders.WHERE(~(LIKE(comment, \"%special%requests%\")))\n",
 980:     "customer_info = customers.CALCULATE(\n",
 981:     "    key,\n",
 982:     "    num_non_special_orders=COUNT(selected_orders),\n",
 983:     ")\n",
 984:     "output = customer_info.PARTITION(name=\"num_order_groups\", by=num_non_special_orders).CALCULATE(\n",
 985:     "    C_COUNT=num_non_special_orders, CUSTDIST=COUNT(customers)\n",
 986:     ").ORDER_BY(CUSTDIST.DESC(), C_COUNT.DESC())\n",
 987:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
 988:    ]

 994:    "source": [
 995:     "## Query 14\n",
 996:     "\n",
 997:     "This question seeks seeks to determine **the impact of a promotion on revenue within a particular month**. More specifically, it determines what percentage of the revenue in a given year and month was derived from promotional parts. The query considers only parts actually shipped in that month and gives the percentage. Revenue is defined as extended price times one minus the discount. The chosen year and month are September of 1995.\n",
 998:     "\n",
 999:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1000:     "\n",
1001:     "```SQL\n",
1002:     "SELECT\n",
1003:     "    100.00 * SUM(CASE\n",
1004:     "                     WHEN P_TYPE LIKE 'PROMO%'\n",
1005:     "                     THEN L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT)\n",
1006:     "                     ELSE 0\n",
1007:     "                 END) / SUM(L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT)) AS PROMO_REVENUE\n",
1008:     "FROM\n",
1009:     "    LINEITEM,\n",
1010:     "    PART\n",
1011:     "WHERE\n",
1012:     "    L_PARTKEY = P_PARTKEY\n",
1013:     "    AND L_SHIPDATE >= DATE '1995-09-01'\n",
1014:     "    AND L_SHIPDATE < DATE '1995-10-01';\n",
1015:     "```"
1016:    ]
1017:   },
1018:   {
1019:    "cell_type": "code",
1020:    "execution_count": null,
1021:    "id": "8a843681-0893-4636-a312-75095c730de3",
1022:    "metadata": {},
1023:    "outputs": [],
1024:    "source": [
1025:     "%%pydough\n",
1026:     "\n",
1027:     "value = extended_price * (1 - discount)\n",
1028:     "selected_lines = lines.WHERE(\n",
1029:     "    (ship_date >= datetime.date(1995, 9, 1))\n",
1030:     "    & (ship_date < datetime.date(1995, 10, 1))\n",
1031:     ").CALCULATE(\n",
1032:     "    value=value,\n",
1033:     "    promo_value=IFF(STARTSWITH(part.part_type, \"PROMO\"), value, 0),\n",
1034:     ")\n",
1035:     "output = TPCH.CALCULATE(PROMO_REVENUE=100.0 * SUM(selected_lines.promo_value) / SUM(selected_lines.value))\n",
1036:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1037:    ]
1038:   },

1042:    "metadata": {},
1043:    "source": [
1044:     "## Query 15\n",
1045:     "\n",
1046:     "This question seeks to determine **the top supplier within a particular quarter**. It does so by finding the supplier who contributed the most to the overall revenue for parts shipped during a given quarter of a given year. In case of a tie, the query lists all suppliers whose contribution was equal to the maximum, presented in supplier number order. The chosen quarter is the first 3 months of 1996.\n",
1047:     "\n",
1048:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1049:     "\n",
1050:     "```SQL\n",
1051:     "with REVENUE (SUPPLIER_NO, TOTAL_REVENUE) AS\n",
1052:     "    SELECT\n",
1053:     "        L_SUPPKEY,\n",
1054:     "        SUM(L_EXTENDEDPRICE * (1 - L_DISCOUNT))\n",
1055:     "    FROM\n",
1056:     "        LINEITEM\n",
1057:     "    WHERE\n",
1058:     "        L_SHIPDATE >= DATE '1996-01-01'\n",
1059:     "        AND L_SHIPDATE < DATE '1996-04-01'\n",
1060:     "    GROUP BY\n",
1061:     "        L_SUPPKEY;\n",
1062:     "\n",
1063:     "SELECT\n",
1064:     "    S_SUPPKEY,\n",
1065:     "    S_NAME,\n",
1066:     "    S_ADDRESS,\n",
1067:     "    S_PHONE,\n",
1068:     "    TOTAL_REVENUE\n",
1069:     "FROM\n",
1070:     "    SUPPLIER,\n",
1071:     "    REVENUE\n",
1072:     "WHERE\n",
1073:     "    S_SUPPKEY = SUPPLIER_NO AND\n",
1074:     "    TOTAL_REVENUE = (\n",
1075:     "        SELECT\n",
1076:     "            MAX(TOTAL_REVENUE)\n",
1077:     "        FROM\n",
1078:     "            REVENUE0\n",
1079:     "    )\n",
1080:     "ORDER BY\n",
1081:     "    SUPPLIER_NO;\n",
1082:     "```\n",
1083:     "\n",
1084:     "With PyDough, the total revenue per-supplier can be expressed via contextless expressions which are first placed into context for the global aggregation to find the maximum revenue overall, then used again to be associated per-supplier."
1085:    ]
1086:   },
1087:   {
1088:    "cell_type": "code",
1089:    "execution_count": null,
1090:    "id": "a3f9b025-3ae7-4c7d-888c-a430cbe536b2",
1091:    "metadata": {},
1092:    "outputs": [],
1093:    "source": [
1094:     "%%pydough\n",
1095:     "\n",
1096:     "selected_lines = lines.WHERE(\n",

1098:     "    & (ship_date < datetime.date(1996, 4, 1))\n",
1099:     ")\n",
1100:     "total = SUM(selected_lines.extended_price * (1 - selected_lines.discount))\n",
1101:     "output = TPCH.CALCULATE(\n",
1102:     "    max_revenue=MAX(suppliers.WHERE(HAS(selected_lines)).CALCULATE(total_revenue=total).total_revenue)\n",
1103:     ").suppliers.WHERE(HAS(selected_lines)).CALCULATE(\n",
1104:     "    S_SUPPKEY=key,\n",
1105:     "    S_NAME=name,\n",
1106:     "    S_ADDRESS=address,\n",
1107:     "    S_PHONE=phone,\n",
1108:     "    TOTAL_REVENUE=total,\n",
1109:     ").WHERE(TOTAL_REVENUE == max_revenue).ORDER_BY(S_SUPPKEY.ASC())\n",
1110:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1111:    ]

1117:    "source": [
1118:     "## Query 16\n",
1119:     "\n",
1120:     "This question seeks to determine **how many suppliers can meet the needs of a part with a particular set of attributes**. It does so by counting the number of suppliers who can supply parts that satisfy a particular customer's requirements. The customer is interested in parts of eight different sizes as long as they are not of a given type, not of a given brand, and not from a supplier who has had complaints registered at the Better Business Bureau. Results must be presented in descending count and ascending brand, type, and size. The chosen brand, part type, and sizes are `'Brand#45'`, `'MEDIUM POLISHED'`, and `[49, 14, 23, 45, 19, 3, 36, 9]`, respectively.\n",
1121:     "\n",
1122:     "\n",
1123:     "\n",
1124:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1125:     "\n",
1126:     "```SQL\n",
1127:     "select\n",
1128:     "    p_brand,\n",
1129:     "    p_type,\n",
1130:     "    p_size,\n",
1131:     "    count(distinct ps_suppkey) as supplier_cnt\n",
1132:     "from\n",
1133:     "    partsupp,\n",
1134:     "    part\n",
1135:     "where\n",
1136:     "    p_partkey = ps_partkey\n",
1137:     "    and p_brand <> 'BRAND#45'\n",
1138:     "    and p_type not like 'MEDIUM POLISHED%'\n",
1139:     "    and p_size in (49, 14, 23, 45, 19, 3, 36, 9)\n",
1140:     "    and ps_suppkey not in (\n",
1141:     "        select\n",
1142:     "            s_suppkey\n",
1143:     "        from\n",
1144:     "            supplier\n",
1145:     "        where\n",
1146:     "            s_comment like '%Customer%Complaints%'\n",
1147:     "    )\n",
1148:     "group by\n",
1149:     "    p_brand,\n",
1150:     "    p_type,\n",
1151:     "    p_size\n",
1152:     "order by\n",
1153:     "    supplier_cnt desc,\n",
1154:     "    p_brand,\n",
1155:     "    p_type,\n",
1156:     "    p_size;\n",
1157:     "```"
1158:    ]
1159:   },
1160:   {
1161:    "cell_type": "code",
1162:    "execution_count": null,
1163:    "id": "1e22a800-e9ea-4b75-9921-c01553922c2e",
1164:    "metadata": {},
1165:    "outputs": [],
1166:    "source": [
1167:     "%%pydough\n",
1168:     "\n",
1169:     "selected_records = (\n",
1170:     "    parts.CALCULATE(\n",
1171:     "        p_brand=brand,\n",
1172:     "        p_type=part_type,\n",
1173:     "        p_size=size,\n",
1174:     "    ).WHERE(\n",
1175:     "        (brand != \"BRAND#45\")\n",
1176:     "        & ~STARTSWITH(part_type, \"MEDIUM POLISHED%\")\n",
1177:     "        & ISIN(size, [49, 14, 23, 45, 19, 3, 36, 9])\n",
1178:     "    )\n",
1179:     "    .supply_records\n",
1180:     "    .WHERE(~LIKE(supplier.comment, \"%Customer%Complaints%\"))\n",
1181:     ")\n",
1182:     "output = selected_records.PARTITION(\n",
1183:     "    name=\"groups\", by=(p_brand, p_type, p_size)\n",
1184:     ").CALCULATE(\n",
1185:     "    P_BRAND=p_brand,\n",
1186:     "    P_TYPE=p_type,\n",
1187:     "    P_SIZE=p_size,\n",
1188:     "    SUPPLIER_COUNT=NDISTINCT(supply_records.supplier_key),\n",
1189:     ").ORDER_BY(SUPPLIER_COUNT.DESC(), P_BRAND.ASC(), P_TYPE.ASC(), P_SIZE.ASC())\n",
1190:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1191:    ]
1192:   },

1194:    "cell_type": "markdown",
1195:    "id": "c5c44905-cb4b-44b6-a106-f643df1abd2a",
1196:    "metadata": {},
1197:    "source": [
1198:     "## Query 17\n",
1199:     "\n",
1200:     "This question seeks to determine **how much average yearly revenue would be lost if orders were no longer filled for small quantities of certain parts**. It does so by considering parts of a given brand and with a given container type and determines the average lineitem quantity of such parts ordered for all orders (past and pending) in the 7-year database. What would be the average yearly gross (undiscounted) loss in revenue if orders for these parts with a quantity of less than 20% of this average were no longer taken? The chosen brand and container type are `'Brand#23'` and `MED BOX`, respectively.\n",
1201:     "\n",
1202:     "\n",
1203:     "\n",
1204:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1205:     "\n",
1206:     "```SQL\n",
1207:     "select\n",
1208:     "    sum(l_extendedprice) / 7.0 as avg_yearly\n",
1209:     "from\n",
1210:     "    lineitem,\n",
1211:     "    part\n",
1212:     "where\n",
1213:     "    p_partkey = l_partkey\n",
1214:     "    and p_brand = 'Brand#23'\n",
1215:     "    and p_container = 'MED BOX'\n",
1216:     "    and l_quantity < (\n",
1217:     "        select\n",
1218:     "            0.2 * avg(l_quantity)\n",
1219:     "        from\n",
1220:     "            lineitem\n",
1221:     "        where\n",
1222:     "            l_partkey = p_partkey\n",
1223:     "    )\n",
1224:     "```\n",
1225:     "\n",
1226:     "PyDough bypasses the need for the correlated subquery by first aggregating lineitems by part, then stepping into the lineitems and backreferencing to compare against the per-part average value."
1227:    ]
1228:   },
1229:   {
1230:    "cell_type": "code",
1231:    "execution_count": null,
1232:    "id": "4824db18-364b-4ba3-98a2-70ee8930c074",
1233:    "metadata": {},
1234:    "outputs": [],
1235:    "source": [
1236:     "%%pydough\n",
1237:     "\n",
1238:     "selected_lines = parts.WHERE(\n",
1239:     "    (brand == \"Brand#23\") & (container == \"MED BOX\")\n",
1240:     ").CALCULATE(\n",
1241:     "    avg_quantity=AVG(lines.quantity)\n",
1242:     ").lines.WHERE(quantity < 0.2 * avg_quantity)\n",
1243:     "output = TPCH.CALCULATE(AVG_YEARLY=SUM(selected_lines.extended_price) / 7.0)\n",
1244:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1245:    ]
1246:   },

1252:     "## Query 18\n",
1253:     "\n",
1254:     "This question seeks to **ranks customers based on their status as having placed a large quantity order**. It does so by calculating a list of the top 100 customers who have ever placed large quantity orders. It lists the customer name, customer key, the order key, date and total price and the quantity for the order.\n",
1255:     "\n",
1256:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1257:     "\n",
1258:     "```SQL\n",
1259:     "select\n",
1260:     "    c_name,\n",
1261:     "    c_custkey,\n",
1262:     "    o_orderkey,\n",
1263:     "    o_orderdate,\n",
1264:     "    o_totalprice,\n",
1265:     "    sum(l_quantity)\n",
1266:     "from\n",
1267:     "    customer,\n",
1268:     "    orders,\n",
1269:     "    lineitem\n",
1270:     "where\n",
1271:     "    o_orderkey in (\n",
1272:     "        select\n",
1273:     "            l_orderkey\n",
1274:     "        from\n",
1275:     "            lineitem\n",
1276:     "        group by\n",
1277:     "            l_orderkey \n",
1278:     "        having\n",
1279:     "            sum(l_quantity) > 300\n",
1280:     "        )\n",
1281:     "    and c_custkey = o_custkey\n",
1282:     "    and o_orderkey = l_orderkey\n",
1283:     "group by\n",
1284:     "    c_name,\n",
1285:     "    c_custkey,\n",
1286:     "    o_orderkey,\n",
1287:     "    o_orderdate,\n",
1288:     "    o_totalprice\n",
1289:     "order by\n",
1290:     "    o_totalprice desc,\n",
1291:     "    o_orderdate;\n",
1292:     "```\n",
1293:     "\n",
1294:     "Notice that PyDough can simplify this by phrasing this as an operation being done per-order, thus eliding the need to do any manual aggregation."
1295:    ]
1296:   },

1323:    "source": [
1324:     "## Query 19\n",
1325:     "\n",
1326:     "This question seeks to **report the gross discounted revenue resulting from select parts with a set of handling details**. More specifically, it finds the gross discounted revenue for all orders for three different types of parts that were shipped by air and delivered in person. Parts are selected based on the combination of specific brands, a list of containers, and a range of sizes. The allowed combinations are:\n",
1327:     "\n",
1328:     "- The brand is `'BRAND#12'`, the quantity is between 1 and 11, the size is between 1 and 5, and the container type is one of `['SM CASE', 'SM BOX', 'SM PACK', 'SM PKG']`.\n",
1329:     "- The brand is `'BRAND#23'`, the quantity is between 10 and 20, the size is between 1 and 10, and the container type is one of `['MED BAG', 'MED BOX', 'MED PKG', 'MED PACK']`.\n",
1330:     "- The brand is `'BRAND#34'`, the quantity is between 20 and 30, the size is between 1 and 15, and the container type is one of `['LG CASE', 'LG BOX', 'LG PACK', 'LG PKG']`.\n",
1331:     "\n",
1332:     "\n",
1333:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1334:     "\n",
1335:     "```SQL\n",
1336:     "select\n",
1337:     "    sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) ) as revenue\n",
1338:     "from\n",
1339:     "    lineitem,\n",
1340:     "    part\n",
1341:     "where\n",
1342:     "    (\n",
1343:     "        p_partkey = l_partkey\n",
1344:     "        and p_brand = 'Brand#12'\n",
1345:     "        and p_container in ( 'SM CASE', 'SM BOX', 'SM PACK', 'SM PKG')\n",
1346:     "        and l_quantity >= 1 and l_quantity <= 1 + 10\n",
1347:     "        and p_size between 1 and 5\n",
1348:     "        and l_shipmode in ('AIR', 'AIR REG')\n",
1349:     "        and l_shipinstruct = 'DELIVER IN PERSON'\n",
1350:     "    )\n",
1351:     "    or\n",
1352:     "    (\n",
1353:     "        p_partkey = l_partkey\n",
1354:     "        and p_brand = 'Brand#23'\n",
1355:     "        and p_container in ('MED BAG', 'MED BOX', 'MED PKG', 'MED PACK')\n",
1356:     "        and l_quantity >= 10 and l_quantity <= 10 + 10\n",
1357:     "        and p_size between 1 and 10\n",
1358:     "        and l_shipmode in ('AIR', 'AIR REG')\n",
1359:     "        and l_shipinstruct = 'DELIVER IN PERSON'\n",
1360:     "    )\n",
1361:     "    or\n",
1362:     "    (\n",
1363:     "        p_partkey = l_partkey\n",
1364:     "        and p_brand = 'Brand#34'\n",
1365:     "        and p_container in ('LG CASE', 'LG BOX', 'LG PACK', 'LG PKG')\n",
1366:     "        and l_quantity >= 20 and l_quantity <= 20 + 10\n",
1367:     "        and p_size between 1 and 15\n",
1368:     "        and l_shipmode in ('AIR', 'AIR REG')\n",
1369:     "        and l_shipinstruct = 'DELIVER IN PERSON'\n",
1370:     "    )\n",
1371:     "```"
1372:    ]
1373:   },
1374:   {
1375:    "cell_type": "code",
1376:    "execution_count": null,
1377:    "id": "aeaaa90e-000e-4a12-91e9-4100d308d312",
1378:    "metadata": {},
1379:    "outputs": [],
1380:    "source": [
1381:     "%%pydough\n",
1382:     "\n",
1383:     "selected_lines = lines.WHERE(\n",
1384:     "    (ISIN(ship_mode, (\"AIR\", \"AIR REG\")))\n",
1385:     "    & (ship_instruct == \"DELIVER IN PERSON\")\n",
1386:     "    & (part.size >= 1)\n",
1387:     "    & (\n",
1388:     "        (\n",
1389:     "            (part.size <= 5)\n",
1390:     "            & (quantity >= 1)\n",
1391:     "            & (quantity <= 11)\n",
1392:     "            & ISIN(\n",
1393:     "                part.container,\n",
1394:     "                (\"SM CASE\", \"SM BOX\", \"SM PACK\", \"SM PKG\"),\n",
1395:     "            )\n",
1396:     "            & (part.brand == \"Brand#12\")\n",
1397:     "        )\n",
1398:     "        | (\n",
1399:     "            (part.size <= 10)\n",
1400:     "            & (quantity >= 10)\n",

1403:     "                part.container,\n",
1404:     "                (\"MED BAG\", \"MED BOX\", \"MED PACK\", \"MED PKG\"),\n",
1405:     "            )\n",
1406:     "            & (part.brand == \"Brand#23\")\n",
1407:     "        )\n",
1408:     "        | (\n",
1409:     "            (part.size <= 15)\n",
1410:     "            & (quantity >= 20)\n",
1411:     "            & (quantity <= 30)\n",
1412:     "            & ISIN(\n",
1413:     "                part.container,\n",
1414:     "                (\"LG CASE\", \"LG BOX\", \"LG PACK\", \"LG PKG\"),\n",
1415:     "            )\n",
1416:     "            & (part.brand == \"Brand#34\")\n",
1417:     "        )\n",
1418:     "    )\n",
1419:     ")\n",
1420:     "output = TPCH.CALCULATE(\n",
1421:     "    REVENUE=SUM(selected_lines.extended_price * (1 - selected_lines.discount))\n",
1422:     ")\n",
1423:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1424:    ]
1425:   },
1426:   {
1427:    "cell_type": "markdown",
1428:    "id": "860e2d30-5fb9-48ad-ba6d-b2cc7145f97f",
1429:    "metadata": {},
1430:    "source": [
1431:     "## Query 20\n",
1432:     "\n",
1433:     "This question seeks to **determine supppliers in a particular nation that may be candidate for discounts over a year in question**. More specifically, it identifies suppliers who have an excess of a given part available; an excess is defined to be more than 50% of the parts like the given part that the supplier shipped in a given year for a given nation. Only parts whose names share a certain naming convention are considered. The chosen year and nation are 1994 and Canada, respectively. The chosen naming convention is parts whose names start with `'forest'`.\n",
1434:     "\n",
1435:     "\n",
1436:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1437:     "\n",
1438:     "```SQL\n",
1439:     "select\n",
1440:     "    s_name,\n",
1441:     "    s_address\n",
1442:     "from\n",
1443:     "    supplier, nation\n",
1444:     "where\n",
1445:     "    s_suppkey in (\n",
1446:     "        select\n",
1447:     "            ps_suppkey\n",
1448:     "        from\n",
1449:     "            partsupp\n",
1450:     "        where\n",
1451:     "            ps_partkey in (\n",
1452:     "                select\n",
1453:     "                    p_partkey\n",
1454:     "                from\n",
1455:     "                    part\n",
1456:     "                where\n",
1457:     "                    p_name like 'forest%'\n",
1458:     "            )\n",
1459:     "            and ps_availqty > (\n",
1460:     "                select\n",
1461:     "                    0.5 * sum(l_quantity)\n",
1462:     "                from\n",
1463:     "                    lineitem\n",
1464:     "                where\n",
1465:     "                    l_partkey = ps_partkey\n",
1466:     "                    and l_suppkey = ps_suppkey\n",
1467:     "                    and l_shipdate >= date('1994-01-01')\n",
1468:     "                    and l_shipdate < date('1994-01-01') + interval '1' year\n",
1469:     "            )\n",
1470:     "    )\n",
1471:     "    and s_nationkey = n_nationkey\n",
1472:     "    and n_name = 'CANADA'\n",
1473:     "order by\n",
1474:     "    s_name\n",
1475:     "```\n",
1476:     "\n",
1477:     "Notice that the SQL version requires repeated use of subqueries, but PyDough can combine the `part_qty` and `selected_part_supplied` sections into a single extended expression that cleanly represents the filter requirement."
1478:    ]
1479:   },
1480:   {
1481:    "cell_type": "code",
1482:    "execution_count": null,
1483:    "id": "640f1835-b274-433a-8cbe-150440087856",
1484:    "metadata": {},
1485:    "outputs": [],
1486:    "source": [
1487:     "%%pydough\n",
1488:     "\n",
1489:     "part_qty = SUM(\n",
1490:     "    lines.WHERE(\n",
1491:     "        (ship_date >= datetime.date(1994, 1, 1))\n",
1492:     "        & (ship_date < datetime.date(1995, 1, 1))\n",
1493:     "    ).quantity\n",
1494:     ")\n",
1495:     "selected_part_supplied = supply_records.CALCULATE(\n",
1496:     "        availqty\n",
1497:     ").part.WHERE(\n",
1498:     "    STARTSWITH(name, \"forest\") & (availqty > part_qty * 0.5)\n",
1499:     ")\n",
1500:     "output = suppliers.CALCULATE(\n",
1501:     "    S_NAME=name,\n",
1502:     "    S_ADDRESS=address,\n",
1503:     ").WHERE((nation.name == \"CANADA\") & COUNT(selected_part_supplied) > 0).ORDER_BY(S_NAME.ASC())\n",
1504:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1505:    ]
1506:   },
1507:   {
1508:    "cell_type": "markdown",
1509:    "id": "82c059e6",
1510:    "metadata": {},
1511:    "source": [
1512:     "## Query 21\n",
1513:     "\n",
1514:     "This query **identifies certain suppliers who were not able to ship required parts in a timely manner**. It does so by counting, for each Saudi Arabian supplier, how many times their product was part of a multi-supplier order (with current status of 'F') where they were the only supplier who failed to meet the committed delivery date.\n",
1515:     "\n",
1516:     "\n",
1517:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1518:     "\n",
1519:     "```SQL\n",
1520:     "select\n",
1521:     "    S_NAME,\n",
1522:     "    count(*) as NUMWAIT\n",
1523:     "from\n",
1524:     "    supplier,\n",
1525:     "    lineitem l1,\n",
1526:     "    orders,\n",
1527:     "    nation\n",
1528:     "where\n",
1529:     "    s_suppkey = l1.l_suppkey\n",
1530:     "    and o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey\n",
1531:     "    and o_orderstatus = 'F'\n",
1532:     "    and l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate\n",
1533:     "    and exists (\n",
1534:     "        select\n",
1535:     "            *\n",
1536:     "        from\n",
1537:     "            lineitem l2\n",
1538:     "        where\n",
1539:     "            l2.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey\n",
1540:     "            and l2.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey\n",
1541:     "    )\n",
1542:     "    and not exists (\n",
1543:     "        select\n",
1544:     "            *\n",
1545:     "        from\n",
1546:     "            lineitem l3\n",
1547:     "        where\n",
1548:     "            l3.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey\n",
1549:     "            and l3.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey\n",
1550:     "            and l3.l_receiptdate > l3.l_commitdate\n",
1551:     "    )\n",
1552:     "    and s_nationkey = n_nationkey\n",
1553:     "    and n_name = 'SAUDI ARABIA'\n",
1554:     "group by\n",
1555:     "    s_name\n",
1556:     "order by\n",
1557:     "    numwait desc,\n",
1558:     "    s_name\n",
1559:     "```"
1560:    ]
1561:   },
1562:   {
1563:    "cell_type": "code",
1564:    "execution_count": null,
1565:    "id": "8e400982",
1566:    "metadata": {},
1567:    "outputs": [],
1568:    "source": [
1569:     "%%pydough\n",
1570:     "\n",
1571:     "date_check = receipt_date > commit_date\n",
1572:     "selected_orders = lines.CALCULATE(original_key=supplier_key).WHERE(date_check).order\n",
1573:     "different_supplier = supplier_key != original_key\n",
1574:     "waiting_entries = selected_orders.WHERE(\n",
1575:     "    (order_status == \"F\")\n",
1576:     "    & HAS(lines.WHERE(different_supplier))\n",
1577:     "    & HASNOT(lines.WHERE(different_supplier & date_check))\n",
1578:     ")\n",
1579:     "output = (\n",
1580:     "    suppliers.WHERE(nation.name == \"SAUDI ARABIA\")\n",
1581:     "    .CALCULATE(\n",
1582:     "        S_NAME=name,\n",
1583:     "        NUMWAIT=COUNT(waiting_entries),\n",
1584:     "    )\n",
1585:     "    .ORDER_BY(NUMWAIT.DESC(), S_NAME.ASC())\n",
1586:     ")\n",
1587:     "\n",
1588:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1589:    ]
1590:   },
1591:   {
1592:    "cell_type": "markdown",
1593:    "id": "be8bbff8",
1594:    "metadata": {},
1595:    "source": [
1596:     "## Query 22\n",
1597:     "\n",
1598:     "This query **identifies geographies where there are customers who may be likely to make a purchase**. It does so by breaking down how many customers, by country code of their phone number (only including customers from certain country codes), have not placed an order but have an account balance that is above the average for all positive account balances of such customers. Also includes the total balance for all such customers for each country code. The country codes to include are 13, 31, 23, 29, 30, 18 and 17.\n",
1599:     "\n",
1600:     "\n",
1601:     "Here is the corresponding SQL:\n",
1602:     "\n",
1603:     "```SQL\n",
1604:     "select\n",
1605:     "    CNTRYCODE,\n",
1606:     "    count(*) as NUMCUST,\n",
1607:     "    sum(c_acctbal) as TOTALACCTBAL\n",
1608:     "from (\n",
1609:     "    select\n",
1610:     "        substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) as cntrycode,\n",
1611:     "        c_acctbal\n",
1612:     "    from\n",
1613:     "        customer\n",
1614:     "    where\n",
1615:     "        substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) in\n",
1616:     "            ('13', '31', '23', '29', '30', '18', '17')\n",
1617:     "    and c_acctbal > (\n",
1618:     "        select\n",
1619:     "            avg(c_acctbal)\n",
1620:     "        from\n",
1621:     "            customer\n",
1622:     "        where\n",
1623:     "            c_acctbal > 0.00\n",
1624:     "            and substring (c_phone from 1 for 2) in\n",
1625:     "                ('13', '31', '23', '29', '30', '18', '17')\n",
1626:     "    )\n",
1627:     "    and not exists (\n",
1628:     "        select\n",
1629:     "            *\n",
1630:     "        from\n",
1631:     "            orders\n",
1632:     "        where\n",
1633:     "            o_custkey = c_custkey\n",
1634:     "    )\n",
1635:     "    ) as custsale\n",
1636:     "group by\n",
1637:     "    cntrycode\n",
1638:     "order by\n",
1639:     "    cntrycode\n",
1640:     "```"
1641:    ]
1642:   },
1643:   {
1644:    "cell_type": "code",
1645:    "execution_count": null,
1646:    "id": "ed31951a-e76d-40f3-ad70-c911ba80c205",
1647:    "metadata": {},
1648:    "outputs": [],
1649:    "source": [
1650:     "%%pydough\n",
1651:     "\n",
1652:     "is_selected_code = ISIN(cntry_code, (\"13\", \"31\", \"23\", \"29\", \"30\", \"18\", \"17\"))\n",
1653:     "selected_customers = customers.CALCULATE(cntry_code=phone[:2]).WHERE(is_selected_code)\n",
1654:     "output = (\n",
1655:     "    TPCH\n",
1656:     "    .CALCULATE(global_avg_balance=AVG(selected_customers.WHERE(acctbal > 0.0).acctbal))\n",
1657:     "    .customers\n",
1658:     "    .CALCULATE(cntry_code=phone[:2])\n",
1659:     "    .WHERE(is_selected_code & (acctbal > global_avg_balance) & (COUNT(orders) == 0))\n",
1660:     "    .PARTITION(\n",
1661:     "        name=\"countries\",\n",
1662:     "        by=cntry_code,\n",
1663:     "    )\n",
1664:     "    .CALCULATE(\n",
1665:     "        CNTRY_CODE=cntry_code,\n",
1666:     "        NUM_CUSTS=COUNT(customers),\n",
1667:     "        TOTACCTBAL=SUM(customers.acctbal),\n",
1668:     "    )\n",
1669:     ")\n",
1670:     "pydough.to_df(output)"
1671:    ]
1672:   },
