## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/core/dataProcessor.js
````javascript
  1: // Data Processor - Processes metadata into nodes and links
  2: /**
  3:  * Process metadata from a database schema/model into a graph representation
  4:  * with nodes (tables/collections) and links (relationships).
  5:  *
  6:  * This is the main entry point for converting database metadata into a
  7:  * visualization-ready format.
  8:  *
  9:  * @param {Object} data - The metadata from the JSON file containing database schema information
 10:  * @returns {Object} An object containing nodes, links arrays and the graph name:
 11:  *   - nodes: Array of collection nodes with their properties and visual attributes
 12:  *   - links: Array of relationships between collections
 13:  *   - graphName: The name of the processed graph
 14:  */
 15: export function processMetadata(data) {
 16:   const nodes = [];
 17:   const links = [];
 18: 
 19:   // Extract the first graph from the metadata
 20:   const graphName = Object.keys(data)[0];
 21:   if (!graphName) {
 22:     console.warn("No graph data found");
 23:     return { nodes, links, graphName: null };
 24:   }
 25: 
 26:   const collections = data[graphName] || {};
 27:   console.log("Collections found:", Object.keys(collections).length);
 28: 
 29:   // First pass: Process all collections to create nodes
 30:   processCollections(collections, nodes);
 31: 
 32:   // Second pass: Handle reverse relationships
 33:   processReverseRelationships(nodes);
 34: 
 35:   // Third pass: Create links based on all subcollection relationships
 36:   createLinks(nodes, links);
 37:   // Debugging breakpoint to inspect the final graph data
 38:   return { nodes, links, graphName };
 39: }
 40: 
 41: /**
 42:  * Process database collections into graph nodes with visual properties.
 43:  *
 44:  * Iterates through each collection in the metadata, extracts its properties (columns)
 45:  * and relationships (subcollections), and creates a node object with positioning
 46:  * information for graph visualization.
 47:  *
 48:  * @param {Object} collections - The collections from the metadata, where keys are collection names
 49:  * @param {Array} nodes - The array to store created node objects (modified in-place)
 50:  */
 51: function processCollections(collections, nodes) {
 52:   Object.entries(collections).forEach(
 53:     ([collectionName, collectionData], index) => {
 54:       console.log(`Processing collection: ${collectionName}`);
 55:       // Extract table columns and subcollections for display
 56:       const columns = [];
 57:       const subcollections = [];
 58: 
 59:       if (collectionData.properties) {
 60:         processProperties(
 61:           collectionName,
 62:           collectionData,
 63:           columns,
 64:           subcollections
 65:         );
 66:       }
 67: 
 68:       // Calculate height based on properties with more padding
 69:       // Height is dynamic based on number of properties to ensure all are visible
 70:       const height = Math.max(
 71:         250,
 72:         150 + (columns.length + subcollections.length) * 22
 73:       );
 74: 
 75:       // Create the node object with visual coordinates and data properties
 76:       nodes.push({
 77:         id: collectionName,
 78:         name: collectionName,
 79:         columns: columns,
 80:         subcollections: subcollections,
 81:         tablePath: collectionData.table_path || "No path specified",
 82:         uniqueProperties: collectionData.unique_properties || ["id"],
 83:         // Position nodes in a grid pattern for initial visualization
 84:         x: 150 + (index % 3) * 500,
 85:         y: 150 + Math.floor(index / 3) * 400,
 86:         width: 350,
 87:         height: height,
 88:         // These properties are used for hierarchical tree visualization layouts
 89:         treePosition: null,
 90:         treeLevel: null,
 91:         treeParent: null,
 92:       });
 93:     }
 94:   );
 95: 
 96:   console.log(`Created ${nodes.length} nodes`);
 97: }
 98: 
 99: /**
100:  * Extract and categorize properties from a collection into table columns and relationships.
101:  *
102:  * Processes each property in a collection, categorizing them as either:
103:  * - Regular table columns (table_column type)
104:  * - Relationships to other collections (simple_join, compound, or cartesian_product types)
105:  *
106:  * @param {string} collectionName - The name of the collection being processed
107:  * @param {Object} collectionData - The collection data containing properties and metadata
108:  * @param {Array} columns - Output array to store column information (modified in-place)
109:  * @param {Array} subcollections - Output array to store relationship information (modified in-place)
110:  */
111: function processProperties(
112:   collectionName,
113:   collectionData,
114:   columns,
115:   subcollections
116: ) {
117:   Object.entries(collectionData.properties).forEach(([propName, propData]) => {
118:     // Handle regular table columns (attributes)
119:     if (propData.type === "table_column") {
120:       columns.push({
121:         name: propName,
122:         columnName: propData.column_name,
123:         dataType: propData.data_type,
124:       });
125:     }
126:     // Handle relationship properties between collections
127:     else if (
128:       ["simple_join", "cartesian_product", "general_join"].includes(
129:         propData.type
130:       )
131:     ) {
132:       processRelationship(
133:         collectionName,
134:         propName,
135:         propData,
136:         collectionData,
137:         subcollections
138:       );
139:     }
140:   });
141: }
142: 
143: /**
144:  * Process a relationship property between collections and add it to subcollections.
145:  *
146:  * Handles different relationship types (simple_join, compound, cartesian_product)
147:  * and determines the target collection for each relationship. Creates a structured
148:  * representation of the relationship with all its attributes.
149:  *
150:  * @param {string} collectionName - The name of the source collection
151:  * @param {string} propName - The name of the relationship property
152:  * @param {Object} propData - The relationship property data with type and connection details
153:  * @param {Object} collectionData - The parent collection data containing all properties
154:  * @param {Array} subcollections - Array to store the processed relationship (modified in-place)
155:  */
156: function processRelationship(
157:   collectionName,
158:   propName,
159:   propData,
160:   collectionData,
161:   subcollections
162: ) {
163:   let targetCollection;
164:   let condition = null; // Variable to store the condition for general_join
165: 
166:   try {
167:     // Handle different relationship types to determine the target collection
168:     if (propData.type === "simple_join") {
169:       // For simple joins, the target is directly specified
170:       targetCollection = propData.other_collection_name;
171:     } else if (propData.type === "general_join") {
172:       // For general joins, target is specified, and there's a condition
173:       targetCollection = propData.other_collection_name;
174:       condition = propData.condition; // Extract the condition string
175:     } else {
176:       // For cartesian product relationships
177:       targetCollection = propData.other_collection_name;
178:     }
179:   } catch (e) {
180:     console.error(`Error processing relationship ${propName}:`, e);
181:     targetCollection = "unknown";
182:   }
183: 
184:   // Only add subcollection if we have a valid target
185:   if (targetCollection && targetCollection !== "unknown") {
186:     console.log(
187:       `Adding subcollection: ${propName} (${propData.type}) -> ${targetCollection}`
188:     );
189: 
190:     // Create the relationship object with all needed properties for visualization
191:     subcollections.push({
192:       name: propName,
193:       type: propData.type,
194:       target: targetCollection,
195:       singular: propData.singular || false, // One-to-one relationship flag
196:       noCollisions: propData.no_collisions || false, // Indicates if duplicate relations are prevented
197:       primary: propData.primary_property, // Primary join property
198:       condition: condition, // Add the condition field (will be null for non-general joins)
199:       propertyData: propData, // Store the original property data for reference
200:       isForward: true, // Flag this as a forward relationship (vs reverse relationships created later)
201:     });
202:   }
203: }
204: 
205: /**
206:  * Create bidirectional relationships by adding reverse relationships to target nodes.
207:  *
208:  * For each forward relationship from collection A to B, this function creates
209:  * a corresponding reverse relationship from B to A, ensuring proper navigation
210:  * in both directions. Handles relationship cardinality appropriately.
211:  *
212:  * @param {Array} nodes - The array of all node objects with their subcollections
213:  */
214: function processReverseRelationships(nodes) {
215:   nodes.forEach((sourceNode) => {
216:     sourceNode.subcollections.forEach((subcollection) => {
217:       const targetNode = nodes.find((n) => n.id === subcollection.target);
218:       if (targetNode && subcollection.propertyData?.reverse_relationship_name) {
219:         console.log(
220:           `Adding reverse relationship from ${targetNode.id} to ${sourceNode.id}`
221:         );
222: 
223:         // Transform the condition for the reverse relationship if it exists
224:         let reverseCondition = subcollection.condition;
225:         if (reverseCondition) {
226:           // Use placeholders to safely swap 'self.' and 'other.'
227:           const tempSelf = "__TEMP_SELF__";
228:           reverseCondition = reverseCondition.replace(/self\./g, tempSelf);
229:           reverseCondition = reverseCondition.replace(/other\./g, "self.");
230:           reverseCondition = reverseCondition.replace(
231:             new RegExp(tempSelf, "g"),
232:             "other."
233:           );
234:         }
235: 
236:         targetNode.subcollections.push({
237:           name: subcollection.propertyData.reverse_relationship_name,
238:           type: subcollection.type, // Keep the same type
239:           target: sourceNode.id,
240:           singular: !subcollection.singular, // Reverse cardinality (approximate)
241:           noCollisions: subcollection.noCollisions, // Maintain collision property
242:           primary: subcollection.primary, // Reverse relationships might not have a clear primary property
243:           condition: reverseCondition, // Use the transformed condition
244:           propertyData: { original_relationship: subcollection.name }, // Reference original
245:           isForward: false, // This is a reverse relationship
246:         });
247:       }
248:     });
249:   });
250: }
251: 
252: /**
253:  * Create graph links based on the relationships between collections.
254:  *
255:  * Transforms the subcollection relationships stored in each node into visible
256:  * links for the graph visualization. Each link contains detailed information
257:  * about the relationship type, cardinality, and direction.
258:  *
259:  * @param {Array} nodes - The array of all node objects
260:  * @param {Array} links - The array to store the created link objects (modified in-place)
261:  */
262: function createLinks(nodes, links) {
263:   nodes.forEach((sourceNode) => {
264:     sourceNode.subcollections.forEach((subcollection) => {
265:       const targetNode = nodes.find((n) => n.id === subcollection.target);
266:       if (targetNode) {
267:         console.log(
268:           `Creating link: ${sourceNode.id} -> ${targetNode.id} (${subcollection.type})`
269:         );
270:         links.push({
271:           source: sourceNode.id,
272:           target: targetNode.id,
273:           type: subcollection.type,
274:           singular: subcollection.singular,
275:           name: subcollection.name, // Add the relationship name to the link
276:           condition: subcollection.condition, // Add the condition to the link data
277:         });
278:       }
279:     });
280:   });
281: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/core/graphCreator.js
````javascript
  1: // Graph Creator - Orchestrates the creation of the graph visualization
  2: // This module is the central coordinator that brings together all visualization components
  3: 
  4: import { processMetadata } from "./dataProcessor.js";
  5: import { setupMarkers } from "../renderers/markerRenderer.js";
  6: import { createNodes } from "../renderers/nodeRenderer.js";
  7: import { createLinks } from "../renderers/linkRenderer.js";
  8: import { setupZoom, createZoomControls } from "../interactions/zoomHandler.js";
  9: import { setupDrag } from "../interactions/dragHandler.js";
 10: import { setupHighlighting } from "../interactions/highlightHandler.js";
 11: import {
 12:   createTooltip,
 13:   showNodeTooltip,
 14:   hideTooltip,
 15:   isMouseOverTooltip,
 16:   clearHoverElement,
 17:   forceHideTooltips,
 18:   scheduleHide,
 19:   cancelHide,
 20:   isMouseInBottomRightQuadrant,
 21: } from "../interactions/tooltipHandler.js";
 22: import { setupForceSimulation } from "../layouts/forceLayout.js";
 23: import { applyGraphStyles } from "../styles/graphStyles.js";
 24: import { calculateLinkPath } from "../utils/geometryUtils.js";
 25: 
 26: /**
 27:  * Create the graph visualization from metadata
 28:  *
 29:  * This is the main orchestration function that:
 30:  * 1. Processes the raw metadata into nodes and links
 31:  * 2. Sets up the SVG container and visualization groups
 32:  * 3. Initializes interactive components (zoom, drag, tooltips)
 33:  * 4. Creates visual elements (nodes, links, markers)
 34:  * 5. Sets up the force simulation for automatic layout
 35:  * 6. Configures event handlers for interactivity
 36:  *
 37:  * @param {Object} data - The metadata from the JSON file containing database schema
 38:  */
 39: export function createGraph(data) {
 40:   console.log("Creating graph visualization...");
 41: 
 42:   // Process the metadata into D3-compatible node and link structures
 43:   const { nodes, links, graphName } = processMetadata(data);
 44: 
 45:   // Debug logging
 46:   console.log("Processed metadata:");
 47:   console.log("Number of nodes:", nodes.length);
 48:   console.log("Number of links:", links.length);
 49:   console.log("Links:", links);
 50: 
 51:   // Get the dimensions of the container for proper sizing
 52:   const container = document.getElementById("graph");
 53:   if (!container) {
 54:     console.error("Graph container not found!");
 55:     return;
 56:   }
 57: 
 58:   // Clear any existing visualization
 59:   container.innerHTML = "";
 60: 
 61:   const width = container.clientWidth || 1000;
 62:   const height = container.clientHeight || 800;
 63:   console.log("Container dimensions:", width, height);
 64: 
 65:   // Create the main SVG container that will hold all visualization elements
 66:   const svg = d3
 67:     .select("#graph")
 68:     .append("svg")
 69:     .attr("width", width)
 70:     .attr("height", height);
 71: 
 72:   // Validate the graph data before proceeding
 73:   if (!graphName) {
 74:     handleNoData(svg, width, height, "No metadata found");
 75:     return;
 76:   }
 77: 
 78:   const collections = data[graphName] || {};
 79:   // Ensure there are collections to display
 80:   if (Object.keys(collections).length === 0) {
 81:     handleNoData(svg, width, height, "No collections found in metadata");
 82:     return;
 83:   }
 84: 
 85:   // Create a tooltip element for displaying additional information on hover
 86:   const tooltip = createTooltip();
 87: 
 88:   // Create a group element for coordinated zoom/pan operations
 89:   // All visualization elements will be added to this group for unified transformation
 90:   const g = svg.append("g");
 91: 
 92:   // Initialize arrow markers for link endpoints
 93:   // These define the different arrowheads based on relationship types
 94:   setupMarkers(svg);
 95: 
 96:   // Configure zoom and pan behavior for the visualization
 97:   setupZoom(svg, g);
 98: 
 99:   // Add zoom control buttons and instructions to the visualization
100:   createZoomControls(svg, width, height);
101: 
102:   // Initialize the force-directed simulation that will position nodes
103:   // Force simulation uses physics-based forces to arrange nodes and links
104:   const simulation = setupForceSimulation(nodes, links, width, height);
105: 
106:   // Render the links (relationships) between collections
107:   // These are SVG paths with directional markers
108:   const link = createLinks(g, links, nodes);
109: 
110:   // Debug logging for link creation
111:   console.log("Created link elements:", link.size());
112: 
113:   // Render the nodes (collections) with their properties
114:   // Each node is a complex SVG group with multiple elements
115:   const tooltipHandlers = {
116:     tooltip: tooltip,
117:     showNodeTooltip,
118:     hideTooltip,
119:     isMouseOverTooltip,
120:     clearHoverElement,
121:     scheduleHide,
122:     cancelHide,
123:   };
124:   const node = createNodes(g, nodes, tooltipHandlers);
125: 
126:   // State variables to track interactive modes
127:   let activeNode = null; // Currently selected node for tree view
128:   let isTreeView = false; // Whether we're in tree view mode
129: 
130:   // Create a state object to share with drag handler
131:   const state = {
132:     isTreeView,
133:     // Track if we've already added tree view tooltips
134:     treeViewTooltipsAdded: false,
135:     // Callback to exit tree view mode while keeping current positions
136:     onExitTreeView: () => {
137:       console.log("Exiting tree view mode due to node drag");
138:       // Force hide any visible tooltips
139:       forceHideTooltips();
140: 
141:       isTreeView = false;
142:       activeNode = null;
143: 
144:       // Don't reset node positions since we want to keep the layout
145:       // Mark all nodes as not part of the tree anymore
146:       nodes.forEach((node) => {
147:         // Keep fx/fy positions but clear tree metadata
148:         node.treePosition = null;
149:         node.treeLevel = null;
150:         node.treeParent = null;
151:       });
152: 
153:       // Remove tree-specific highlighting
154:       node
155:         .classed("node-highlighted", false)
156:         .classed("node-primary", false)
157:         .classed("node-depth-1", false)
158:         .classed("node-depth-2", false)
159:         .classed("node-faded", false);
160: 
161:       // Reset link styling
162:       link.each(function () {
163:         d3.select(this)
164:           .select("path")
165:           .classed("link-highlighted", false)
166:           .attr("marker-end", (d) => `url(#arrowhead-${d.type})`);
167: 
168:         d3.select(this)
169:           .select("text")
170:           .classed("link-label-highlighted", false)
171:           .attr("dy", 20)
172:           .style("font-size", "16px")
173:           .style("letter-spacing", "0.5px");
174:       });
175: 
176:       // Update the state for drag handler
177:       updateDragBehavior();
178:     },
179:   };
180: 
181:   // Make nodes draggable to allow manual positioning
182:   // This enhances the user experience when exploring the graph
183:   setupDrag(node, simulation, state);
184: 
185:   // Function to update drag behavior when tree view state changes
186:   const updateDragBehavior = () => {
187:     // Update the shared state object
188:     state.isTreeView = isTreeView;
189:   };
190: 
191:   // Configure highlight behavior for connected nodes and links
192:   // This helps visualize relationships when hovering over elements
193:   const { highlightConnections, resetHighlighting, createTreeLayout } =
194:     setupHighlighting(
195:       node,
196:       link,
197:       nodes,
198:       links,
199:       tooltip,
200:       simulation,
201:       svg,
202:       width,
203:       height
204:     );
205: 
206:   // Configure interactive behavior for nodes (hover and click events)
207:   node
208:     .on("mouseover", (event, d) => {
209:       // Highlight connections if not in tree view mode
210:       if (!isTreeView) {
211:         highlightConnections(event, d);
212:       }
213:     })
214:     .on("mouseout", (event, d) => {
215:       const nodeId = `node-${d.id}`;
216: 
217:       // Always clear hover element tracking when leaving node
218:       // But only if we're not hovering over the tooltip indicator or tooltip
219:       const isOnTooltipIndicator =
220:         event.relatedTarget &&
221:         (event.relatedTarget.classList.contains("tooltip-indicator") ||
222:           event.relatedTarget.parentNode.classList.contains(
223:             "tooltip-indicator-group"
224:           ));
225: 
226:       // Use the tooltip element we have in scope
227:       const isOnTooltip = isMouseOverTooltip(event, tooltip);
228: 
229:       if (!isOnTooltipIndicator && !isOnTooltip) {
230:         clearHoverElement(nodeId);
231:       }
232: 
233:       // Reset highlighting when mouse leaves node
234:       if (!isTreeView) {
235:         resetHighlighting();
236:       }
237:     })
238:     .on("click", (event, d) => {
239:       // If already in tree view mode and clicking a different node
240:       if (isTreeView && activeNode !== d.id) {
241:         // Force hide any visible tooltips
242:         forceHideTooltips();
243: 
244:         // First reset the existing tree layout
245:         resetTreeLayout(false); // Keep fixed positions when changing root node
246: 
247:         // Make the clicked node the new root for tree view
248:         activeNode = d.id;
249:         createTreeLayout(d);
250:         return;
251:       }
252: 
253:       // Toggle between force layout and tree layout views
254:       // If clicking the same node again, return to force layout
255:       if (activeNode === d.id) {
256:         // Force hide any visible tooltips
257:         forceHideTooltips();
258: 
259:         isTreeView = false;
260:         activeNode = null;
261:         resetHighlighting();
262: 
263:         // Release fixed positions to allow force simulation to resume
264:         resetTreeLayout(true);
265: 
266:         // Update drag behavior for new state
267:         updateDragBehavior();
268: 
269:         // Restart the force simulation with high alpha for movement
270:         simulation.alpha(1).restart();
271:       } else {
272:         // Force hide any visible tooltips
273:         forceHideTooltips();
274: 
275:         // Switch to tree view centered on the clicked node
276:         isTreeView = true;
277:         activeNode = d.id;
278: 
279:         // Update drag behavior for new state
280:         updateDragBehavior();
281: 
282:         // Arrange nodes in a hierarchical tree layout
283:         createTreeLayout(d);
284: 
285:         // Ensure we have tooltip functionality on all nodes in tree view
286:         if (!state.treeViewTooltipsAdded) {
287:           state.treeViewTooltipsAdded = true;
288: 
289:           // Clear any previous event handlers if they exist
290:           svg
291:             .selectAll(".node")
292:             .on("mouseover.tooltip", null)
293:             .on("mouseout.tooltip", null);
294:         }
295:       }
296:     });
297: 
298:   // Helper function to reset the tree layout
299:   function resetTreeLayout(clearFixedPositions = true) {
300:     // Release fixed positions to allow force simulation to resume
301:     nodes.forEach((node) => {
302:       if (clearFixedPositions) {
303:         node.fx = null;
304:         node.fy = null;
305:       }
306:       node.treePosition = null; // Clear tree positioning data
307:       node.treeLevel = null;
308:       node.treeParent = null;
309:     });
310:   }
311: 
312:   // Update visual elements on each simulation tick
313:   // This is the animation loop that moves nodes and links
314:   simulation.on("tick", () => {
315:     // Update link paths to follow their connected nodes
316:     link.each(function (d) {
317:       // Find the source and target node objects for this link
318:       // Needed here because the 'd' object only holds IDs initially
319:       const sourceNode = nodes.find((n) => n.id === d.source.id);
320:       const targetNode = nodes.find((n) => n.id === d.target.id);
321:       const paths = calculateLinkPath(sourceNode, targetNode); // Use the utility function
322:       // Update path
323:       d3.select(this).select("path").attr("d", paths.forward);
324:     });
325: 
326:     // Update node positions based on simulation
327:     node.attr("transform", (d) => `translate(${d.x},${d.y})`);
328:   });
329: 
330:   // Start the simulation if we have nodes to display
331:   if (nodes.length > 0) {
332:     console.log("Starting force simulation");
333:     simulation.alpha(1).restart(); // High alpha means more movement
334:   } else {
335:     handleNoData(svg, width, height, "No nodes found to display");
336:   }
337: 
338:   // Apply CSS styling to the visualization elements
339:   applyGraphStyles();
340: }
341: 
342: /**
343:  * Handle empty or invalid data scenarios with a user-friendly message
344:  *
345:  * Displays an informative message in the center of the SVG when no
346:  * visualization data is available or when errors occur.
347:  *
348:  * @param {Object} svg - The SVG element where the message will be displayed
349:  * @param {number} width - The width of the SVG
350:  * @param {number} height - The height of the SVG
351:  * @param {string} message - The message to display to the user
352:  */
353: function handleNoData(svg, width, height, message) {
354:   console.warn(message);
355:   svg
356:     .append("text")
357:     .attr("x", width / 2)
358:     .attr("y", height / 2)
359:     .attr("text-anchor", "middle")
360:     .style("font-size", "20px")
361:     .text(message);
362: }
````
