````javascript
 15:   displayLoadPrompt(); // Display initial prompt
 16: }
 17: 
 18: /**
 19:  * Setup file upload button: Handles file selection, JSON parsing, storing graph data,
 20:  * updating the dropdown, and displaying the newly loaded graph.
 21:  */
 22: function setupFileUpload() {
 23:   const fileInput = document.getElementById("jsonFileInput");
 24:   const loadButton = document.getElementById("loadJsonButton");
 25: 
 26:   loadButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
 27:     fileInput.click();
 28:   });
 29: 
 30:   fileInput.addEventListener("change", (event) => {
 31:     const file = event.target.files[0];
 32:     if (file) {
 33:       if (file.type === "application/json" || file.name.endsWith(".json")) {
 34:         const reader = new FileReader();
 35: 
 36:         reader.onload = (e) => {
 37:           try {
 38:             const data = JSON.parse(e.target.result);
 39:             const graphName = file.name;
 40:             console.log(
 41:               `JSON file '${graphName}' loaded and parsed successfully.`
 42:             );
 43: 
 44:             // Store the graph data
 45:             loadedGraphs.set(graphName, data);
 46: 
 47:             // Update the dropdown list
 48:             updateGraphListDropdown();
 49: 
 50:             // Display the newly loaded graph
 51:             displayGraph(graphName);
 52: 
 53:             // Reset file input to allow loading the same file again if needed
 54:             fileInput.value = "";
 55:           } catch (error) {
 56:             console.error("Error parsing JSON file:", error);
 57:             alert(
 58:               "Error parsing JSON file. Please check that it's valid JSON."
 59:             );
 60:           }
 61:         };
 62: 
 63:         reader.onerror = () => {
 64:           console.error("Error reading file");
 65:           alert("Error reading file. Please try again.");
 66:         };
 67: 
 68:         reader.readAsText(file);
 69:       } else {
 70:         alert("Please select a JSON file.");
 71:       }
 72:     }
 73:   });
 74: }
 75: 
 76: /**
 77:  * Setup hamburger menu interaction: Toggles dropdown visibility on button click
 78:  * and closes dropdown when clicking outside.
 79:  */
 80: function setupHamburgerMenu() {
 81:   const hamburgerBtn = document.getElementById("hamburger-btn");
 82:   const dropdown = document.getElementById("graph-list-dropdown");
 83: 
 84:   hamburgerBtn.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
 85:     event.stopPropagation(); // Prevent click from immediately closing the menu
 86:     dropdown.classList.toggle("show");
 87:   });
 88: 
 89:   // Close the dropdown if the user clicks outside of it
 90:   window.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
 91:     if (
 92:       !dropdown.contains(event.target) &&
 93:       !hamburgerBtn.contains(event.target)
 94:     ) {
 95:       if (dropdown.classList.contains("show")) {
 96:         dropdown.classList.remove("show");
 97:       }
 98:     }
 99:   });
100: }
101: 
102: /**
103:  * Update the graph list in the hamburger dropdown menu.
104:  * Populates the list with names of loaded graphs and handles click events to switch graphs.
105:  */
106: function updateGraphListDropdown() {
107:   const graphList = document.getElementById("graph-list");
108:   const dropdown = document.getElementById("graph-list-dropdown");
109: 
110:   // Clear existing list items
111:   graphList.innerHTML = "";
112: 
113:   if (loadedGraphs.size === 0) {
114:     const li = document.createElement("li");
115:     li.textContent = "No graphs loaded";
116:     li.style.fontStyle = "italic";
117:     li.style.color = "#888";
118:     graphList.appendChild(li);
119:     return;
120:   }
121: 
122:   // Add newly loaded graphs
123:   loadedGraphs.forEach((data, graphName) => {
124:     const li = document.createElement("li");
125:     li.textContent = graphName;
126:     if (graphName === currentGraphName) {
127:       li.style.fontWeight = "bold"; // Highlight current graph
128:     }
129:     li.addEventListener("click", () => {
130:       displayGraph(graphName);
131:       dropdown.classList.remove("show"); // Close dropdown after selection
132:     });
133:     graphList.appendChild(li);
134:   });
135: }
136: 
137: /**
138:  * Display the selected graph.
139:  * Clears the container (via createGraph) and renders the graph corresponding to the given name.
140:  * @param {string} graphName - The name (key) of the graph to display in the loadedGraphs map.
141:  */
142: function displayGraph(graphName) {
143:   if (!loadedGraphs.has(graphName)) {
144:     console.error(`Graph '${graphName}' not found.`);
145:     return;
146:   }
147: 
148:   console.log(`Displaying graph: ${graphName}`);
149:   currentGraphName = graphName;
150:   const data = loadedGraphs.get(graphName);
151: 
152:   // Create the new graph (createGraph clears the container internally)
153:   createGraph(data);
154: 
155:   // Update the dropdown to potentially highlight the new current graph
156:   updateGraphListDropdown();
157: }
158: 
159: /**
160:  * Display initial prompt message in the graph container when no graph is loaded.
161:  */
162: function displayLoadPrompt() {
163:   const container = document.getElementById("graph");
164:   if (!container) {
165:     console.error("Graph container not found!");
166:     return;
167:   }
168: 
169:   // Clear any existing content (like a previous graph)
170:   d3.select(container).selectAll("*").remove();
171: 
172:   const width = container.clientWidth || 1000;
173:   const height = container.clientHeight || 800;
174: 
175:   const svg = d3
176:     .select("#graph")
177:     .append("svg")
178:     .attr("width", width)
179:     .attr("height", height);
180: 
181:   // Add a message prompting the user to load a file
182:   svg
183:     .append("text")
184:     .attr("x", width / 2)
185:     .attr("y", height / 2 - 20)
186:     .attr("text-anchor", "middle")
187:     .style("font-size", "24px")
188:     .style("fill", "#555")
189:     .text("No graph loaded");
190: 
191:   svg
192:     .append("text")
193:     .attr("x", width / 2)
194:     .attr("y", height / 2 + 20)
195:     .attr("text-anchor", "middle")
196:     .style("font-size", "18px")
197:     .style("fill", "#777")
198:     .text("Click 'Load JSON File' to visualize your graph data");
199: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/core/README.md
````markdown
 1: # Core Graph Components
 2: 
 3: This directory contains the core modules responsible for loading data, processing it into a graph structure, and orchestrating the creation of the graph visualization.
 4: 
 5: ## Files
 6: 
 7: - `graphInitializer.js`: Handles the initialization process, including setting up the JSON file upload mechanism, parsing the loaded data, and triggering the graph creation. Displays an initial prompt if no data is loaded.
 8: - `dataProcessor.js`: Processes the raw JSON metadata. It identifies collections (nodes) and their properties, extracts relationships (links) between them (including handling different join types and reverse relationships), and transforms the data into `nodes` and `links` arrays suitable for D3.js.
 9: - `graphCreator.js`: The main orchestrator for the visualization. It takes the processed nodes and links, sets up the SVG canvas, initializes D3 components (force simulation, zoom, drag, tooltips), renders the visual elements (nodes, links, markers), applies styles, and manages user interactions like highlighting and tree view layouts.
10: 
11: ## Responsibilities
12: 
13: - Setting up the user interface for loading graph data (JSON file).
14: - Parsing and validating the loaded JSON data.
15: - Transforming raw metadata into graph-compatible `nodes` and `links` structures.
16: - Handling various relationship types and ensuring bidirectionality.
17: - Orchestrating the D3.js visualization setup, including SVG creation, layout initialization, and component rendering.
18: - Managing user interactions (zoom, pan, drag, hover, click) and visual feedback (highlighting, tooltips).
19: - Implementing dynamic layouts like force-directed graphs and hierarchical tree views.
20: 
21: ## Data Flow
22: 
23: 1. `graphInitializer.js` sets up the UI and waits for a JSON file upload.
24: 2. Upon file load, it reads and parses the JSON data.
25: 3. `graphInitializer.js` calls `createGraph` in `graphCreator.js` with the parsed data.
26: 4. `graphCreator.js` calls `processMetadata` in `dataProcessor.js` to transform the raw data into `nodes` and `links`.
27: 5. `graphCreator.js` uses the processed `nodes` and `links` to build and render the interactive D3.js visualization.
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/interactions/dragHandler.js
````javascript
 1: // Drag Handler - Implements dragging functionality for nodes
 2: 
 3: /**
 4:  * Setup drag functionality for nodes
 5:  * @param {Object} node - The D3 selection of nodes
 6:  * @param {Object} simulation - The D3 force simulation
 7:  * @param {Object} state - Object containing application state, including isTreeView
 8:  */
 9: export function setupDrag(node, simulation, state) {
10:   node.call(
11:     d3
12:       .drag()
13:       .on("start", (event, d) => dragstarted(event, d, simulation, state))
14:       .on("drag", (event, d) => dragged(event, d, state))
15:       .on("end", (event, d) => dragended(event, d, simulation, state))
16:   );
17: }
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Handle the start of a drag operation
21:  * @param {Object} event - The drag event
22:  * @param {Object} d - The node data
23:  * @param {Object} simulation - The D3 force simulation
24:  * @param {Object} state - Object containing application state, including isTreeView
25:  */
26: function dragstarted(event, d, simulation, state) {
27:   // Exit tree view mode if we're in it, but preserve current positions
28:   if (state.isTreeView) {
29:     // Call the callback to exit tree view mode
30:     if (state.onExitTreeView) {
31:       state.onExitTreeView();
32:     }
33:   }
34: 
35:   if (!event.active) simulation.alphaTarget(0.3).restart();
36: 
37:   // Keep the current position as the fixed position
38:   d.fx = d.x;
39:   d.fy = d.y;
40: }
41: 
42: /**
43:  * Handle the drag operation
44:  * @param {Object} event - The drag event
45:  * @param {Object} d - The node data
46:  * @param {Object} state - Object containing application state, including isTreeView
47:  */
48: function dragged(event, d, state) {
49:   d.fx = event.x;
50:   d.fy = event.y;
51: }
52: 
53: /**
54:  * Handle the end of a drag operation
55:  * @param {Object} event - The drag event
56:  * @param {Object} d - The node data
57:  * @param {Object} simulation - The D3 force simulation
58:  * @param {Object} state - Object containing application state, including isTreeView
59:  */
60: function dragended(event, d, simulation, state) {
61:   if (!event.active) simulation.alphaTarget(0);
62: 
63:   // Keep positions fixed after drag in normal mode to prevent nodes from floating away
64:   d.fx = d.x;
65:   d.fy = d.y;
66: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/interactions/highlightHandler.js
````javascript
  1: // Highlight Handler - Handles highlighting of nodes and connections
  2: 
  3: import {
  4:   showNodeTooltip,
  5:   showLinkTooltip,
  6:   hideTooltip,
  7:   isMouseOverTooltip,
  8:   clearHoverElement,
  9: } from "./tooltipHandler.js";
 10: import { createTreeLayout } from "../layouts/treeLayout.js";
 11: 
 12: /**
 13:  * Setup highlighting functionality for nodes and links.
 14:  * Attaches mouseover/mouseout listeners to links for basic highlighting and tooltip display.
 15:  * Also provides functions for more complex highlighting triggered by other events (e.g., node clicks).
 16:  *
 17:  * @param {Object} node - The D3 selection of node elements (<g class="node">).
 18:  * @param {Object} link - The D3 selection of link elements (<g class="link-group">).
 19:  * @param {Array} nodes - The complete array of node data objects.
 20:  * @param {Array} links - The complete array of link data objects.
 21:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The D3 selection of the tooltip element.
 22:  * @param {Object} simulation - The D3 force simulation instance.
 23:  * @param {Object} svg - The main SVG element D3 selection.
 24:  * @param {number} width - The width of the SVG canvas.
 25:  * @param {number} height - The height of the SVG canvas.
 26:  * @returns {Object} An object containing callable functions:
 27:  *   - `highlightConnections`: Function to highlight all nodes reachable from a given node via outgoing links.
 28:  *   - `resetHighlighting`: Function to remove all highlighting from nodes and links.
 29:  *   - `createTreeLayout`: Function to initiate the tree layout starting from a given root node.
 30:  */
 31: export function setupHighlighting(
 32:   node,
 33:   link,
 34:   nodes,
 35:   links,
 36:   tooltip,
 37:   simulation,
 38:   svg,
 39:   width,
 40:   height
 41: ) {
 42:   // Add mouseover functionality to links
 43:   link
 44:     .on("mouseover", function (event, d) {
 45:       const linkId = `link-${d.source.id}-${d.target.id}-${d.name}`;
 46:       showLinkTooltip(tooltip, d, event, linkId);
 47:       highlightLink(this, true);
 48:       highlightNodes(node, d.source.id, d.target.id, true);
 49:     })
 50:     .on("mouseout", function (event, d) {
 51:       const linkId = `link-${d.source.id}-${d.target.id}-${d.name}`;
 52:       // Only hide tooltip if not hovering over tooltip itself
 53:       // We'll let the tooltip's own mouseout handler hide it when appropriate
 54:       if (!isMouseOverTooltip(event, tooltip)) {
 55:         hideTooltip(tooltip);
 56:       }
 57:       // Always clear the hover element reference
 58:       clearHoverElement(linkId);
 59:       highlightLink(this, false);
 60:       highlightNodes(node, d.source.id, d.target.id, false);
 61:     });
 62: 
 63:   return {
 64:     highlightConnections: (event, d) =>
 65:       highlightConnections(event, d, node, link, nodes, links, tooltip),
 66:     resetHighlighting: () => resetHighlighting(node, link, tooltip),
 67:     createTreeLayout: (rootNode) =>
 68:       createTreeLayout(
 69:         rootNode,
 70:         nodes,
 71:         links,
 72:         node,
 73:         link,
 74:         simulation,
 75:         svg,
 76:         width,
 77:         height
 78:       ),
 79:   };
 80: }
 81: 
 82: /**
 83:  * Highlight a link
 84:  * @param {Object} linkElement - The link element to highlight
 85:  * @param {boolean} highlight - Whether to highlight or unhighlight
 86:  */
 87: function highlightLink(linkElement, highlight) {
 88:   // Highlight or unhighlight both forward and reverse paths
 89:   d3.select(linkElement)
 90:     .selectAll("path")
 91:     .classed("link-highlighted", highlight)
 92:     .style("stroke-width", highlight ? "3px" : null)
 93:     .attr(
 94:       "marker-end",
 95:       (d) =>
 96:         `url(#arrowhead-${
 97:           highlight
 98:             ? "highlighted"
 99:             : d.type === "general_join"
100:             ? "general_join"
101:             : d.type === "cartesian_product"
102:             ? "cartesian_product"
103:             : d.type
104:         })`
105:     );
106: 
107:   // Highlight or unhighlight both forward and reverse labels
108:   d3.select(linkElement)
109:     .selectAll("text")
110:     .classed("link-label-highlighted", highlight)
111:     .attr("dy", highlight ? 30 : 20) // Use positive values for positioning
112:     .transition()
113:     .duration(200)
114:     .style("font-size", highlight ? "26px" : "16px") // Increase/decrease size
115:     .style("letter-spacing", highlight ? "1.2px" : "0.5px"); // Adjust letter spacing
116: }
117: 
118: /**
119:  * Highlight nodes
120:  * @param {Object} node - The D3 selection of nodes
121:  * @param {string} sourceId - The source node ID
122:  * @param {string} targetId - The target node ID
123:  * @param {boolean} highlight - Whether to highlight or unhighlight
124:  */
125: function highlightNodes(node, sourceId, targetId, highlight) {
126:   node
127:     .filter((n) => n.id === sourceId || n.id === targetId)
128:     .classed("node-highlighted", highlight);
129: }
130: 
131: /**
132:  * Highlight connections starting from a node
133:  * @param {Object} event - The mouse event
134:  * @param {Object} d - The node data
135:  * @param {Object} node - The D3 selection of nodes
136:  * @param {Object} link - The D3 selection of links
137:  * @param {Array} nodes - The array of nodes
138:  * @param {Array} links - The array of links
139:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The tooltip element
140:  */
141: function highlightConnections(event, d, node, link, nodes, links, tooltip) {
142:   // Reset previous highlighting
143:   resetHighlighting(node, link, tooltip);
144: 
145:   // BFS to find all connected nodes - only following outgoing edges
146:   const queue = [{ id: d.id, depth: 0 }];
147:   const visited = new Set([d.id]);
148:   const highlightedLinks = new Set();
149:   const highlightedNodes = new Set([d.id]); // Track highlighted nodes separately
150: 
151:   while (queue.length > 0) {
152:     const current = queue.shift();
153: 
154:     // Process only outgoing connections
155:     links.forEach((link, linkIndex) => {
156:       // Only process outgoing links (node is source) to unvisited nodes
157:       if (link.source.id === current.id && !visited.has(link.target.id)) {
158:         highlightedLinks.add(linkIndex);
159:         visited.add(link.target.id);
160:         highlightedNodes.add(link.target.id);
161:         queue.push({ id: link.target.id, depth: current.depth + 1 });
162:       }
163:     });
164:   }
165: 
166:   // Highlight the visited nodes
167:   node
168:     .classed("node-highlighted", (n) => highlightedNodes.has(n.id))
169:     .classed("node-primary", (n) => n.id === d.id);
170: 
171:   // Highlight all components of the links (paths and labels)
172:   link.each(function (l, i) {
173:     if (highlightedLinks.has(i)) {
174:       // Highlight the path
175:       d3.select(this)
176:         .select("path")
177:         .classed("link-highlighted", true)
178:         .attr("marker-end", `url(#arrowhead-highlighted)`);
179: 
180:       // Highlight and increase the size of the label
181:       d3.select(this)
182:         .select("text")
183:         .classed("link-label-highlighted", true)
184:         .attr("dy", 30) // Use positive value for positioning
185:         .transition()
186:         .duration(200)
187:         .style("font-size", "25px") // Increase font size to 25px
188:         .style("letter-spacing", "1.2px"); // Adjust letter spacing for better readability
189:     }
190:   });
191: }
192: 
193: /**
194:  * Reset highlighting for all nodes and links
195:  * @param {Object} node - The D3 selection of nodes
196:  * @param {Object} link - The D3 selection of links
197:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The tooltip element
198:  */
199: function resetHighlighting(node, link, tooltip) {
200:   node.classed("node-highlighted", false).classed("node-primary", false);
201: 
202:   // Reset link styling
203:   link.each(function (d) {
204:     // Reset path styling
205:     d3.select(this)
206:       .select("path")
207:       .classed("link-highlighted", false)
208:       .style("stroke-width", null)
209:       .attr(
210:         "marker-end",
211:         (d) =>
212:           `url(#arrowhead-${
213:             d.type === "general_join"
214:               ? "general_join"
215:               : d.type === "cartesian_product"
216:               ? "cartesian_product"
217:               : d.type
218:           })`
219:       );
220: 
221:     // Reset text styling and size
222:     d3.select(this)
223:       .select("text")
224:       .classed("link-label-highlighted", false)
225:       .attr("dy", 20) // Return to default position with positive value
226:       .transition()
227:       .duration(200)
228:       .style("font-size", "16px") // Return to normal size
229:       .style("letter-spacing", "0.5px"); // Return to normal letter spacing
230:   });
231: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/interactions/README.md
````markdown
 1: # Graph Interactions
 2: 
 3: This directory contains modules responsible for handling user interactions with the graph visualization, providing navigation, exploration, and information display capabilities.
 4: 
 5: ## Files
 6: 
 7: - `dragHandler.js`: Implements node dragging using `d3.drag`. Allows users to manually position nodes, fixing their position (`fx`, `fy`) and optionally restarting the force simulation. Handles exiting tree view mode upon dragging.
 8: - `highlightHandler.js`: Manages visual highlighting of nodes and links. It includes functions to highlight connected nodes/links on hover (over links or nodes) and provides functionality to switch to a hierarchical tree layout (`createTreeLayout`) originating from a clicked node. Includes logic to reset highlighting.
 9: - `zoomHandler.js`: Implements zoom (mouse wheel) and pan (background drag) using `d3.zoom`. Configures zoom behavior (scale extent, disabling double-click zoom), adds UI controls (zoom buttons, instructions), and prevents page scroll.
10: - `tooltipHandler.js`: Creates and manages a single HTML tooltip element. Shows context-dependent information for nodes or links on hover (triggered by specific elements like tooltip indicators or link paths). Handles tooltip visibility logic, including delayed hiding and preventing closure when hovering over the tooltip itself.
11: 
12: ## Responsibilities
13: 
14: - Capturing and interpreting user input events (click, drag, mouseover, mouseout, wheel) on SVG elements (nodes, links, background, UI controls).
15: - Modifying the graph's visual state in response to interactions (e.g., applying/removing CSS classes for highlighting, updating element positions, changing SVG transform for zoom/pan).
16: - Interacting with other modules (e.g., restarting the force simulation during drag, triggering tooltip display).
17: - Managing interaction-specific states (e.g., whether tree view is active, which element is currently hovered for tooltip management).
18: - Providing UI elements for interaction control (zoom buttons, instructions).
19: 
20: ## Interaction Types
21: 
22: - **Drag & Drop:** Users can reposition nodes by dragging them. The node's position becomes fixed after dragging.
23: - **Highlighting:** Hovering over a node highlights itself and its outgoing neighbors and links. Hovering over a link highlights the link and its connected nodes. Specific styles are applied via CSS classes.
24: - **Zoom & Pan:** Users can zoom using the mouse wheel or zoom buttons, and pan by dragging the SVG background.
25: - **Tooltips:** Hovering over specific indicators on nodes or over links displays detailed information in a floating tooltip panel.
26: - **Tree View:** Clicking a node triggers `highlightHandler.js` to rearrange the graph into a hierarchical tree layout centered on that node (using logic from `layouts/treeLayout.js`). Clicking another node resets and recreates the tree view.
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/interactions/tooltipHandler.js
````javascript
  1: // Tooltip Handler - Manages tooltip display on hover over nodes and links
  2: 
  3: // Track which element (node or link) the mouse is currently over
  4: let currentHoverElement = null;
  5: // ID for tooltip auto-hide timeout - Managed globally now
  6: let pendingHideTimeoutId = null;
  7: 
  8: /**
  9:  * Creates and appends the main tooltip div element to the document body.
 10:  * The tooltip is initially hidden and configured with mouse event handlers
 11:  * to prevent auto-hiding when the mouse is moved over the tooltip itself.
 12:  *
 13:  * @returns {Object} The D3 selection of the created tooltip div.
 14:  */
 15: export function createTooltip() {
 16:   const tooltip = d3
 17:     .select("body")
 18:     .append("div")
 19:     .attr("class", "tooltip")
 20:     .style("opacity", 0);
 21: 
 22:   tooltip
 23:     .on("mouseover", function () {
 24:       // Cancel any pending hide when mouse enters the tooltip
 25:       cancelHide();
 26:       // Ensure it's visible and interactive
 27:       d3.select(this).transition().duration(0).style("opacity", 0.9);
 28:       d3.select(this).style("pointer-events", "auto");
 29:     })
 30:     .on("mouseout", function (event) {
 31:       // Hide immediately when mouse leaves the tooltip itself
 32:       hideTooltip(d3.select(this));
 33:       // Clear hover tracking associated with this tooltip session
 34:       if (currentHoverElement) {
 35:         clearHoverElement(currentHoverElement);
 36:       }
 37:     });
 38: 
 39:   return tooltip;
 40: }
 41: 
 42: /**
 43:  * Shows and populates the tooltip with details about a graph node.
 44:  * Calculates the tooltip position based on the mouse event coordinates.
 45:  *
 46:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The D3 selection of the tooltip element.
 47:  * @param {Object} node - The data object for the node being hovered.
 48:  * @param {Object} event - The D3 mouse event that triggered the tooltip.
 49:  * @param {string} elementId - A unique identifier for the hovered element (e.g., "node-123") used for tracking.
 50:  */
 51: export function showNodeTooltip(tooltip, node, event, elementId) {
 52:   // Update the current hover element
 53:   currentHoverElement = elementId;
 54: 
 55:   // Make tooltip visible and interactive
 56:   tooltip.transition().duration(200).style("opacity", 0.9);
 57:   tooltip.style("pointer-events", "auto"); // Ensure tooltip is interactive when shown
 58: 
 59:   // Create a table-like structured tooltip that's still compact
 60:   let tooltipContent = `<div class="tooltip-title">${node.name}</div>`;
 61: 
 62:   // Create a table structure for the data
 63:   tooltipContent += `<table class="tooltip-table">
 64:     <tr>
 65:       <td class="tooltip-label">Path:</td>
 66:       <td>${node.tablePath}</td>
 67:     </tr>
 68:     <tr>
 69:       <td class="tooltip-label">Unique by:</td>
 70:       <td>${formatUniqueProperties(node.uniqueProperties)}</td>
 71:     </tr>
 72:   </table>`;
 73: 
 74:   // Add columns with smaller font
 75:   if (node.columns && node.columns.length > 0) {
 76:     tooltipContent += `<div class="tooltip-section">
 77:       <div class="tooltip-section-title">Columns</div>
 78:       <div class="tooltip-small-content">`;
 79: 
 80:     // Only show first 8 columns with smaller font to keep compact
 81:     const displayColumns = node.columns.slice(0, 8);
 82:     displayColumns.forEach((col) => {
 83:       tooltipContent += `<div class="tooltip-column">${col.name} <span class="tooltip-datatype">(${col.dataType})</span></div>`;
 84:     });
 85: 
 86:     // If more columns exist, add a count
 87:     if (node.columns.length > 8) {
 88:       tooltipContent += `<div class="tooltip-more">+${
 89:         node.columns.length - 8
 90:       } more</div>`;
 91:     }
 92: 
 93:     tooltipContent += `</div></div>`;
 94:   }
 95: 
 96:   // Add relationships with smaller font
 97:   if (node.subcollections && node.subcollections.length > 0) {
 98:     tooltipContent += `<div class="tooltip-section">
 99:       <div class="tooltip-section-title">Relationships</div>
100:       <div class="tooltip-small-content">`;
101: 
102:     // Only show first 5 relationships with smaller font to keep compact
103:     const displayRelations = node.subcollections.slice(0, 5);
104:     displayRelations.forEach((rel) => {
105:       tooltipContent += `<div class="tooltip-relation">${rel.name} <span class="tooltip-relation-type">(${rel.type} → ${rel.target})</span></div>`;
106:     });
107: 
108:     // If more relationships exist, add a count
109:     if (node.subcollections.length > 5) {
110:       tooltipContent += `<div class="tooltip-more">+${
111:         node.subcollections.length - 5
112:       } more</div>`;
113:     }
114: 
115:     tooltipContent += `</div></div>`;
116:   }
117: 
118:   tooltip
119:     .html(tooltipContent)
120:     .style("left", event.pageX + 10 + "px")
121:     .style("top", event.pageY - 28 + "px");
122: }
123: 
124: /**
125:  * Formats an array of unique properties (or arrays of properties) into a compact string.
126:  * Used for display within the node tooltip.
127:  *
128:  * @param {Array<string>|Array<Array<string>>} properties - The unique properties array from node data.
129:  * @returns {string} A formatted string representation (e.g., "prop1, prop2 | prop3, prop4" or "None").
130:  */
131: function formatUniqueProperties(properties) {
132:   if (!properties || properties.length === 0) return "None";
133: 
134:   return Array.isArray(properties[0])
135:     ? properties.map((arr) => arr.join(", ")).join(" | ")
136:     : properties.join(", ");
137: }
138: 
139: /**
140:  * Shows and populates the tooltip with details about a graph link (relationship).
141:  * Calculates the tooltip position based on the mouse event coordinates.
142:  *
143:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The D3 selection of the tooltip element.
144:  * @param {Object} link - The data object for the link being hovered.
145:  * @param {Object} event - The D3 mouse event that triggered the tooltip.
146:  * @param {string} elementId - A unique identifier for the hovered element (e.g., "link-a-b-rel") used for tracking.
147:  */
148: export function showLinkTooltip(tooltip, link, event, elementId) {
149:   // Update the current hover element
150:   currentHoverElement = elementId;
151: 
152:   tooltip.transition().duration(200).style("opacity", 0.9);
153: 
154:   // Create a table-like structured tooltip
155:   let tooltipContent = `<div class="tooltip-title">${link.source.id}.${link.name} → ${link.target.id}</div>`;
156: 
157:   // Create a table structure for the data
158:   tooltipContent += `<table class="tooltip-table">
159:     <tr>
160:       <td class="tooltip-label">Type:</td>
161:       <td>${link.type}</td>
162:     </tr>`;
163: 
164:   // Add minimal relationship properties
165:   if (
166:     link.type === "simple_join" ||
167:     link.type === "compound" ||
168:     link.type === "general_join"
169:   ) {
170:     tooltipContent += `
171:     <tr>
172:       <td class="tooltip-label">Singular:</td>
173:       <td><span class="${link.singular ? "true-value" : "false-value"}">${
174:       link.singular ? "Yes" : "No"
175:     }</span></td>
176:     </tr>
177:     <tr>
178:       <td class="tooltip-label">No Collisions:</td>
179:       <td><span class="${link.noCollisions ? "true-value" : "false-value"}">${
180:       link.noCollisions ? "Yes" : "No"
181:     }</span></td>
182:     </tr>`;
183: 
184:     // If it's a general join, add the condition
185:     if (link.type === "general_join" && link.condition) {
186:       tooltipContent += `
187:       <tr>
188:         <td class="tooltip-label">Condition:</td>
189:         <td>${link.condition}</td>
190:       </tr>`;
191:     }
192:   }
193: 
194:   tooltipContent += `</table>`;
195: 
196:   // Add reverse relationship note at the bottom if needed
197:   if (link.isReverse) {
198:     tooltipContent += `<div class="tooltip-hint">(Reverse relationship)</div>`;
199:   }
200: 
201:   tooltip
202:     .html(tooltipContent)
203:     .style("left", event.pageX + 10 + "px")
204:     .style("top", event.pageY - 28 + "px");
205: }
206: 
207: /**
208:  * Clears the global tracking variable for the currently hovered element,
209:  * but only if the provided elementId matches the currently tracked one.
210:  * This prevents clearing the hover state if the mouse quickly moves between elements.
211:  *
212:  * @param {string} elementId - The unique identifier of the element whose hover state might need clearing.
213:  */
214: export function clearHoverElement(elementId) {
215:   // Only clear if we're still tracking the same element
216:   if (currentHoverElement === elementId) {
217:     currentHoverElement = null;
218:   }
219: }
220: 
221: /**
222:  * Hides the tooltip by transitioning its opacity to 0 and disabling pointer events.
223:  *
224:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The D3 selection of the tooltip element.
225:  */
226: export function hideTooltip(tooltip) {
227:   tooltip.transition().duration(200).style("opacity", 0);
228:   tooltip.style("pointer-events", "none");
229: }
230: 
231: /**
232:  * Cancels any scheduled tooltip hide operation (clears the pending timeout).
233:  * This is typically called when the mouse enters the tooltip itself or another graph element.
234:  */
235: export function cancelHide() {
236:   if (pendingHideTimeoutId) {
237:     clearTimeout(pendingHideTimeoutId);
238:     pendingHideTimeoutId = null;
239:   }
240: }
241: 
242: /**
243:  * Schedules the tooltip to be hidden after a specified delay.
244:  * If a hide operation is already scheduled, it is cancelled first.
245:  * When the hide operation completes, the associated hover element tracking is cleared.
246:  *
247:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The D3 selection of the tooltip element.
248:  * @param {string} elementId - The unique identifier of the element associated with this hide action.
249:  * @param {number} delay - The delay in milliseconds before hiding the tooltip.
250:  */
251: export function scheduleHide(tooltip, elementId, delay) {
252:   // Clear any existing timer first
253:   cancelHide();
254: 
255:   pendingHideTimeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
256:     hideTooltip(tooltip);
257:     clearHoverElement(elementId); // Clear tracking when hiding completes
258:     pendingHideTimeoutId = null;
259:   }, delay);
260: }
261: 
262: /**
263:  * Checks if the current mouse event coordinates are within the bounds of the tooltip element.
264:  *
265:  * @param {Object} event - The D3 mouse event (containing clientX, clientY).
266:  * @param {Object} tooltip - The D3 selection of the tooltip element.
267:  * @returns {boolean} True if the mouse coordinates are inside the tooltip's bounding rectangle, false otherwise.
268:  */
269: export function isMouseOverTooltip(event, tooltip) {
270:   const tooltipNode = tooltip.node();
271:   if (!tooltipNode) return false;
272: 
273:   const tooltipBounds = tooltipNode.getBoundingClientRect();
274:   const x = event.clientX;
275:   const y = event.clientY;
276: 
277:   return (
278:     x >= tooltipBounds.left &&
279:     x <= tooltipBounds.right &&
280:     y >= tooltipBounds.top &&
281:     y <= tooltipBounds.bottom
282:   );
283: }
284: 
285: /**
286:  * Immediately hides any visible tooltip, cancels pending hide operations,
287:  * and resets the hover element tracking state.
288:  * Useful for situations like view changes or graph reloads where tooltips should disappear instantly.
289:  */
290: export function forceHideTooltips() {
291:   // Reset tracking variables
292:   currentHoverElement = null;
293: 
294:   // Clear any pending timeouts
295:   if (pendingHideTimeoutId) {
296:     clearTimeout(pendingHideTimeoutId);
297:     pendingHideTimeoutId = null;
298:   }
299: 
300:   // Hide the tooltip immediately
301:   const tooltip = d3.select("body").select(".tooltip");
302:   if (!tooltip.empty()) {
303:     tooltip.transition().duration(0).style("opacity", 0);
304:   }
305: }
306: 
307: /**
308:  * Checks if the mouse event coordinates are over the small tooltip indicator
309:  * circle rendered in the bottom-right corner of a node.
310:  *
311:  * @param {Object} event - The D3 mouse event (containing clientX, clientY).
312:  * @param {Object} node - The data object for the node whose indicator is being checked.
313:  * @returns {boolean} True if the mouse is within the indicator's bounds (plus a small buffer), false otherwise.
314:  */
315: export function isMouseInBottomRightQuadrant(event, node) {
316:   // Get the node element
317:   const nodeElement = document.getElementById(`node-${node.id}`);
318:   if (!nodeElement) return false;
319: 
320:   // Find the tooltip indicator circle within the node
321:   const indicator = nodeElement.querySelector(".tooltip-indicator");
322:   if (!indicator) return false;
323: 
324:   // Get indicator bounds
325:   const indicatorBounds = indicator.getBoundingClientRect();
326: 
327:   // Calculate distance from mouse to center of indicator
328:   const dx = event.clientX - (indicatorBounds.left + indicatorBounds.width / 2);
329:   const dy = event.clientY - (indicatorBounds.top + indicatorBounds.height / 2);
330:   const distance = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
331: 
332:   // Check if mouse is within the indicator circle (with a small buffer)
333:   // The indicator has radius 8, we add a few pixels buffer for easier interaction
334:   return distance <= 12;
335: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/interactions/zoomHandler.js
````javascript
  1: // Zoom Handler - Implements zoom and pan functionality for the graph
  2: 
  3: /**
  4:  * Initializes and configures the D3 zoom behavior for the SVG canvas.
  5:  * Sets up the zoom/pan limits, attaches the zoom listener to the main SVG group,
  6:  * disables double-click zoom, prevents page scroll during zoom, and sets an initial transform.
  7:  *
  8:  * @param {Object} svg - The D3 selection of the main SVG element.
  9:  * @param {Object} g - The D3 selection of the primary SVG group (`<g>`) that contains all graph elements (nodes, links).
 10:  *                  This is the group whose transform will be updated by the zoom behavior.
 11:  * @returns {Object} The configured D3 zoom behavior object, which can be used to programmatically control zoom/pan.
 12:  */
 13: export function setupZoom(svg, g) {
 14:   // Enable zoom and pan behavior with enhanced settings
 15:   const zoom = d3
 16:     .zoom()
 17:     .scaleExtent([0.05, 8]) // Allow zooming out more (to 5% of original size)
 18:     .on("zoom", (event) => {
 19:       g.attr("transform", event.transform);
 20:       // Log zoom level for debugging
 21:       console.log("Zoom level:", event.transform.k);
 22:     });
 23: 
 24:   // Apply zoom to SVG and enable proper event handling
 25:   svg
 26:     .call(zoom)
 27:     .on("dblclick.zoom", null) // Disable double-click zoom to avoid accidental zoom
 28:     .on("wheel", (event) => {
 29:       // Prevent page scrolling when zooming the graph
 30:       if (event.target.closest("svg")) {
 31:         event.preventDefault();
 32:       }
 33:     });
 34: 
 35:   // Initialize with a more zoomed out view to show the whole graph
 36:   svg.call(
 37:     zoom.transform,
 38:     d3.zoomIdentity
 39:       .translate(svg.attr("width") / 2, svg.attr("height") / 2)
 40:       .scale(0.4)
 41:   );
 42: 
 43:   return zoom;
 44: }
 45: 
 46: /**
 47:  * Creates and appends zoom instruction text and zoom control buttons (+/-) to the SVG canvas.
 48:  * These elements are positioned in corners and are not affected by the zoom/pan transforms applied to the main graph group `g`.
 49:  *
 50:  * @param {Object} svg - The D3 selection of the main SVG element where controls will be added.
 51:  * @param {number} width - The width of the SVG canvas, used for positioning controls.
 52:  * @param {number} height - The height of the SVG canvas, used for positioning controls.
 53:  */
 54: export function createZoomControls(svg, width, height) {
 55:   // Add zoom instructions text
 56:   svg
 57:     .append("text")
 58:     .attr("class", "zoom-instructions")
 59:     .attr("x", 20)
 60:     .attr("y", height - 20)
 61:     .style("font-size", "14px")
 62:     .style("fill", "#666")
 63:     .text("Use mouse wheel to zoom, drag to pan");
 64: 
 65:   // Add zoom controls
 66:   const zoomControls = svg
 67:     .append("g")
 68:     .attr("class", "zoom-controls")
 69:     .attr("transform", `translate(${width - 100}, ${height - 80})`);
 70: 
 71:   // Zoom in button
 72:   createZoomButton(zoomControls, 0, 0, "+", 1.3, svg);
 73: 
 74:   // Zoom out button
 75:   createZoomButton(zoomControls, 0, 40, "−", 0.7, svg);
 76: }
 77: 
 78: /**
 79:  * Creates a single zoom button (background rectangle and text label) within a given container group.
 80:  * Attaches a click handler to trigger a zoom transition on the main SVG element.
 81:  *
 82:  * @param {Object} container - The D3 selection of the SVG group (`<g>`) where the button should be appended.
 83:  * @param {number} x - The x-coordinate for the button's top-left corner, relative to the container.
 84:  * @param {number} y - The y-coordinate for the button's top-left corner, relative to the container.
 85:  * @param {string} label - The text label for the button (e.g., "+", "−").
 86:  * @param {number} scaleFactor - The multiplicative factor to apply when the button is clicked (e.g., 1.3 for zoom in, 0.7 for zoom out).
 87:  * @param {Object} svg - The D3 selection of the main SVG element, which the zoom action targets.
 88:  */
 89: function createZoomButton(container, x, y, label, scaleFactor, svg) {
 90:   // Create button background
 91:   container
 92:     .append("rect")
 93:     .attr("x", x)
 94:     .attr("y", y)
 95:     .attr("width", 30)
 96:     .attr("height", 30)
 97:     .attr("rx", 5)
 98:     .attr("fill", "#f8f9fa")
 99:     .attr("stroke", "#ddd")
100:     .style("cursor", "pointer")
101:     .on("click", () => {
102:       svg.transition().duration(300).call(d3.zoom().scaleBy, scaleFactor);
103:     });
104: 
105:   // Create button label
106:   container
107:     .append("text")
108:     .attr("x", x + 15)
109:     .attr("y", y + 20)
110:     .attr("text-anchor", "middle")
111:     .style("font-size", "18px")
112:     .style("font-weight", "bold")
113:     .style("user-select", "none")
114:     .style("cursor", "pointer")
115:     .text(label)
116:     .on("click", () => {
117:       svg.transition().duration(300).call(d3.zoom().scaleBy, scaleFactor);
118:     });
119: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/layouts/forceLayout.js
````javascript
 1: // Force Layout - Implements a force-directed graph layout using D3.js
 2: // D3 force simulations use physics-based calculations to position nodes in a network graph
 3: 
 4: /**
 5:  * Setup the force simulation for the graph
 6:  *
 7:  * - D3 force layout uses physics simulation to position elements
 8:  * - Forces can be gravity, collision, links, and charges
 9:  * - The simulation runs continuously until it reaches equilibrium
10:  *
11:  * @param {Array} nodes - The array of nodes to position
12:  * @param {Array} links - The array of links connecting nodes
13:  * @param {number} width - The width of the SVG container
14:  * @param {number} height - The height of the SVG container
15:  * @returns {Object} The D3 force simulation instance that can be used to update positions
16:  */
17: export function setupForceSimulation(nodes, links, width, height) {
18:   return d3
19:     .forceSimulation(nodes) // Initialize the simulation with our nodes
20:     .force(
21:       "link",
22:       d3
23:         .forceLink(links) // Add link forces that pull connected nodes together
24:         .id((d) => d.id) // Specify which property to use as node identifier
25:         .distance(600) // Target distance between linked nodes (higher = more spread out)
26:     )
27:     .force("charge", d3.forceManyBody().strength(-6000)) // Add repulsion between nodes (negative = repel, positive = attract)
28:     .force("center", d3.forceCenter(width / 2, height / 2)) // Add centering force to keep the graph centered in view
29:     .force(
30:       "collision",
31:       d3.forceCollide().radius((d) => Math.sqrt(d.width * d.height) / 2 + 150) // Prevent node overlap by adding collision detection
32:     );
33: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/layouts/README.md
````markdown
 1: # Graph Layouts
 2: 
 3: This directory contains modules that define strategies for positioning nodes and links within the visualization area.
 4: 
 5: ## Files
 6: 
 7: - `forceLayout.js`: Configures and initializes the default D3.js force-directed simulation. This layout uses physics-based forces (link attraction, node repulsion, collision avoidance, centering) to automatically arrange the graph.
 8: - `treeLayout.js`: Implements a hierarchical tree layout algorithm. When invoked, it arranges a subset of the graph (starting from a selected root node and following outgoing links) into distinct levels, setting fixed positions (`fx`, `fy`) for nodes in the tree.
 9: 
10: ## Responsibilities
11: 
12: - Calculating and assigning `x`, `y` coordinates (or `fx`, `fy` for fixed positions) to each node.
13: - Defining the spatial arrangement of the graph based on either physics simulation or hierarchical structure.
14: - Interacting with the D3 simulation (e.g., initializing forces, restarting the simulation).
15: - Providing functions to switch between layout modes (e.g., triggering the tree layout calculation).
16: 
17: ## Layout Types
18: 
19: ### Force Layout (`forceLayout.js`)
20: 
21: - **Mechanism:** Uses D3's `forceSimulation` with link, charge, center, and collision forces.
22: - **Behavior:** Nodes push apart, links pull together, nodes avoid overlapping, and the whole graph tends towards the center.
23: - **Use Case:** Default view for exploring the overall network structure.
24: - **Activation:** Initialized by `graphCreator.js`.
25: 
26: ### Tree Layout (`treeLayout.js`)
27: 
28: - **Mechanism:** Custom BFS algorithm calculates levels and horizontal positions based on outgoing relationships from a root node. Sets `fx`/`fy` coordinates to fix nodes in a tree structure.
29: - **Behavior:** Organizes nodes into clear parent-child levels. Nodes not part of the selected hierarchy are moved off-screen. Uses fixed positioning, overriding the force simulation for tree nodes.
30: - **Use Case:** Visualizing the hierarchy or dependencies originating from a specific node.
31: - **Activation:** Triggered by `highlightHandler.js` (`createTreeLayout` function) upon node click.
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/layouts/treeLayout.js
````javascript
  1: // Tree Layout - Implements a hierarchical tree visualization layout
  2: // This layout organizes nodes in a parent-child hierarchy with multiple levels
  3: 
  4: /**
  5:  * Calculates and applies a hierarchical tree layout starting from a given root node.
  6:  *
  7:  * This function performs the following steps:
  8:  * 1. Resets any existing tree layout properties on all nodes.
  9:  * 2. Performs a Breadth-First Search (BFS) starting from the `rootNode`,
 10:  *    following only outgoing links to discover reachable nodes.
 11:  * 3. Assigns `treeLevel` (depth) and `treeParent` (ID of parent) to discovered nodes.
 12:  * 4. Calculates a relative horizontal `treePosition` for nodes within each level to spread them out.
 13:  * 5. Sets fixed positions (`fx`, `fy`) for all nodes:
 14:  *    - Nodes in the tree are positioned according to their level (vertical) and position (horizontal).
 15:  *    - Nodes *not* in the tree are moved far off-screen by setting high `fx`/`fy` values.
 16:  * 6. Calls `highlightTreeView` to apply specific visual styles to tree nodes/links.
 17:  * 7. Restarts the D3 force simulation so it respects the new `fx`/`fy` values.
 18:  * 8. Calls `fitTreeToView` to adjust the SVG zoom/pan to focus on the generated tree.
 19:  *
 20:  * Note: This function modifies the `nodes` array in-place, adding/updating `treeLevel`,
 21:  * `treePosition`, `treeParent`, `fx`, and `fy` properties on the node objects.
 22:  *
 23:  * @param {Object} rootNode - The node data object to use as the root of the tree.
 24:  * @param {Array} nodes - The complete array of node data objects.
 25:  * @param {Array} links - The complete array of link data objects.
 26:  * @param {Object} node - The D3 selection of node elements (<g class="node">).
 27:  * @param {Object} link - The D3 selection of link elements (<g class="link-group">).
 28:  * @param {Object} simulation - The D3 force simulation instance.
 29:  * @param {Object} svg - The main SVG element D3 selection.
 30:  * @param {number} width - The width of the SVG canvas.
 31:  * @param {number} height - The height of the SVG canvas.
 32:  */
 33: export function createTreeLayout(
 34:   rootNode,
 35:   nodes,
 36:   links,
 37:   node,
 38:   link,
 39:   simulation,
 40:   svg,
 41:   width,
 42:   height
 43: ) {
 44:   // Reset all tree positions
 45:   nodes.forEach((n) => {
 46:     n.treePosition = null; // Horizontal position within level
 47:     n.treeLevel = null; // Vertical level in hierarchy (0 = root)
 48:     n.treeParent = null; // ID of parent node
 49:   });
 50: 
 51:   // Set root node
 52:   const root = nodes.find((n) => n.id === rootNode.id);
 53:   root.treeLevel = 0;
 54:   root.treePosition = 0;
 55: 
 56:   // BFS to establish tree relationships - only for outgoing edges
 57:   // Breadth-First Search ensures we process level by level
 58:   const queue = [{ id: root.id, level: 0 }];
 59:   const visited = new Set([root.id]);
 60:   const nodesByLevel = new Map(); // Maps level number to array of nodes
 61:   nodesByLevel.set(0, [root]);
 62: 
 63:   while (queue.length > 0) {
 64:     const current = queue.shift();
 65:     const nextLevel = current.level + 1;
 66: 
 67:     // Only process outgoing connections
 68:     links.forEach((link) => {
 69:       // Only consider outgoing connections (current is source)
 70:       if (link.source.id === current.id && !visited.has(link.target.id)) {
 71:         const targetNode = nodes.find((n) => n.id === link.target.id);
 72: 
 73:         if (targetNode) {
 74:           // Set tree properties
 75:           targetNode.treeLevel = nextLevel;
 76:           targetNode.treeParent = current.id;
 77:           targetNode.connectionType = "outgoing";
 78: 
 79:           // Add to level collection
 80:           if (!nodesByLevel.has(nextLevel)) {
 81:             nodesByLevel.set(nextLevel, []);
 82:           }
 83:           nodesByLevel.get(nextLevel).push(targetNode);
 84: 
 85:           // Add to processing queue and mark as visited
 86:           queue.push({ id: targetNode.id, level: nextLevel });
 87:           visited.add(targetNode.id);
 88:         }
 89:       }
 90:     });
 91:   }
 92: 
 93:   // Calculate horizontal positions for each level
 94:   // This distributes nodes evenly across the width
 95:   nodesByLevel.forEach((levelNodes, level) => {
 96:     const levelWidth = levelNodes.length;
 97:     levelNodes.forEach((node, i) => {
 98:       // Calculate position with more even spacing
 99:       // Centers nodes within their level (negative values on left, positive on right)
100:       node.treePosition = i - (levelWidth - 1) / 2;
101:     });
102:   });
103: 
104:   // Apply tree layout with increased spacing
105:   const LEVEL_VERTICAL_SPACING = 800; // Vertical distance between tree levels
106:   const HORIZONTAL_SPACING = 850; // Horizontal distance between sibling nodes
107: 
108:   // Get the maximum number of nodes at any level for horizontal centering
109:   let maxNodesInLevel = 0;
110:   nodesByLevel.forEach((nodes) => {
111:     maxNodesInLevel = Math.max(maxNodesInLevel, nodes.length);
112:   });
113: 
114:   nodes.forEach((node) => {
115:     if (node.treeLevel !== null) {
116:       // Fix nodes in place in a tree structure with better centering
117:       // Using fx/fy properties to override force simulation positions
118:       // These fixed positions ensure the tree structure is maintained and dragging is unnecessary
119:       node.fx = width / 2 + node.treePosition * HORIZONTAL_SPACING;
120:       node.fy = height / 5 + node.treeLevel * LEVEL_VERTICAL_SPACING;
121:     } else {
122:       // Move unconnected nodes far away
123:       node.fx = width * 2; // Move off-screen
124:       node.fy = height * 2;
125:     }
126:   });
127: 
128:   // Highlight only the nodes and links in the tree
129:   highlightTreeView(rootNode, nodes, links, node, link);
130: 
131:   // Restart simulation with fixed nodes
132:   // This updates the visualization with new positions
133:   simulation.alpha(1).restart();
134: 
135:   // Set zoom to fit the tree better
136:   fitTreeToView(nodes, svg, width, height);
137: }
138: 
139: /**
140:  * Applies visual highlighting styles specific to the tree view.
141:  * This function assumes that `treeLevel`, `treeParent`, etc., have already been calculated
142:  * and set on the node objects by `createTreeLayout`.
143:  *
144:  * Steps:
145:  * 1. Identifies all nodes and links that are part of the current tree structure.
146:  * 2. Resets any previous highlighting/styling on all nodes and links.
147:  * 3. Applies specific CSS classes to nodes based on their tree status and level:
148:  *    - `.node-highlighted` for all tree nodes.
149:  *    - `.node-primary` for the root node.
150:  *    - `.node-depth-1`, `.node-depth-2` for nodes at specific levels.
151:  *    - `.node-faded` for nodes *not* part of the tree.
152:  * 4. Applies specific styling to links that connect nodes within the tree:
153:  *    - Uses `.link-highlighted` class.
154:  *    - Sets marker to `arrowhead-highlighted`.
155:  *    - Adjusts label position (`dy`) and size/spacing for emphasis.
156:  * 5. Applies minor text style adjustments (letter-spacing) to tree nodes after a short delay.
157:  *
158:  * @param {Object} rootNode - The node data object used as the root of the tree.
159:  * @param {Array} nodes - The complete array of node data objects (with tree properties calculated).
160:  * @param {Array} links - The complete array of link data objects.
161:  * @param {Object} node - The D3 selection of node elements (<g class="node">).
162:  * @param {Object} link - The D3 selection of link elements (<g class="link-group">).
163:  */
164: function highlightTreeView(rootNode, nodes, links, node, link) {
165:   // Identify nodes and links that are part of the tree
166:   const treeNodes = new Set();
167:   const treeLinks = new Map(); // Maps link index to boolean
168: 
169:   // Identify all nodes in the tree
170:   nodes.forEach((n) => {
171:     if (n.treeLevel !== null) {
172:       treeNodes.add(n.id);
173:     }
174:   });
175: 
176:   // Identify links that are part of the tree (only outgoing links from parent to child)
177:   links.forEach((l, i) => {
178:     const sourceNode = nodes.find((n) => n.id === l.source.id);
179:     const targetNode = nodes.find((n) => n.id === l.target.id);
180: 
181:     // A link is part of the tree if the source is a parent and target is its child
182:     const isTreeLink =
183:       sourceNode.treeLevel !== null &&
184:       targetNode.treeLevel !== null &&
185:       targetNode.treeParent === sourceNode.id;
186: 
187:     treeLinks.set(i, isTreeLink);
188:   });
189: 
190:   // First reset all highlighting to ensure clean state
191:   node
192:     .classed("node-highlighted", false)
193:     .classed("node-primary", false)
194:     .classed("node-depth-1", false)
195:     .classed("node-depth-2", false)
196:     .classed("node-faded", false);
197: 
198:   // Reset all link styling
199:   link.each(function () {
200:     d3.select(this)
201:       .select("path")
202:       .classed("link-highlighted", false)
203:       .attr("marker-end", (d) => `url(#arrowhead-${d.type})`);
204: 
205:     d3.select(this)
206:       .select("text")
207:       .classed("link-label-highlighted", false)
208:       .attr("dy", 20)
209:       .style("font-size", "16px")
210:       .style("letter-spacing", "0.5px");
211:   });
212: 
213:   // Apply highlighting to nodes
214:   node
215:     .classed("node-highlighted", (n) => n.treeLevel !== null) // Highlight all tree nodes
216:     .classed("node-primary", (n) => n.id === rootNode.id) // Special highlight for root
217:     .classed("node-depth-1", (n) => n.treeLevel === 1) // Level 1 styling
218:     .classed("node-depth-2", (n) => n.treeLevel === 2) // Level 2 styling
219:     .classed("node-faded", (n) => n.treeLevel === null); // Fade non-tree nodes
220: 
221:   // Apply highlighting to links - only outgoing connections
222:   link.each(function (l, i) {
223:     const isTreeLink = treeLinks.get(i);
224: 
225:     if (isTreeLink) {
226:       // Highlight the path
227:       d3.select(this)
228:         .select("path")
229:         .classed("link-highlighted", true)
230:         .attr("marker-end", "url(#arrowhead-highlighted)");
231: 
232:       // Highlight and increase size of the label
233:       const textElement = d3.select(this).select("text");
234: 
235:       // Position text labels better in tree mode - use different dy values based on level
236:       const sourceLevel = nodes.find((n) => n.id === l.source.id).treeLevel;
237:       const targetLevel = nodes.find((n) => n.id === l.target.id).treeLevel;
238: 
239:       // If the link connects nodes with different tree levels, adjust vertical position
240:       if (sourceLevel !== null && targetLevel !== null) {
241:         // Use positive dy value for consistent positioning with other views
242:         textElement.attr("dy", 30); // Use positive value for positioning
243:       }
244: 
245:       textElement
246:         .classed("link-label-highlighted", true)
247:         .transition()
248:         .duration(200)
249:         .style("font-size", "26px") // Consistent with hover highlight size
250:         .style("letter-spacing", "1.2px"); // Match letter spacing with other highlighted links
251:     }
252:   });
253: 
254:   // Add a slight delay before applying additional text styles to ensure transitions complete
255:   setTimeout(() => {
256:     // Enhance text readability for highlighted nodes in the tree
257:     node.each(function (n) {
258:       if (n.treeLevel !== null) {
259:         // Select all text elements in this node
260:         d3.select(this)
261:           .selectAll("text")
262:           .style("letter-spacing", function () {
263:             // Apply larger spacing to titles, normal spacing to other text
264:             return d3.select(this).classed("node-title") ? "1px" : "0.8px";
265:           });
266:       }
267:     });
268:   }, 250);
269: }
270: 
271: /**
272:  * Calculates the appropriate zoom transform (scale and translate) to fit the
273:  * currently laid-out tree structure within the SVG viewport bounds and applies it.
274:  *
275:  * Steps:
276:  * 1. Filters the `nodes` array to include only those nodes that are part of the tree
277:  *    (i.e., have a non-null `treeLevel`).
278:  * 2. Calculates the bounding box (min/max X and Y coordinates) encompassing all tree nodes,
279:  *    using their fixed positions (`fx`, `fy`) and dimensions (`width`, `height`).
280:  * 3. Adds padding to the bounding box.
281:  * 4. Calculates the required scale factor to fit the padded bounding box within the
282:  *    SVG `width` and `height`, ensuring the scale doesn't exceed 1.0 and applying a small margin.
283:  * 5. Calculates the translation needed to center the bounding box within the viewport.
284:  * 6. Applies the calculated scale and translation to the main SVG element using a smooth
285:  *    zoom transition after a short delay (allowing the simulation tick to potentially update positions first).
286:  *
287:  * @param {Array} nodes - The complete array of node data objects (with tree properties and `fx`/`fy` calculated).
288:  * @param {Object} svg - The D3 selection of the main SVG element.
289:  * @param {number} width - The width of the SVG canvas.
290:  * @param {number} height - The height of the SVG canvas.
291:  */
292: function fitTreeToView(nodes, svg, width, height) {
293:   // Filter to only include tree nodes (those with a level assigned)
294:   const treeNodes = nodes.filter((n) => n.treeLevel !== null);
295:   if (treeNodes.length > 0) {
296:     // Calculate bounds
297:     let minX = Infinity,
298:       maxX = -Infinity,
299:       minY = Infinity,
300:       maxY = -Infinity;
301:     treeNodes.forEach((n) => {
302:       minX = Math.min(minX, n.fx - n.width / 2);
303:       maxX = Math.max(maxX, n.fx + n.width / 2);
304:       minY = Math.min(minY, n.fy - n.height / 2);
305:       maxY = Math.max(maxY, n.fy + n.height / 2);
306:     });
307: 
308:     // Add padding
309:     const padding = 100;
310:     minX -= padding;
311:     maxX += padding;
312:     minY -= padding;
313:     maxY += padding;
314: 
315:     // Calculate scale and translate to fit the tree
316:     // Constrains to 90% of the available space to maintain a margin
317:     const scale =
318:       Math.min(
319:         width / (maxX - minX),
320:         height / (maxY - minY),
321:         1.0 // Limit max scale
322:       ) * 0.9; // 90% to add some margin
323: 
324:     // Apply zoom transform after a slight delay to let nodes position themselves
325:     setTimeout(() => {
326:       const centerX = (minX + maxX) / 2;
327:       const centerY = (minY + maxY) / 2;
328:       svg
329:         .transition()
330:         .duration(750)
331:         .call(
332:           d3.zoom().transform,
333:           d3.zoomIdentity
334:             .translate(width / 2, height / 2) // Center in viewport
335:             .scale(scale) // Apply calculated scale
336:             .translate(-centerX, -centerY) // Offset to position tree properly
337:         );
338:     }, 500);
339:   }
340: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/renderers/linkRenderer.js

````javascript
 1: // Link Renderer - Renders relationship links between database collections
 2: 
 3: /**
 4:  * Creates visual links representing database relationships between collections
 5:  * @param {Object} g - SVG group for graph visualization
 6:  * @param {Array} links - Array of relationship data (simple_join or cartesian_product)
 7:  * @param {Array} nodes - Array of node objects for looking up source and target
 8:  * @returns {Object} D3 selection of link groups for force simulation updates
 9:  */
10: export function createLinks(g, links, nodes) {
11:   console.log("Creating links:", links.length);
12:   // Process links to ensure source and target are node objects not just IDs
13:   links.forEach((link) => {
14:     // If source or target are string IDs, convert them to node objects
15:     if (typeof link.source === "string") {
16:       link.sourceId = link.source;
17:       link.source = nodes.find((node) => node.id === link.source);
18:     }
19:     if (typeof link.target === "string") {
20:       link.targetId = link.target;
21:       link.target = nodes.find((node) => node.id === link.target);
22:     }
23:   });
24: 
25:   // Create link groups with relationship-specific styling
26:   // Groups contain path, arrowhead, and label for each database relationship
27:   const link = g
28:     .selectAll(".link")
29:     .data(links)
30:     .enter()
31:     .append("g")
32:     .attr("class", (d) => `link-group link-${d.type}`);
33: 
34:   console.log("Created link groups:", link.size());
35: 
36:   // Draw relationship paths with directional arrowheads
37:   link
38:     .append("path")
39:     .attr("class", (d) => `link link-${d.type}`)
40:     .attr(
41:       "marker-end",
42:       (d) =>
43:         `url(#arrowhead-${d.type === "general_join" ? "general_join" : d.type})`
44:     )
45:     .attr("id", (d, i) => `link-${i}`)
46:     .attr("d", (d) => {
47:       // If path data exists, use it, otherwise calculate a default path
48:       if (d.path && d.path.forward) {
49:         return d.path.forward;
50:       }
51: 
52:       // Skip links with missing source or target node
53:       if (!d.source || !d.target) {
54:         console.error("Link missing source or target:", d);
55:         return "M0,0L0,0"; // Empty path
56:       }
57: 
58:       // Default path calculation
59:       const sourceX = d.source.x + d.source.width / 2;
60:       const sourceY = d.source.y + d.source.height / 2;
61:       const targetX = d.target.x + d.target.width / 2;
62:       const targetY = d.target.y + d.target.height / 2;
63:       const path = `M${sourceX},${sourceY}L${targetX},${targetY}`;
64:       console.log("Path:", path);
65:       return path;
66:     });
67: 
68:   // Add relationship labels with proper orientation
69:   link
70:     .append("text")
71:     .attr("class", (d) => `link-label`)
72:     .attr("dy", 20) // Position below the line with positive value
73:     .style("font-size", "16px")
74:     .style("font-weight", "bold")
75:     .style("pointer-events", "none") // Prevent the text from interfering with hover events
76:     .style("paint-order", "stroke") // Draw stroke first, then fill
77:     .style("stroke", "white") // White stroke for background/outline
78:     .style("stroke-width", "3px") // Thickness of background
79:     .style("stroke-linecap", "round") // Round the stroke ends
80:     .style("stroke-linejoin", "round") // Round the stroke corners
81:     .append("textPath")
82:     .attr("xlink:href", (d, i) => `#link-${i}`)
83:     .attr("startOffset", "50%")
84:     .attr("text-anchor", "middle")
85:     .attr("side", "left") // Place text on the left side of the path to flip orientation
86:     .text((d) => {
87:       return d.name;
88:     });
89: 
90:   console.log("Finished creating links");
91:   return link;
92: }
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/meta_visualizer/public/js/graph/renderers/markerRenderer.js
````javascript
 1: // Marker Renderer - Renders arrow markers for links
 2: 
 3: /**
 4:  * Setup arrow markers for different link types
 5:  * @param {Object} svg - The SVG element
 6:  */
 7: export function setupMarkers(svg) {
 8:   // Define arrow markers
 9:   svg
10:     .append("defs")
11:     .selectAll("marker")
12:     .data([
13:       "standard",
14:       "simple_join",
15:       "cartesian_product",
16:       "general_join",
17:       "highlighted",
18:     ])
19:     .enter()
20:     .append("marker")
21:     .attr("id", (d) => `arrowhead-${d}`)
22:     .attr("viewBox", "0 -5 10 10")
23:     .attr("refX", 33)
24:     .attr("refY", 0)
25:     .attr("markerWidth", 10)
26:     .attr("markerHeight", 10)
27:     .attr("orient", "auto")
28:     .append("path")
29:     .attr("d", (d) => getMarkerPath(d))
30:     .attr("class", (d) =>
31:       d === "highlighted"
32:         ? "arrowhead-highlighted"
33:         : d === "general_join"
34:         ? "arrowhead-general_join"
35:         : d === "cartesian_product"
36:         ? "arrowhead-cartesian_product"
37:         : "arrowhead"
38:     );
39: }
40: 
41: /**
42:  * Get the SVG path for a marker based on its type
43:  * @param {string} type - The type of marker
44:  * @returns {string} The SVG path
45:  */
46: function getMarkerPath(type) {
47:   if (type === "simple_join") {
48:     return "M0,-5L10,0L0,5";
49:   } else if (type === "cartesian_product") {
50:     return "M0,-5L10,0L0,5M-2,-3L8,0L-2,3";
51:   } else {
52:     return "M0,-5L10,0L0,5";
53:   }
54: }
````
