````python
 51: 
 52: def decompose_aggregations(node: Aggregate, config: PyDoughConfigs) -> RelationalNode:
 53:     """
 54:     Splits up an aggregate node into an aggregate followed by a projection when
 55:     the aggregate contains 1+ calls to functions that can be split into 1+
 56:     calls to partial aggregates, e.g. how AVG(X) = SUM(X)/COUNT(X).
 57: 
 58:     Args:
 59:         `node`: the aggregate node to be decomposed.
 60:         `config`: the current configuration settings.
 61: 
 62:     Returns:
 63:         The projection node on top of the new aggregate, overall containing the
 64:         equivalent to the original aggregations.
 65:     """
 66:     decomposable: dict[str, CallExpression] = {}
 67:     new_aggregations: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {}
 68:     final_agg_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {}
 69:     # First, separate the aggregations that should be decomposed from those
 70:     # that should not. Place the ones that should in the decomposable dict
 71:     # to deal with later, and place the rest in the new output dictionaries.
 72:     for name, agg in node.aggregations.items():
 73:         if agg.op in decomposable_aggfuncs:
 74:             decomposable[name] = agg
 75:         else:
 76:             new_aggregations[name] = agg
 77:             final_agg_columns[name] = ColumnReference(name, agg.data_type)
 78: 
 79:     # For each decomposable agg call, invoke the procedure to split it into
 80:     # multiple aggregation calls that are placed in `new_aggregations` (without
 81:     # adding any new duplicates), then the logic to combine them with scalar
 82:     # computations in `final_agg_columns`.
 83:     for name, agg in decomposable.items():
 84:         # Decompose the aggregate into its components.
 85:         agg_input: RelationalExpression = agg.inputs[0]
 86:         if agg.op == pydop.AVG:
 87:             # AVG is decomposed into SUM and COUNT, and then the division
 88:             # is done in the projection.
 89:             sum_call: CallExpression = CallExpression(
 90:                 pydop.SUM,
 91:                 agg.data_type,
 92:                 [agg_input],
 93:             )
 94:             count_call: CallExpression = CallExpression(
 95:                 pydop.COUNT,
 96:                 Int64Type(),
 97:                 [agg_input],
 98:             )
 99:             sum_name: str = fetch_or_insert(new_aggregations, sum_call)
100:             count_name: str = fetch_or_insert(new_aggregations, count_call)
101:             avg_call: CallExpression = CallExpression(
102:                 pydop.DIV,
103:                 agg.data_type,
104:                 [
105:                     ColumnReference(sum_name, sum_call.data_type),
106:                     ColumnReference(count_name, count_call.data_type),
107:                 ],
108:             )
109:             # If the config specifies that the default value for AVG should be
110:             # zero, wrap the division in a DEFAULT_TO call.
111:             if config.avg_default_zero:
112:                 avg_call = CallExpression(
113:                     pydop.DEFAULT_TO,
114:                     agg.data_type,
115:                     [avg_call, LiteralExpression(0, Int64Type())],
116:                 )
117:             final_agg_columns[name] = avg_call
118:         else:
119:             raise NotImplementedError(f"Unsupported aggregate function: {agg.op}")
120: 
121:     # Build the new aggregate with the new projection on top of it to derive
122:     # any aggregation calls by combining aggfunc values.
123:     aggs: dict[str, CallExpression] = {}
124:     for name, agg_expr in new_aggregations.items():
125:         assert isinstance(agg_expr, CallExpression)
126:         aggs[name] = agg_expr
127:     new_aggregate: Aggregate = Aggregate(node.input, node.keys, aggs)
128:     project_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {}
129:     for name, expr in node.keys.items():
130:         project_columns[name] = expr
131:     project_columns.update(
132:         {name: final_agg_columns[name] for name in node.aggregations}
133:     )
134:     return Project(new_aggregate, project_columns)

137: def transpose_aggregate_join(
138:     node: Aggregate,
139:     join: Join,
140:     agg_side: int,
141:     side_keys: list[ColumnReference],
142:     config: PyDoughConfigs,
143: ) -> RelationalNode:
144:     """
145:     Transposes the aggregate node above the join into two aggregate nodes,
146:     one above the join and one below the join. Does the transformation
147:     in-place, and either returns the node or a post-processing aggregation
148:     on top of it, then recursively transforms the inputs by passing back to
149:     split_partial_aggregates.
150: 
151:     Args:
152:         `node`: the aggregate node to be split.
153:         `join`: the join node that the aggregate is above.
154:         `agg_side`: the index of the input to the join that the aggregate is
155:         being pushed into.
156:         `side_keys`: the list of equi-join keys from the side of the join
157:         that the aggregate is being pushed into.
158:         `config`: the current configuration settings.
159: 
160:     Returns:
161:         The transformed node. The transformation is also done-in-place.
162:     """
163:     agg_input_name: str | None = join.default_input_aliases[agg_side]
164:     # Keep a dictionary for the projection columns that will be used to post-process
165:     # the output of the aggregates, if needed.
166:     need_projection: bool = False
167:     projection_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {**node.keys}
168:     # Mark columns from the pushdown side of the join to be pruned, except for
169:     # the agg/join keys.
170:     join_columns_to_prune: set[str] = set()
171:     for name, col in join.columns.items():
172:         if (
173:             isinstance(col, ColumnReference)
174:             and (col.input_name == agg_input_name)
175:             and (name not in node.keys)
176:             and (col not in side_keys)
177:         ):
178:             join_columns_to_prune.add(name)
179: 
180:     # Calculate the aggregate terms to go above vs below the join.
181:     agg_input: RelationalNode = join.inputs[agg_side]
182:     top_aggs: dict[str, CallExpression] = {}
183:     input_aggs: dict[str, CallExpression] = {}
184:     for name, agg in node.aggregations.items():
185:         # Pick the name of the aggregate output column that
186:         # does not collide with an existing used name.
187:         bottom_name: str = name
188:         idx: int = 0
189:         while bottom_name in join.columns and bottom_name not in join_columns_to_prune:
190:             bottom_name = f"{name}_{idx}"
191:             idx += 1
192:         # Build the aggregation calls for before/after the join, and place them
193:         # in the dictionaries that will build the new aggregate nodes.
194:         top_aggfunc, bottom_aggfunc = partial_aggregates[agg.op]
195:         top_aggs[name] = CallExpression(
196:             top_aggfunc,
197:             agg.data_type,
198:             [ColumnReference(bottom_name, agg.data_type)],
199:         )
200:         # Insert the column reference for the top-aggfunc into the projection,
201:         # and if needed wrap it in a DEFAULT_TO call for COUNT. This is
202:         # required for left joins, or no-groupby aggregates.
203:         if agg.op == pydop.COUNT and (
204:             join.join_types[0] != JoinType.INNER or len(node.keys) == 0
205:         ):
206:             projection_columns[name] = CallExpression(
207:                 pydop.DEFAULT_TO,
208:                 agg.data_type,
209:                 [
210:                     ColumnReference(name, agg.data_type),
211:                     LiteralExpression(0, Int64Type()),
212:                 ],
213:             )
214:             need_projection = True
215:         else:
216:             projection_columns[name] = ColumnReference(name, agg.data_type)
217:         input_aggs[bottom_name] = CallExpression(
218:             bottom_aggfunc,
219:             agg.data_type,
220:             [transpose_expression(arg, join.columns) for arg in agg.inputs],
221:         )
222:         join_columns_to_prune.discard(bottom_name)
223:         join.columns[bottom_name] = ColumnReference(
224:             bottom_name, agg.data_type, agg_input_name
225:         )
226:     # Remove the columns that are no longer needed from the join.
227:     for name in join_columns_to_prune:
228:         join.columns.pop(name)
229: 
230:     # Derive which columns are used as aggregate keys by
231:     # the input.
232:     input_keys: dict[str, ColumnReference] = {}
233:     for ref in side_keys:
234:         transposed_ref = transpose_expression(ref, join.columns)
235:         assert isinstance(transposed_ref, ColumnReference)
236:         input_keys[transposed_ref.name] = transposed_ref

238:         transposed_agg_key = transpose_expression(
239:             agg_key, join.columns, keep_input_names=True
240:         )
241:         assert isinstance(transposed_agg_key, ColumnReference)
242:         if transposed_agg_key.input_name == agg_input_name:

245:     # Push the bottom-aggregate beneath the join

247:     # Replace the aggregation above the join with the top

249:     node._aggregations = top_aggs
250:     node._columns = {**node.columns, **top_aggs}

252:         return Project(node, projection_columns)
253:     else:
254:         return node

256: 
257: def attempt_join_aggregate_transpose(
258:     node: Aggregate, join: Join, config: PyDoughConfigs
259: ) -> tuple[RelationalNode, bool]:
260:     """
261:     Determine whether the aggregate join transpose operation can occur, and if
262:     so invoke it, otherwise return the top node un-modified.
263: 
264:     Args:
265:         `node`: the aggregate node to be transformed.
266:         `join`: the join node that the aggregate is above.
267:         `config`: the current configuration settings.
268: 
269:     Returns:
270:         A tuple where the first element is the transformed node, and the second
271:         is a boolean indicating whether the output needs to have its inputs
272:         recursively transformed (if False, it means they have already been
273:         recursively transformed).
274:     """
275:     # Verify there are exactly two inputs to the join
276:     if len(join.inputs) != 2:
277:         return node, True
278: 
279:     # Verify all of the aggfuncs are from the functions that can be split.
280:     if not all(
281:         call.op in partial_aggregates or call.op in decomposable_aggfuncs
282:         for call in node.aggregations.values()
283:     ):
284:         return node, True
285: 
286:     # Parse the join condition to identify the lists of equi-join keys
287:     # from the LHS and RHS, and verify that all of the columns used by
288:     # the condition are in those lists.
289:     lhs_keys, rhs_keys = extract_equijoin_keys(join)
290:     finder: ColumnReferenceFinder = ColumnReferenceFinder()
291:     for cond in join.conditions:
292:         cond.accept(finder)
293:     condition_cols: set[ColumnReference] = finder.get_column_references()
294:     if not all(col in lhs_keys or col in rhs_keys for col in condition_cols):
295:         return node, True
296: 
297:     # Identify which side of the join the aggfuncs refer to, and
298:     # make sure it is an INNER (+ there is only one side).
299:     finder.reset()
300:     for agg_call in node.aggregations.values():
301:         transpose_expression(agg_call, join.columns, True).accept(finder)
302:     agg_input_names: set[str | None] = {
303:         ref.input_name for ref in finder.get_column_references()
304:     }
305:     if len(agg_input_names) != 1:
306:         return node, True
307: 
308:     agg_input_name: str | None = agg_input_names.pop()
309:     agg_side: int = 0 if agg_input_name == join.default_input_aliases[0] else 1
310:     side_keys: list[ColumnReference] = (lhs_keys, rhs_keys)[agg_side]
311:     # Make sure the aggregate is being pushed into an INNER side.
312:     if agg_side == 1 and join.join_types[0] != JoinType.INNER:
313:         return node, True
314: 
315:     # If there are any AVG calls, rewrite the aggregate into
316:     # a call with SUM and COUNT derived, with a projection
317:     # dividing the two, then repeat the process.
318:     if any(call.op in decomposable_aggfuncs for call in node.aggregations.values()):
319:         return split_partial_aggregates(
320:             decompose_aggregations(node, config), config
321:         ), False
322: 
323:     # Otherwise, invoke the transposition procedure.
324:     return transpose_aggregate_join(node, join, agg_side, side_keys, config), True
325: 
326: 
327: def split_partial_aggregates(
328:     node: RelationalNode, config: PyDoughConfigs
329: ) -> RelationalNode:
330:     """
331:     Splits partial aggregates above joins into two aggregates, one above the
332:     join and one below the join, from the entire relational plan rooted at the
333:     current node.
334: 
335:     Args:
336:         `node`: the root node of the relational plan to be transformed.
337:         `config`: the current configuration settings.
338: 
339:     Returns:
340:         The transformed node. The transformation is also done-in-place.
341:     """
342:     # If the aggregate+join pattern is detected, attempt to do the transpose.
343:     handle_inputs: bool = True
344:     if isinstance(node, Aggregate) and isinstance(node.input, Join):
345:         node, handle_inputs = attempt_join_aggregate_transpose(node, node.input, config)
346: 
347:     # If needed, recursively invoke the procedure on all inputs to the node.
348:     if handle_inputs:
349:         node = node.copy(
350:             inputs=[split_partial_aggregates(input, config) for input in node.inputs]
351:         )
352:     return node
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/conversion/filter_pushdown.py
````python
  1: """
  2: Logic used to transpose filters lower into relational trees.
  3: """
  4: 
  5: __all__ = ["push_filters"]
  6: 
  7: 
  8: from pydough.relational import (
  9:     Aggregate,
 10:     ColumnReference,
 11:     EmptySingleton,
 12:     Filter,
 13:     Join,
 14:     JoinType,
 15:     Limit,
 16:     Project,
 17:     RelationalExpression,
 18:     RelationalNode,
 19:     Scan,
 20: )
 21: from pydough.relational.rel_util import (
 22:     build_filter,
 23:     contains_window,
 24:     false_when_null_columns,
 25:     get_conjunctions,
 26:     only_references_columns,
 27:     partition_expressions,
 28:     transpose_expression,
 29: )
 30: 
 31: 
 32: def push_filters(
 33:     node: RelationalNode, filters: set[RelationalExpression]
 34: ) -> RelationalNode:
 35:     """
 36:     Transpose filter conditions down as far as possible.
 37: 
 38:     Args:
 39:         `node`: The current node of the relational tree.
 40:         `filters`: The set of filter conditions to push down representing
 41:         predicates from ancestor nodes that can be pushed this far down.
 42: 
 43:     Returns:
 44:         The transformed version of `node` with the conditions of `filters`
 45:         pushed down as far as possible, either materializing them above the
 46:         node or into one of its inputs, or possibly both if there are multiple
 47:         filters.
 48:     """
 49:     remaining_filters: set[RelationalExpression]
 50:     pushable_filters: set[RelationalExpression]
 51:     match node:
 52:         case Filter():
 53:             # Add all of the conditions from the filters pushed down this far
 54:             # with the filters from the current node. If there is a window
 55:             # function, materialize all of them at this point, otherwise push
 56:             # all of them further.
 57:             filters.update(get_conjunctions(node.condition))
 58:             if contains_window(node.condition):
 59:                 return build_filter(push_filters(node.input, set()), filters)
 60:             else:
 61:                 return push_filters(node.input, filters)
 62:         case Project():
 63:             if any(contains_window(expr) for expr in node.columns.values()):
 64:                 # If there is a window function, materialize all filters at
 65:                 # this point.
 66:                 pushable_filters, remaining_filters = set(), filters
 67:             else:
 68:                 # Otherwise push all filters that only depend on columns in
 69:                 # the project that are pass-through of another column.
 70:                 # For example consider the following:
 71:                 # `filters`: `{a > 0, b > 0, a > b}`
 72:                 # `node`: `Project(columns={"a": "x", "b": "LENGTH(y)"})`
 73:                 # Then the only filter that can be pushed down is `a > 0`,
 74:                 # which becomes `x > 0`.
 75:                 allowed_cols: set[str] = set()
 76:                 for name, expr in node.columns.items():
 77:                     if isinstance(expr, ColumnReference):
 78:                         allowed_cols.add(name)
 79:                 pushable_filters, remaining_filters = partition_expressions(
 80:                     filters,
 81:                     lambda expr: only_references_columns(expr, allowed_cols),
 82:                 )
 83:                 pushable_filters = {
 84:                     transpose_expression(expr, node.columns)
 85:                     for expr in pushable_filters
 86:                 }
 87:             node._input = push_filters(node.input, pushable_filters)
 88:             return build_filter(node, remaining_filters)
 89:         case Join():
 90:             remaining_filters = filters
 91:             input_cols: list[set[str]] = [set() for _ in range(len(node.inputs))]
 92:             for name, expr in node.columns.items():
 93:                 if not isinstance(expr, ColumnReference):
 94:                     continue
 95:                 input_name: str | None = expr.input_name
 96:                 input_idx = node.default_input_aliases.index(input_name)
 97:                 input_cols[input_idx].add(name)
 98:             # For each input to the join, push down any filters that only
 99:             # reference columns from that input.
100:             for idx, child in enumerate(node.inputs):
101:                 if idx > 0 and node.join_types[idx - 1] == JoinType.LEFT:
102:                     # If doing a left join, only push filters if they depend
103:                     # on the input and are false if the input is null. If this
104:                     # happens, the left join becomes an inner join.
105:                     pushable_filters, remaining_filters = partition_expressions(
106:                         remaining_filters,
107:                         lambda expr: only_references_columns(expr, input_cols[idx])
108:                         and false_when_null_columns(expr, input_cols[idx]),
109:                     )
110:                     if pushable_filters:
111:                         node.join_types[idx - 1] = JoinType.INNER
112:                 else:
113:                     pushable_filters, remaining_filters = partition_expressions(
114:                         remaining_filters,
115:                         lambda expr: only_references_columns(expr, input_cols[idx]),
116:                     )
117:                 pushable_filters = {
118:                     transpose_expression(expr, node.columns)
119:                     for expr in pushable_filters
120:                 }
121:                 node.inputs[idx] = push_filters(child, pushable_filters)
122:             # Materialize all of the remaining filters.
123:             return build_filter(node, remaining_filters)
124:         case Aggregate():
125:             # Only push filters that only depend on the key columns of the
126:             # aggregate, since they will delete entire groups.
127:             pushable_filters, remaining_filters = partition_expressions(
128:                 filters,
129:                 lambda expr: only_references_columns(expr, set(node.keys)),
130:             )
131:             pushable_filters = {
132:                 transpose_expression(expr, node.columns) for expr in pushable_filters
133:             }
134:             node._input = push_filters(node.input, pushable_filters)
135:             # Materialize all of the remaining filters.
136:             return build_filter(node, remaining_filters)
137:         case Limit():
138:             # Materialize all of the remaining filters since a filter cannot
139:             # be transposed beneath a limit without changing its output.
140:             node._input = push_filters(node.input, set())
141:             return build_filter(node, filters)
142:         case EmptySingleton() | Scan():
143:             # For remaining nodes, materialize all of the remaining filters.
144:             return build_filter(node, filters)
145:         case _:
146:             raise NotImplementedError(
147:                 f"push_filters not implemented for {node.__class__.__name__}"
148:             )
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/conversion/hybrid_decorrelater.py
````python
  1: """
  2: Logic for applying de-correlation to hybrid trees before relational conversion
  3: if the correlate is not a semi/anti join.
  4: """
  5: 
  6: __all__ = ["run_hybrid_decorrelation"]
  7: 
  8: 
  9: import copy
 10: 
 11: from .hybrid_tree import (
 12:     ConnectionType,
 13:     HybridBackRefExpr,
 14:     HybridCalculate,
 15:     HybridChildPullUp,
 16:     HybridChildRefExpr,
 17:     HybridColumnExpr,
 18:     HybridConnection,
 19:     HybridCorrelExpr,
 20:     HybridExpr,
 21:     HybridFilter,
 22:     HybridFunctionExpr,
 23:     HybridLiteralExpr,
 24:     HybridNoop,
 25:     HybridPartition,
 26:     HybridRefExpr,
 27:     HybridTree,
 28:     HybridWindowExpr,
 29: )
 30: 
 31: 
 32: class Decorrelater:
 33:     """
 34:     Class that encapsulates the logic used for de-correlation of hybrid trees.
 35:     """
 36: 
 37:     def make_decorrelate_parent(
 38:         self, hybrid: HybridTree, child_idx: int, required_steps: int
 39:     ) -> tuple[HybridTree, int]:
 40:         """
 41:         Creates a snapshot of the ancestry of the hybrid tree that contains
 42:         a correlated child, without any of its children, its descendants, or
 43:         any pipeline operators that do not need to be there.
 44: 
 45:         Args:
 46:             `hybrid`: The hybrid tree to create a snapshot of in order to aid
 47:             in the de-correlation of a correlated child.
 48:             `child_idx`: The index of the correlated child of hybrid that the
 49:             snapshot is being created to aid in the de-correlation of.
 50:             `required_steps`: The index of the last pipeline operator that
 51:             needs to be included in the snapshot in order for the child to be
 52:             derivable.
 53: 
 54:         Returns:
 55:             A tuple where the first entry is a snapshot of `hybrid` and its
 56:             ancestry in the hybrid tree, without without any of its children or
 57:             pipeline operators that occur during or after the derivation of the
 58:             correlated child, or without any of its descendants. The second
 59:             entry is the number of ancestor layers that should be skipped due
 60:             to the PARTITION edge case.
 61:         """
 62:         if isinstance(hybrid.pipeline[0], HybridPartition) and child_idx == 0:
 63:             # Special case: if the correlated child is the data argument of a
 64:             # partition operation, then the parent to snapshot is actually the
 65:             # parent of the level containing the partition operation. In this
 66:             # case, all of the parent's children & pipeline operators should be
 67:             # included in the snapshot.
 68:             if hybrid.parent is None:
 69:                 raise ValueError(
 70:                     "Malformed hybrid tree: partition data input to a partition node cannot contain a correlated reference to the partition node."
 71:                 )
 72:             result = self.make_decorrelate_parent(
 73:                 hybrid.parent, len(hybrid.parent.children), len(hybrid.pipeline)
 74:             )
 75:             return result[0], result[1] + 1
 76:         # Temporarily detach the successor of the current level, then create a
 77:         # deep copy of the current level (which will include its ancestors),
 78:         # then reattach the successor back to the original. This ensures that
 79:         # the descendants of the current level are not included when providing
 80:         # the parent to the correlated child as its new ancestor.
 81:         successor: HybridTree | None = hybrid.successor
 82:         hybrid._successor = None
 83:         new_hybrid: HybridTree = copy.deepcopy(hybrid)
 84:         hybrid._successor = successor
 85:         # Ensure the new parent only includes the children & pipeline operators
 86:         # that is has to.
 87:         new_hybrid._children = new_hybrid._children[:child_idx]
 88:         new_hybrid._pipeline = new_hybrid._pipeline[: required_steps + 1]
 89:         return new_hybrid, 0
 90: 
 91:     def remove_correl_refs(
 92:         self, expr: HybridExpr, parent: HybridTree, child_height: int
 93:     ) -> HybridExpr:
 94:         """
 95:         Recursively & destructively removes correlated references within a
 96:         hybrid expression if they point to a specific correlated ancestor
 97:         hybrid tree, and replaces them with corresponding BACK references.
 98: 
 99:         Args:
100:             `expr`: The hybrid expression to remove correlated references from.
101:             `parent`: The correlated ancestor hybrid tree that the correlated
102:             references should point to when they are targeted for removal.
103:             `child_height`: The height of the correlated child within the
104:             hybrid tree that the correlated references is point to. This is
105:             the number of BACK indices to shift by when replacing the
106:             correlated reference with a BACK reference.
107: 
108:         Returns:
109:             The hybrid expression with all correlated references to `parent`
110:             replaced with corresponding BACK references. The replacement also
111:             happens in-place.
112:         """
113:         match expr:
114:             case HybridCorrelExpr():
115:                 # If the correlated reference points to the parent, then
116:                 # replace it with a BACK reference. Otherwise, recursively
117:                 # transform its input expression in case it contains another
118:                 # correlated reference.
119:                 if expr.hybrid is parent:
120:                     result: HybridExpr | None = expr.expr.shift_back(child_height)
121:                     assert result is not None
122:                     return result
123:                 else:
124:                     expr.expr = self.remove_correl_refs(expr.expr, parent, child_height)
125:                     return expr
126:             case HybridFunctionExpr():
127:                 # For regular functions, recursively transform all of their
128:                 # arguments.
129:                 for idx, arg in enumerate(expr.args):
130:                     expr.args[idx] = self.remove_correl_refs(arg, parent, child_height)
131:                 return expr
132:             case HybridWindowExpr():
133:                 # For window functions, recursively transform all of their
134:                 # arguments, partition keys, and order keys.
135:                 for idx, arg in enumerate(expr.args):
136:                     expr.args[idx] = self.remove_correl_refs(arg, parent, child_height)
137:                 for idx, arg in enumerate(expr.partition_args):
138:                     expr.partition_args[idx] = self.remove_correl_refs(
139:                         arg, parent, child_height
140:                     )
141:                 for order_arg in expr.order_args:
142:                     order_arg.expr = self.remove_correl_refs(
143:                         order_arg.expr, parent, child_height
144:                     )
145:                 return expr
146:             case (
147:                 HybridBackRefExpr()
148:                 | HybridRefExpr()
149:                 | HybridChildRefExpr()
150:                 | HybridLiteralExpr()
151:                 | HybridColumnExpr()
152:             ):
153:                 # All other expression types do not require any transformation
154:                 # to de-correlate since they cannot contain correlations.
155:                 return expr
156:             case _:
157:                 raise NotImplementedError(
158:                     f"Unsupported expression type: {expr.__class__.__name__}."
159:                 )
160: 
161:     def correl_ref_purge(
162:         self,
163:         level: HybridTree | None,
164:         old_parent: HybridTree,
165:         new_parent: HybridTree,
166:         child_height: int,
167:     ) -> None:
168:         """
169:         The recursive procedure to remove correlated references from the
170:         expressions of a hybrid tree or any of its ancestors or children if
171:         they refer to a specific correlated ancestor that is being removed.
172: 
173:         Args:
174:             `level`: The current level of the hybrid tree to remove correlated
175:             references from.
176:             `old_parent`: The correlated ancestor hybrid tree that the correlated
177:             references should point to when they are targeted for removal.
178:             `new_parent`: The ancestor of `level` that removal should stop at
179:             because it is the transposed snapshot of `old_parent`, and
180:             therefore it & its ancestors cannot contain any more correlated
181:             references that would be targeted for removal.
182:             `child_height`: The height of the correlated child within the
183:             hybrid tree that the correlated references is point to. This is
184:             the number of BACK indices to shift by when replacing the
185:             correlated reference with a BACK
186:         """
187:         while level is not None and level is not new_parent:
188:             # First, recursively remove any targeted correlated references from
189:             # the children of the current level.
190:             for child in level.children:
191:                 self.correl_ref_purge(
192:                     child.subtree, old_parent, new_parent, child_height
193:                 )
194:             # Then, remove any correlated references from the pipeline
195:             # operators of the current level. Usually this just means
196:             # transforming the terms/orderings/unique keys of the operation,
197:             # but specific operation types will require special casing if they
198:             # have additional expressions stored in other field that need to be
199:             # transformed.
200:             for operation in level.pipeline:
201:                 for name, expr in operation.terms.items():
202:                     operation.terms[name] = self.remove_correl_refs(
203:                         expr, old_parent, child_height
204:                     )
205:                 for ordering in operation.orderings:
206:                     ordering.expr = self.remove_correl_refs(
207:                         ordering.expr, old_parent, child_height
208:                     )
209:                 for idx, expr in enumerate(operation.unique_exprs):
210:                     operation.unique_exprs[idx] = self.remove_correl_refs(
211:                         expr, old_parent, child_height
212:                     )
213:                 if isinstance(operation, HybridCalculate):
214:                     for str, expr in operation.new_expressions.items():
215:                         operation.new_expressions[str] = self.remove_correl_refs(
216:                             expr, old_parent, child_height
217:                         )
218:                 if isinstance(operation, HybridFilter):
219:                     operation.condition = self.remove_correl_refs(
220:                         operation.condition, old_parent, child_height
221:                     )
222:             # Repeat the process on the ancestor until either loop guard
223:             # condition is no longer True.
224:             level = level.parent
225:             child_height -= 1
226: 
227:     def decorrelate_child(
228:         self,
229:         old_parent: HybridTree,
230:         child_idx: int,
231:         new_parent: HybridTree,
232:         skipped_levels: int,
233:     ) -> int:
234:         """
235:         Runs the logic to de-correlate a child of a hybrid tree that contains
236:         a correlated reference. This involves linking the child to a new parent
237:         as its ancestor, the parent being a snapshot of the original hybrid
238:         tree that contained the correlated child as a child. The transformed
239:         child can now replace correlated references with BACK references that
240:         point to terms in its newly expanded ancestry, and the original hybrid
241:         tree can now join onto this child using its uniqueness keys.
242: 
243:         Args:
244:             `old_parent`: The correlated ancestor hybrid tree that the correlated
245:             references should point to when they are targeted for removal.
246:             `child_idx`: Which child of the hybrid tree the child is.
247:             `new_parent`: The ancestor of `level` that removal should stop at.
248:             `skipped_levels`: The number of ancestor layers that should be
249:             ignored when deriving backshifts of join/agg keys.
250: 
251:         Returns:
252:             The index of the child that was de-correlated, which is usually
253:             the same as `child_idx` but could have been shifted.
254:         """
255:         # First, find the height of the child subtree & its top-most level.
256:         child: HybridConnection = old_parent.children[child_idx]
257:         child_root: HybridTree = child.subtree
258:         child_height: int = 1
259:         while child_root.parent is not None:
260:             child_height += 1
261:             child_root = child_root.parent
262:         # Link the top level of the child subtree to the new parent.
263:         new_parent.add_successor(child_root)
264:         # Replace any correlated references to the original parent with BACK references.
265:         self.correl_ref_purge(child.subtree, old_parent, new_parent, child_height)
266:         # Update the join keys to join on the unique keys of all the ancestors.
267:         new_join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] = []
268:         additional_levels: int = 0
269:         current_level: HybridTree | None = old_parent
270:         new_agg_keys: list[HybridExpr] = []
271:         while current_level is not None:
272:             skip_join: bool = (
273:                 isinstance(current_level.pipeline[0], HybridPartition)
274:                 and child is current_level.children[0]
275:             )
276:             for unique_key in sorted(current_level.pipeline[-1].unique_exprs, key=str):
277:                 lhs_key: HybridExpr | None = unique_key.shift_back(additional_levels)
278:                 rhs_key: HybridExpr | None = unique_key.shift_back(
279:                     additional_levels + child_height - skipped_levels
280:                 )
281:                 assert lhs_key is not None and rhs_key is not None
282:                 if not skip_join:
283:                     new_join_keys.append((lhs_key, rhs_key))
284:                 new_agg_keys.append(rhs_key)
285:             current_level = current_level.parent
286:             additional_levels += 1
287:         child.subtree.join_keys = new_join_keys
288:         child.subtree.general_join_condition = None
289:         # If aggregating, update the aggregation keys accordingly.
290:         if child.connection_type.is_aggregation:
291:             child.subtree.agg_keys = new_agg_keys
292:         # If the child is such that we don't need to keep rows from the parent
293:         # without a match, replace the parent & its ancestors with a
294:         # HybridPullUp node (and replace any other deleted nodes with no-ops).
295:         # This is done in-place, but only if the child is the first child of
296:         # the parent.
297:         if child.connection_type.is_semi and child_idx == min(
298:             old_parent.correlated_children
299:         ):
300:             old_parent._parent = None
301:             old_parent.pipeline[0] = HybridChildPullUp(
302:                 old_parent, child_idx, child_height
303:             )
304:             for i in range(1, child.required_steps + 1):
305:                 old_parent.pipeline[i] = HybridNoop(old_parent.pipeline[i - 1])
306:             child_idx = self.remove_dead_children(old_parent, child_idx)
307:         return child_idx
308: 
309:     def identify_children_used(
310:         self, expr: HybridExpr, unused_children: set[int]
311:     ) -> None:
312:         """
313:         Find all child indices used in an expression and remove them from
314:         a set of indices.
315: 
316:         Args:
317:             `expr`: the expression being checked for child reference indices.
318:             `unused_children`: the set of all children that are unused. This
319:             starts out as the set of all children, and whenever a child
320:             reference is found within `expr`, it is removed from the set.
321:         """
322:         match expr:
323:             case HybridChildRefExpr():
324:                 unused_children.discard(expr.child_idx)
325:             case HybridFunctionExpr():
326:                 for arg in expr.args:
327:                     self.identify_children_used(arg, unused_children)
328:             case HybridWindowExpr():
329:                 for arg in expr.args:
330:                     self.identify_children_used(arg, unused_children)
331:                 for part_arg in expr.partition_args:
332:                     self.identify_children_used(part_arg, unused_children)
333:                 for order_arg in expr.order_args:
334:                     self.identify_children_used(order_arg.expr, unused_children)
335:             case HybridCorrelExpr():
336:                 self.identify_children_used(expr.expr, unused_children)
337: 
338:     def renumber_children_indices(
339:         self, expr: HybridExpr, child_remapping: dict[int, int]
340:     ) -> None:
341:         """
342:         Replaces all child reference indices in a hybrid expression in-place
343:         when the children list was shifted, therefore the index-to-child
344:         correspondence must be re-numbered.
345: 
346:         Args:
347:             `expr`: the expression having its child references modified.
348:             `child_remapping`: the mapping of old->new indices for child
349:             references.
350:         """
351:         match expr:
352:             case HybridChildRefExpr():
353:                 assert expr.child_idx in child_remapping
354:                 expr.child_idx = child_remapping[expr.child_idx]
355:             case HybridFunctionExpr():
356:                 for arg in expr.args:
357:                     self.renumber_children_indices(arg, child_remapping)
358:             case HybridWindowExpr():
359:                 for arg in expr.args:
360:                     self.renumber_children_indices(arg, child_remapping)
361:                 for part_arg in expr.partition_args:
362:                     self.renumber_children_indices(part_arg, child_remapping)
363:                 for order_arg in expr.order_args:
364:                     self.renumber_children_indices(order_arg.expr, child_remapping)
365:             case HybridCorrelExpr():
366:                 self.renumber_children_indices(expr.expr, child_remapping)
367: 
368:     def remove_dead_children(self, hybrid: HybridTree, pullup_child_idx: int) -> int:
369:         """
370:         Deletes any children of a hybrid tree that are no longer referenced
371:         after de-correlation.
372: 
373:         Args:
374:             `hybrid`: The hybrid tree to remove unused children from.
375:             `pullup_child_idx`: The index of the child that became a pull-up
376:             node causing the removal.
377: 
378:         Returns:
379:             The index of the child that the pullup operation corresponds to.
380:         """
381:         # Identify which children are no longer used
382:         children_to_delete: set[int] = set(range(len(hybrid.children)))
383:         for operation in hybrid.pipeline:
384:             match operation:
385:                 case HybridChildPullUp():
386:                     children_to_delete.discard(operation.child_idx)
387:                 case HybridFilter():
388:                     self.identify_children_used(operation.condition, children_to_delete)
389:                 case HybridCalculate():
390:                     for term in operation.new_expressions.values():
391:                         self.identify_children_used(term, children_to_delete)
392:                 case _:
393:                     for term in operation.terms.values():
394:                         self.identify_children_used(term, children_to_delete)
395:         if len(children_to_delete) == 0:
396:             return pullup_child_idx
397:         # Build a renumbering of the remaining children
398:         child_remapping: dict[int, int] = {}
399:         for i in range(len(hybrid.children)):
400:             if i not in children_to_delete:
401:                 child_remapping[i] = len(child_remapping)
402:         # Remove all the unused children (starting from the end)
403:         for child_idx in sorted(children_to_delete, reverse=True):
404:             hybrid.children.pop(child_idx)
405:         for operation in hybrid.pipeline:
406:             match operation:
407:                 case HybridChildPullUp():
408:                     operation.child_idx = child_remapping[operation.child_idx]
409:                 case HybridFilter():
410:                     self.renumber_children_indices(operation.condition, child_remapping)
411:                 case HybridCalculate():
412:                     for term in operation.new_expressions.values():
413:                         self.renumber_children_indices(term, child_remapping)
414:                 case _:
415:                     continue
416:         # Renumber the correlated children
417:         new_correlated_children: set[int] = set()
418:         for correlated_idx in hybrid.correlated_children:
419:             if correlated_idx in child_remapping:
420:                 new_correlated_children.add(child_remapping[correlated_idx])
421:         hybrid._correlated_children = new_correlated_children
422: 
423:         return child_remapping[pullup_child_idx]
424: 
425:     def decorrelate_hybrid_tree(self, hybrid: HybridTree) -> HybridTree:
426:         """
427:         The recursive procedure to remove unwanted correlated references from
428:         the entire hybrid tree, called from the bottom and working upwards
429:         to the top layer, and having each layer also de-correlate its children.
430: 
431:         Args:
432:             `hybrid`: The hybrid tree to remove correlated references from.
433: 
434:         Returns:
435:             The hybrid tree with all invalid correlated references removed as the
436:             tree structure is re-written to allow them to be replaced with BACK
437:             references. The transformation is also done in-place.
438:         """
439:         # Recursively decorrelate the ancestors of the current level of the
440:         # hybrid tree.
441:         if hybrid.parent is not None:
442:             hybrid._parent = self.decorrelate_hybrid_tree(hybrid.parent)
443:             hybrid._parent._successor = hybrid
444:         # Iterate across all the children, identify any that are correlated,
445:         # and transform any of the correlated ones that require decorrelation
446:         # due to the type of connection.
447:         child_idx: int = len(hybrid.children) - 1
448:         original_parent: HybridTree
449:         if len(hybrid.correlated_children) > 0:
450:             original_parent = copy.deepcopy(hybrid)
451:         while child_idx >= 0:
452:             child = hybrid.children[child_idx]
453:             if child_idx not in hybrid.correlated_children:
454:                 child_idx -= 1
455:                 continue
456:             match child.connection_type:
457:                 case (
458:                     ConnectionType.SINGULAR
459:                     | ConnectionType.SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH
460:                     | ConnectionType.AGGREGATION
461:                     | ConnectionType.AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH
462:                 ):
463:                     new_parent, skipped_levels = self.make_decorrelate_parent(
464:                         original_parent,
465:                         child_idx,
466:                         hybrid.children[child_idx].required_steps,
467:                     )
468:                     child_idx = self.decorrelate_child(
469:                         hybrid,
470:                         child_idx,
471:                         new_parent,
472:                         skipped_levels,
473:                     )
474:                 case ConnectionType.NDISTINCT | ConnectionType.NDISTINCT_ONLY_MATCH:
475:                     raise NotImplementedError(
476:                         f"PyDough does not yet support correlated references with the {child.connection_type.name} pattern."
477:                     )
478:                 case (
479:                     ConnectionType.SEMI
480:                     | ConnectionType.ANTI
481:                     | ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_SINGULAR
482:                     | ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION
483:                     | ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_NDISTINCT
484:                 ):
485:                     # These patterns do not require decorrelation since they
486:                     # are supported via correlated SEMI/ANTI joins.
487:                     pass
488:             child_idx -= 1
489:         # Iterate across all the children and recursively decorrelate them.
490:         for child in hybrid.children:
491:             child.subtree = self.decorrelate_hybrid_tree(child.subtree)
492:         return hybrid
493: 
494: 
495: def run_hybrid_decorrelation(hybrid: HybridTree) -> HybridTree:
496:     """
497:     Invokes the procedure to remove correlated references from a hybrid tree
498:     before relational conversion if those correlated references are invalid
499:     (e.g. not from a semi/anti join).
500: 
501:     Args:
502:         `hybrid`: The hybrid tree to remove correlated references from.
503: 
504:     Returns:
505:         The hybrid tree with all invalid correlated references removed as the
506:         tree structure is re-written to allow them to be replaced with BACK
507:         references. The transformation is also done in-place.
508:     """
509:     decorr: Decorrelater = Decorrelater()
510:     return decorr.decorrelate_hybrid_tree(hybrid)
````

````python
 347: class HybridWindowExpr(HybridExpr):
 348:     """
 349:     Class for HybridExpr terms that are window function calls.
 350:     """
 351: 
 352:     def __init__(
 353:         self,
 354:         window_func: pydop.ExpressionWindowOperator,
 355:         args: list[HybridExpr],
 356:         partition_args: list[HybridExpr],
 357:         order_args: list[HybridCollation],
 358:         typ: PyDoughType,
 359:         kwargs: dict[str, object],
 360:     ):
 361:         super().__init__(typ)
 362:         self.window_func: pydop.ExpressionWindowOperator = window_func
 363:         self.args: list[HybridExpr] = args
 364:         self.partition_args: list[HybridExpr] = partition_args
 365:         self.order_args: list[HybridCollation] = order_args
 366:         self.kwargs: dict[str, object] = kwargs
 367: 
 368:     def __repr__(self):
 369:         args_str = ""
 370:         args_str += f"by=[{', '.join([str(arg) for arg in self.args])}]"
 371:         args_str += (
 372:             f", partition=[{', '.join([str(arg) for arg in self.partition_args])}]"
 373:         )
 374:         args_str += f", order=[{', '.join([str(arg) for arg in self.order_args])}]"
 375:         if "allow_ties" in self.kwargs:
 376:             args_str += f", allow_ties={self.kwargs['allow_ties']}"
 377:             if "dense" in self.kwargs:
 378:                 args_str += f", dense={self.kwargs['dense']}"
 379:         return f"{self.window_func.function_name}({args_str})"
 380: 
 381:     def apply_renamings(self, renamings: dict[str, str]) -> "HybridExpr":
 382:         renamed_args: list[HybridExpr] = [
 383:             arg.apply_renamings(renamings) for arg in self.args
 384:         ]
 385:         renamed_partition_args: list[HybridExpr] = [
 386:             arg.apply_renamings(renamings) for arg in self.partition_args
 387:         ]
 388:         renamed_order_args: list[HybridCollation] = []
 389:         for col_arg in self.order_args:
 390:             collation_expr: HybridExpr = col_arg.expr
 391:             renamed_expr: HybridExpr = collation_expr.apply_renamings(renamings)
 392:             if renamed_expr is collation_expr:
 393:                 renamed_order_args.append(col_arg)
 394:             else:
 395:                 renamed_order_args.append(
 396:                     HybridCollation(renamed_expr, col_arg.asc, col_arg.na_first)
 397:                 )
 398:         if (
 399:             all_same(self.args, renamed_args)
 400:             and all_same(self.partition_args, renamed_partition_args)
 401:             and all_same(
 402:                 [arg.expr for arg in self.order_args],
 403:                 [arg.expr for arg in renamed_order_args],
 404:             )
 405:         ):
 406:             return self
 407:         return HybridWindowExpr(
 408:             self.window_func,
 409:             renamed_args,
 410:             renamed_partition_args,
 411:             renamed_order_args,
 412:             self.typ,
 413:             self.kwargs,
 414:         )
 415: 
 416:     def shift_back(self, levels: int) -> HybridExpr | None:
 417:         # Shift all of the inputs to the window function (including regular,
 418:         # partition, and order inputs). Return None if any of them cannot
 419:         # be shifted.
 420:         shifted_args: list[HybridExpr] = []
 421:         shifted_partition_args: list[HybridExpr] = []
 422:         shifted_order_args: list[HybridCollation] = []
 423:         shifted_arg: HybridExpr | None
 424:         for arg in self.args:
 425:             shifted_arg = arg.shift_back(levels)
 426:             if shifted_arg is None:
 427:                 return None
 428:             shifted_args.append(shifted_arg)
 429:         for arg in self.partition_args:
 430:             shifted_arg = arg.shift_back(levels)
 431:             if shifted_arg is None:
 432:                 return None
 433:             shifted_partition_args.append(shifted_arg)
 434:         for order_arg in self.order_args:
 435:             shifted_arg = order_arg.expr.shift_back(levels)
 436:             if shifted_arg is None:
 437:                 return None
 438:             shifted_order_args.append(
 439:                 HybridCollation(shifted_arg, order_arg.asc, order_arg.na_first)
 440:             )
 441:         return HybridWindowExpr(
 442:             self.window_func,
 443:             shifted_args,
 444:             shifted_partition_args,
 445:             shifted_order_args,
 446:             self.typ,
 447:             self.kwargs,
 448:         )
 449: 
 450: 
 451: def all_same(exprs: list[HybridExpr], renamed_exprs: list[HybridExpr]) -> bool:
 452:     """
 453:     Returns whether two lists of hybrid expressions are identical, down to
 454:     identity.
 455:     """
 456:     return len(exprs) == len(renamed_exprs) and all(
 457:         expr is renamed_expr for expr, renamed_expr in zip(exprs, renamed_exprs)
 458:     )
 459: 
 460: 
 461: def shift_join_condition(expr: HybridExpr) -> HybridExpr:
 462:     """
 463:     Shifts an expression used as a general join condition back 1 level, where
 464:     expressions inside of function calls are also shifted, but expressions
 465:     inside correlated references are left alone since they refer to the parent.
 466:     """
 467:     match expr:
 468:         case HybridRefExpr() | HybridBackRefExpr():
 469:             return expr.shift_back(1)
 470:         case HybridFunctionExpr():
 471:             return HybridFunctionExpr(
 472:                 expr.operator,
 473:                 [shift_join_condition(arg) for arg in expr.args],
 474:                 expr.typ,
 475:             )
 476:         case HybridWindowExpr():
 477:             return HybridWindowExpr(
 478:                 expr.window_func,
 479:                 [shift_join_condition(arg) for arg in expr.args],
 480:                 [shift_join_condition(arg) for arg in expr.partition_args],
 481:                 [
 482:                     HybridCollation(
 483:                         shift_join_condition(order_arg.expr),
 484:                         order_arg.asc,
 485:                         order_arg.na_first,
 486:                     )
 487:                     for order_arg in expr.order_args
 488:                 ],
 489:                 expr.typ,
 490:                 expr.kwargs,
 491:             )
 492:         case _:
 493:             return expr

 496: class HybridOperation:
 497:     """
 498:     Base class for an operation done within a pipeline of a HybridTree, such
 499:     as a filter or table collection access. Every such class contains the
 500:     following:
 501:     - `terms`: mapping of names to expressions accessible from that point in
 502:                the pipeline execution.
 503:     - `renamings`: mapping of names to a new name that should be used to access
 504:                them from within `terms`. This is used when a `CALCULATE`
 505:                overrides a term name so that future invocations of the term
 506:                name use the renamed version, while key operations like joins
 507:                can still access the original version.
 508:     - `orderings`: list of collation expressions that specify the order
 509:                that a hybrid operation is sorted by.
 510:     - `unique_exprs`: list of expressions that are used to uniquely identify
 511:                records within the current level of the hybrid tree.
 512:     """
 513: 
 514:     def __init__(
 515:         self,
 516:         terms: dict[str, HybridExpr],
 517:         renamings: dict[str, str],
 518:         orderings: list[HybridCollation],
 519:         unique_exprs: list[HybridExpr],
 520:     ):
 521:         self.terms: dict[str, HybridExpr] = terms
 522:         self.renamings: dict[str, str] = renamings
 523:         self.orderings: list[HybridCollation] = orderings
 524:         self.unique_exprs: list[HybridExpr] = unique_exprs
 525: 
 526:     def search_term_definition(self, name: str) -> HybridExpr | None:
 527:         return self.terms.get(name, None)

 542: class HybridCollectionAccess(HybridOperation):
 543:     """
 544:     Class for HybridOperation corresponding to accessing a collection (either
 545:     directly or as a subcollection).
 546:     """
 547: 
 548:     def __init__(self, collection: CollectionAccess):
 549:         self.collection: CollectionAccess = collection
 550:         terms: dict[str, HybridExpr] = {}
 551:         for name in collection.calc_terms:
 552:             raw_expr = collection.get_term_from_property(name)
 553:             assert isinstance(raw_expr, ColumnProperty)
 554:             terms[name] = HybridColumnExpr(raw_expr)
 555:         unique_exprs: list[HybridExpr] = []
 556:         for name in sorted(collection.unique_terms, key=str):
 557:             expr: PyDoughExpressionQDAG = collection.get_expr(name)
 558:             unique_exprs.append(HybridRefExpr(name, expr.pydough_type))
 559:         self.general_condition: HybridExpr | None = None
 560:         super().__init__(terms, {}, [], unique_exprs)
 561: 
 562:     def __repr__(self):
 563:         return f"COLLECTION[{self.collection.collection.name}]"

 578:             subtree.pipeline[-1].unique_exprs,
 579:         )
 580: 
 581:     def __repr__(self):
 582:         return "PARTITION_CHILD[*]"

 585: class HybridCalculate(HybridOperation):
 586:     """
 587:     Class for HybridOperation corresponding to a CALCULATE operation.
 588:     """
 589: 
 590:     def __init__(
 591:         self,
 592:         predecessor: HybridOperation,
 593:         new_expressions: dict[str, HybridExpr],
 594:         orderings: list[HybridCollation],
 595:     ):
 596:         self.predecessor: HybridOperation = predecessor
 597:         terms: dict[str, HybridExpr] = {}
 598:         renamings: dict[str, str] = {}
 599:         for name, expr in predecessor.terms.items():
 600:             terms[name] = HybridRefExpr(name, expr.typ)
 601:         renamings.update(predecessor.renamings)
 602:         new_renamings: dict[str, str] = {}
 603:         for name, expr in new_expressions.items():
 604:             if name in terms and terms[name] == expr:
 605:                 continue
 606:             expr = expr.apply_renamings(predecessor.renamings)
 607:             used_name: str = name
 608:             idx: int = 0
 609:             while (
 610:                 used_name in terms
 611:                 or used_name in renamings
 612:                 or used_name in new_renamings
 613:             ):
 614:                 if (
 615:                     (used_name not in renamings)
 616:                     and (used_name not in new_renamings)
 617:                     and (self.predecessor.search_term_definition(used_name) == expr)
 618:                 ):
 619:                     break
 620:                 used_name = f"{name}_{idx}"
 621:                 idx += 1
 622:                 new_renamings[name] = used_name
 623:             terms[used_name] = expr
 624:         renamings.update(new_renamings)
 625:         for old_name, new_name in new_renamings.items():
 626:             expr = new_expressions.pop(old_name)
 627:             new_expressions[new_name] = expr
 628:         super().__init__(terms, renamings, orderings, predecessor.unique_exprs)
 629:         self.new_expressions = new_expressions
 630: 
 631:     def __repr__(self):
 632:         return f"CALCULATE[{self.new_expressions}]"
 633: 
 634:     def search_term_definition(self, name: str) -> HybridExpr | None:
 635:         if name in self.new_expressions:
 636:             expr: HybridExpr = self.new_expressions[name]
 637:             if not (isinstance(expr, HybridRefExpr) and expr.name == name):
 638:                 return self.new_expressions[name]
 639:         return self.predecessor.search_term_definition(name)
 640:

 664: class HybridChildPullUp(HybridOperation):
 665:     """
 666:     Class for HybridOperation corresponding to evaluating all of the logic from
 667:     a child subtree of the current pipeline then treating it as the current
 668:     level.
 669:     """
 670: 
 671:     def __init__(
 672:         self,
 673:         hybrid: "HybridTree",
 674:         child_idx: int,
 675:         original_child_height: int,
 676:     ):
 677:         self.child: HybridConnection = hybrid.children[child_idx]
 678:         self.child_idx: int = child_idx
 679:         self.pullup_remapping: dict[HybridExpr, HybridExpr] = {}
 680: 
 681:         # Find the level from the child tree that is the equivalent of the
 682:         # level from the child tree that is being replaced.
 683:         current_level: HybridTree = self.child.subtree
 684:         for _ in range(original_child_height):
 685:             assert current_level.parent is not None
 686:             current_level = current_level.parent
 687: 
 688:         # Snapshot the renamings from the current level, and use its unique
 689:         # terms as the unique terms for this level.
 690:         renamings: dict[str, str] = current_level.pipeline[-1].renamings
 691:         unique_exprs: list[HybridExpr] = []
 692:         for unique_expr in current_level.pipeline[-1].unique_exprs:
 693:             new_unique_expr: HybridExpr | None = unique_expr.shift_back(
 694:                 original_child_height
 695:             )
 696:             assert new_unique_expr is not None
 697:             unique_exprs.append(new_unique_expr)
 698: 
 699:         # Start by adding terms from the bottom level of the child as child ref
 700:         # expressions accessible from the parent.
 701:         terms: dict[str, HybridExpr] = {}
 702:         for term_name, term_expr in current_level.pipeline[-1].terms.items():
 703:             child_ref: HybridChildRefExpr = HybridChildRefExpr(
 704:                 term_name, child_idx, term_expr.typ
 705:             )
 706:             terms[term_name] = child_ref
 707: 
 708:         # Iterate through the level identified earlier & its ancestors to find
 709:         # all of their terms and add them to the parent via accesses to
 710:         # backreferences from the child. These terms are placed in the pullup
 711:         # remapping dictionary so to provide hints on how to translate
 712:         # expressions with regards to the parent level into lookups from within
 713:         # the child subtree.
 714:         extra_height: int = 0
 715:         agg_idx: int = 0
 716:         while True:
 717:             current_terms: dict[str, HybridExpr] = current_level.pipeline[-1].terms
 718:             for term_name in sorted(current_terms):
 719:                 # Identify the expression that is being accessed from one of
 720:                 # the levels of the child subtree.
 721:                 current_expr: HybridExpr = HybridRefExpr(
 722:                     term_name, current_terms[term_name].typ
 723:                 )
 724:                 shifted_expr: HybridExpr | None = current_expr.shift_back(extra_height)
 725:                 assert shifted_expr is not None
 726:                 current_expr = shifted_expr
 727:                 back_expr: HybridExpr = HybridBackRefExpr(
 728:                     term_name,
 729:                     original_child_height + extra_height,
 730:                     current_terms[term_name].typ,
 731:                 )
 732:                 if self.child.connection_type.is_aggregation:
 733:                     # If aggregating, wrap the backreference in an ANYTHING
 734:                     # call that is added to the agg calls list so it can be
 735:                     # passed through the aggregation.
 736:                     passthrough_agg: HybridFunctionExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
 737:                         pydop.ANYTHING, [back_expr], back_expr.typ
 738:                     )
 739:                     agg_name: str
 740:                     # If the aggregation already exists, use it. Otherwise
 741:                     # insert a new aggregation.
 742:                     if passthrough_agg in self.child.aggs.values():
 743:                         agg_name = self.child.fetch_agg_name(passthrough_agg)
 744:                     else:
 745:                         agg_name = f"agg_{agg_idx}"
 746:                         while (
 747:                             agg_name in self.child.aggs
 748:                             or agg_name in self.child.subtree.pipeline[-1].terms
 749:                         ):
 750:                             agg_idx += 1
 751:                             agg_name = f"agg_{agg_idx}"
 752:                         self.child.aggs[agg_name] = passthrough_agg
 753:                         self.pullup_remapping[current_expr] = HybridRefExpr(
 754:                             agg_name, back_expr.typ
 755:                         )
 756:                 else:
 757:                     # Otherwise, add an access to the backreference to the
 758:                     # pullup remapping.
 759:                     self.pullup_remapping[current_expr] = back_expr
 760:             if current_level.parent is None:
 761:                 break
 762:             current_level = current_level.parent
 763:             extra_height += 1
 764: 
 765:         super().__init__(terms, renamings, [], unique_exprs)
 766: 
 767:     def __repr__(self):
 768:         return f"PULLUP[${self.child_idx}: {self.pullup_remapping}]"
 769:
````
