 840: class ConnectionType(Enum):
 841:     """
 842:     An enum describing how a hybrid tree is connected to a child tree.
 843:     """
 844: 
 845:     SINGULAR = 0
 846:     """
 847:     The child should be 1:1 with regards to the parent, and can thus be
 848:     accessed via a simple left join without having to worry about cardinality
 849:     contamination.
 850:     """
 851: 
 852:     AGGREGATION = 1
 853:     """
 854:     The child is being accessed for the purposes of aggregating its columns.
 855:     The aggregation is done on top of the translated subtree before it is
 856:     combined with the parent tree via a left join. The aggregate call may be
 857:     augmented after the left join, e.g. to coalesce with a default value if the
 858:     left join was not used. The grouping keys for the aggregate are the keys
 859:     used to join the parent tree output onto the subtree output.
 860: 
 861:     If this is used as a child access of a `PARTITION` node, there is no left
 862:     join, though some of the post-processing steps may still occur.
 863:     """
 864: 
 865:     NDISTINCT = 2
 866:     """
 867:     The child is being accessed for the purposes of counting how many
 868:     distinct elements it has. This is implemented by grouping the child subtree
 869:     on both the original grouping keys as well as the unique columns of the
 870:     subcollection without any aggregations, then having the `aggs` list contain
 871:     a solitary `COUNT` term before being left-joined. The result is coalesced
 872:     with 0, unless this is used as a child access of a `PARTITION` node.
 873:     """
 874: 
 875:     SEMI = 3
 876:     """
 877:     The child is being used as a semi-join.
 878:     """
 879: 
 880:     SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH = 4
 881:     """
 882:     If a SINGULAR connection overlaps with a SEMI connection, then they are
 883:     fused into a variant of SINGULAR that can use an INNER join instead of a
 884:     LEFT join.
 885:     """
 886: 
 887:     AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH = 5
 888:     """
 889:     If an AGGREGATION connection overlaps with a SEMI connection, then they are
 890:     fused into a variant of AGGREGATION that can use an INNER join instead of a
 891:     LEFT join.
 892:     """
 893: 
 894:     NDISTINCT_ONLY_MATCH = 6
 895:     """
 896:     If a NDISTINCT connection overlaps with a SEMI connection, then they are
 897:     fused into a variant of NDISTINCT that can use an INNER join instead of a
 898:     LEFT join.
 899:     """
 900: 
 901:     ANTI = 7
 902:     """
 903:     The child is being used as an anti-join.
 904:     """
 905: 
 906:     NO_MATCH_SINGULAR = 8
 907:     """
 908:     If a SINGULAR connection overlaps with an ANTI connection, then it
 909:     becomes this connection which still functions as an ANTI but replaces
 910:     all of the child references with NULL.
 911:     """
 912: 
 913:     NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION = 9
 914:     """
 915:     If an AGGREGATION connection overlaps with an ANTI connection, then it
 916:     becomes this connection which still functions as an ANTI but replaces
 917:     all of the aggregation outputs with NULL.
 918:     """
 919: 
 920:     NO_MATCH_NDISTINCT = 10
 921:     """
 922:     If a NDISTINCT connection overlaps with an ANTI connection, then it
 923:     becomes this connection which still functions as an ANTI but replaces
 924:     the NDISTINCT output with 0.
 925:     """
 926: 
 927:     @property
 928:     def is_singular(self) -> bool:
 929:         """
 930:         Whether the connection type corresponds to one of the 3 SINGULAR
 931:         cases.
 932:         """
 933:         return self in (
 934:             ConnectionType.SINGULAR,
 935:             ConnectionType.SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH,
 936:             ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_SINGULAR,
 937:         )
 938: 
 939:     @property
 940:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
 941:         """
 942:         Whether the connection type corresponds to one of the 3 AGGREGATION
 943:         cases.
 944:         """
 945:         return self in (
 946:             ConnectionType.AGGREGATION,
 947:             ConnectionType.AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH,
 948:             ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION,
 949:         )
 950: 
 951:     @property
 952:     def is_ndistinct(self) -> bool:
 953:         """
 954:         Whether the connection type corresponds to one of the 3 NDISTINCT
 955:         cases.
 956:         """
 957:         return self in (
 958:             ConnectionType.NDISTINCT,
 959:             ConnectionType.NDISTINCT_ONLY_MATCH,
 960:             ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_NDISTINCT,
 961:         )
 962: 
 963:     @property
 964:     def is_semi(self) -> bool:
 965:         """
 966:         Whether the connection type corresponds to one of the 4 SEMI cases.
 967:         """
 968:         return self in (
 969:             ConnectionType.SEMI,
 970:             ConnectionType.SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH,
 971:             ConnectionType.AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH,
 972:             ConnectionType.NDISTINCT_ONLY_MATCH,
 973:         )
 974: 
 975:     @property
 976:     def is_anti(self) -> bool:
 977:         """
 978:         Whether the connection type corresponds to one of the 4 ANTI cases.
 979:         """
 980:         return self in (
 981:             ConnectionType.ANTI,
 982:             ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_SINGULAR,
 983:             ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION,
 984:             ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION,
 985:         )
 986: 
 987:     @property
 988:     def is_neutral_matching(self) -> bool:
 989:         """
 990:         Whether the connection type is neutral with regards to how it accesses
 991:         any child terms.
 992:         """
 993:         return self in (ConnectionType.SEMI, ConnectionType.ANTI)
 994: 
 995:     @property
 996:     def is_singular_compatible(self) -> bool:
 997:         """
 998:         Whether the connection type can be reconciled with SINGULAR.
 999:         """
1000:         return self.is_singular or self.is_neutral_matching
1001: 
1002:     @property
1003:     def is_aggregation_compatible(self) -> bool:
1004:         """
1005:         Whether the connection type can be reconciled with AGGREGATION.
1006:         """
1007:         return self.is_aggregation or self.is_neutral_matching
1008: 
1009:     @property
1010:     def is_ndistinct_compatible(self) -> bool:
1011:         """
1012:         Whether the connection type can be reconciled with NDISTINCT.
1013:         """
1014:         return self.is_ndistinct or self.is_neutral_matching
1015: 
1016:     @property
1017:     def join_type(self) -> JoinType:
1018:         """
1019:         The type of join that the connection type corresponds to.
1020:         """
1021:         match self:
1022:             case (
1023:                 ConnectionType.SINGULAR
1024:                 | ConnectionType.AGGREGATION
1025:                 | ConnectionType.NDISTINCT
1026:             ):
1027:                 # A regular connection without SEMI or ANTI has to be a LEFT
1028:                 # join since parent records without subcollection instances
1029:                 # must be maintained.
1030:                 return JoinType.LEFT
1031:             case (
1032:                 ConnectionType.SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH
1033:                 | ConnectionType.AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH
1034:                 | ConnectionType.NDISTINCT_ONLY_MATCH
1035:             ):
1036:                 # A regular connection combined with SEMI can be an INNER join
1037:                 # since records without matches can be dropped.
1038:                 return JoinType.INNER
1039:             case ConnectionType.SEMI:
1040:                 # A standalone SEMI connection just becomes a SEMI join.
1041:                 return JoinType.SEMI
1042:             case (
1043:                 ConnectionType.ANTI
1044:                 | ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_SINGULAR
1045:                 | ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION
1046:                 | ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_NDISTINCT
1047:             ):
1048:                 # Any type of ANTI connection just becomes an ANTI join; the
1049:                 # relational conversion step is responsible for converting any
1050:                 # references to the child expressions/aggregations to NULL
1051:                 # since they do not exist.
1052:                 return JoinType.ANTI
1053:             case _:
1054:                 raise ValueError(f"Connection type {self} does not have a join type")
1055: 
1056:     def reconcile_connection_types(self, other: "ConnectionType") -> "ConnectionType":
1057:         """
1058:         Combines two connection types and returns the resulting connection
1059:         type used when they overlap.
1060: 
1061:         Args:
1062:             `other`: the other connection type that is to be reconciled
1063:             with `self`.
1064: 
1065:         Returns:
1066:             The connection type produced when `self` and `other` overlap.
1067:         """
1068:         # For duplicates, the connection type is unmodified
1069:         if self == other:
1070:             return self
1071: 
1072:         # Determine whether the connection types are being reconciled into
1073:         # a combination that keeps matches or drops matches (has to be
1074:         # exactly one of these).
1075:         either_semi: bool = self.is_semi or other.is_semi
1076:         either_anti: bool = self.is_anti or other.is_anti
1077:         only_match: bool
1078:         if either_semi and not either_anti:
1079:             only_match = True
1080:         elif either_anti and not either_semi:
1081:             only_match = False
1082:         else:
1083:             raise ValueError(
1084:                 f"Malformed or unsupported combination of connection types: {self} and {other}"
1085:             )
1086: 
1087:         # Determine if the connection types are being resolved into a SINGULAR
1088:         # combination.
1089:         if self.is_singular_compatible and other.is_singular_compatible:
1090:             if only_match:
1091:                 return ConnectionType.SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH
1092:             else:
1093:                 return ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_SINGULAR
1094: 
1095:         # Determine if the connection types are being resolved into an
1096:         # AGGREGATION combination.
1097:         if self.is_aggregation_compatible and other.is_aggregation_compatible:
1098:             if only_match:
1099:                 return ConnectionType.AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH
1100:             else:
1101:                 return ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION
1102: 
1103:         # Determine if the connection types are being resolved into a NDISTINCT
1104:         # combination.
1105:         if self.is_ndistinct_compatible and other.is_ndistinct_compatible:
1106:             if only_match:
1107:                 return ConnectionType.NDISTINCT_ONLY_MATCH
1108:             else:
1109:                 return ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_NDISTINCT
1110: 
1111:         # Every other combination is malformed
1112:         raise ValueError(
1113:             f"Malformed combination of connection types: {self} and {other}"
1114:         )
1115: 
1116: 
1117: @dataclass
1118: class HybridConnection:
1119:     """
1120:     Parcel class corresponding to information about one of the children
1121:     of a HybridTree. Contains the following information:
1122:     - `parent`: the HybridTree that the connection exists within.
1123:     - `subtree`: the HybridTree corresponding to the child itself, starting
1124:       from the bottom.
1125:     - `connection_type`: an enum indicating which connection type is being
1126:        used.
1127:     - `required_steps`: an index indicating which step in the pipeline must be
1128:        completed before the child can be defined.
1129:     - `aggs`: a mapping of aggregation calls made onto expressions relative to the
1130:        context of `subtree`.
1131:     """
1132: 
1133:     parent: "HybridTree"
1134:     subtree: "HybridTree"
1135:     connection_type: ConnectionType
1136:     required_steps: int
1137:     aggs: dict[str, HybridFunctionExpr]
1138: 
1139:     def fetch_agg_name(self, call: HybridFunctionExpr) -> str:
1140:         """
1141:         Returns the name of an aggregation call within the connection. Throws
1142:         an error if the aggregation call is not found.
1143: 
1144:         Args:
1145:             `call`: The aggregation call whose name within the child connection
1146:             is being sought.
1147: 
1148:         Returns:
1149:             The string `name` such that `self.aggs[name]` returns call.
1150: 
1151:         Raises:
1152:             `ValueError`: if the aggregation call is not found.
1153:         """
1154:         try:
1155:             return next(name for name, agg in self.aggs.items() if agg == call)
1156:         except StopIteration:
1157:             raise ValueError(f"Aggregation call {call} not found in {self.aggs}")
1158: 
1159: 
1160: class HybridTree:
1161:     """
1162:     The datastructure class used to keep track of the overall computation in
1163:     a tree structure where each level has a pipeline of operations, possibly
1164:     has a singular predecessor and/or successor, and can have children that
1165:     the operations in the pipeline can access.
1166:     """
1167: 
1168:     def __init__(
1169:         self,
1170:         root_operation: HybridOperation,
1171:         ancestral_mapping: dict[str, int],
1172:         is_hidden_level: bool = False,
1173:         is_connection_root: bool = False,
1174:     ):
1175:         self._pipeline: list[HybridOperation] = [root_operation]
1176:         self._children: list[HybridConnection] = []
1177:         self._ancestral_mapping: dict[str, int] = dict(ancestral_mapping)
1178:         self._successor: HybridTree | None = None
1179:         self._parent: HybridTree | None = None
1180:         self._is_hidden_level: bool = is_hidden_level
1181:         self._is_connection_root: bool = is_connection_root
1182:         self._agg_keys: list[HybridExpr] | None = None
1183:         self._join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] | None = None
1184:         self._general_join_condition: HybridExpr | None = None
1185:         self._correlated_children: set[int] = set()
1186:         if isinstance(root_operation, HybridPartition):
1187:             self._join_keys = []
1188: 
1189:     def __repr__(self):
1190:         lines = []
1191:         if self.parent is not None:
1192:             lines.extend(repr(self.parent).splitlines())
1193:         lines.append(" -> ".join(repr(operation) for operation in self.pipeline))
1194:         prefix = " " if self.successor is None else "↓"
1195:         for idx, child in enumerate(self.children):
1196:             lines.append(f"{prefix} child #{idx} ({child.connection_type.name}):")
1197:             if child.subtree.agg_keys is not None:
1198:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}  aggregate: {child.subtree.agg_keys}")
1199:             if len(child.aggs):
1200:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}  aggs: {child.aggs}:")
1201:             if child.subtree.join_keys is not None:
1202:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}  join: {child.subtree.join_keys}")
1203:             if child.subtree.general_join_condition is not None:
1204:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}  join: {child.subtree.general_join_condition}")
1205:             for line in repr(child.subtree).splitlines():
1206:                 lines.append(f"{prefix} {line}")
1207:         return "\n".join(lines)
1208: 
1209:     def __eq__(self, other):
1210:         return type(self) is type(other) and repr(self) == repr(other)
1211: 
1212:     @property
1213:     def pipeline(self) -> list[HybridOperation]:
1214:         """
1215:         The sequence of operations done in the current level of the hybrid
1216:         tree.
1217:         """
1218:         return self._pipeline
1219: 
1220:     @property
1221:     def children(self) -> list[HybridConnection]:
1222:         """
1223:         The child operations evaluated so that they can be used by operations
1224:         in the pipeline.
1225:         """
1226:         return self._children
1227: 
1228:     @property
1229:     def ancestral_mapping(self) -> dict[str, int]:
1230:         """
1231:         The mapping used to identify terms that are references to an alias
1232:         defined in an ancestor.
1233:         """
1234:         return self._ancestral_mapping
1235: 
1236:     @property
1237:     def correlated_children(self) -> set[int]:
1238:         """
1239:         The set of indices of children that contain correlated references to
1240:         the current hybrid tree.
1241:         """
1242:         return self._correlated_children
1243: 
1244:     @property
1245:     def successor(self) -> Optional["HybridTree"]:
1246:         """
1247:         The next level below in the HybridTree, if present.
1248:         """
1249:         return self._successor
1250: 
1251:     @property
1252:     def parent(self) -> Optional["HybridTree"]:
1253:         """
1254:         The previous level above in the HybridTree, if present.
1255:         """
1256:         return self._parent
1257: 
1258:     @property
1259:     def is_hidden_level(self) -> bool:
1260:         """
1261:         True if the current level should be disregarded when converting
1262:         PyDoughQDAG BACK terms to HybridExpr BACK terms.
1263:         """
1264:         return self._is_hidden_level
1265: 
1266:     @property
1267:     def is_connection_root(self) -> bool:
1268:         """
1269:         True if the current level is the top of a subtree located inside of
1270:         a HybridConnection.
1271:         """
1272:         return self._is_connection_root
1273: 
1274:     @property
1275:     def agg_keys(self) -> list[HybridExpr] | None:
1276:         """
1277:         The list of keys used to aggregate this HybridTree relative to its
1278:         ancestor, if it is the base of a HybridConnection.
1279:         """
1280:         return self._agg_keys
1281: 
1282:     @agg_keys.setter
1283:     def agg_keys(self, agg_keys: list[HybridExpr]) -> None:
1284:         """
1285:         Assigns the aggregation keys to a hybrid tree.
1286:         """
1287:         self._agg_keys = agg_keys
1288: 
1289:     @property
1290:     def join_keys(self) -> list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] | None:
1291:         """
1292:         The list of keys used to join this HybridTree relative to its
1293:         ancestor, if it is the base of a HybridConnection.
1294:         """
1295:         return self._join_keys
1296: 
1297:     @join_keys.setter
1298:     def join_keys(self, join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]]) -> None:
1299:         """
1300:         Assigns the join keys to a hybrid tree.
1301:         """
1302:         self._join_keys = join_keys
1303: 
1304:     @property
1305:     def general_join_condition(self) -> HybridExpr | None:
1306:         """
1307:         A hybrid expression used as a general join condition joining this
1308:         HybridTree to its ancestor, if it is the base of a HybridConnection.
1309:         """
1310:         return self._general_join_condition
1311: 
1312:     @general_join_condition.setter
1313:     def general_join_condition(self, condition: HybridExpr) -> None:
1314:         """
1315:         Assigns the general join condition to a hybrid tree.
1316:         """
1317:         self._general_join_condition = condition
1318: 
1319:     def add_child(
1320:         self,
1321:         child: "HybridTree",
1322:         connection_type: ConnectionType,
1323:         original_correlated_children: set[int],
1324:     ) -> int:
1325:         """
1326:         Adds a new child operation to the current level so that operations in
1327:         the pipeline can make use of it.
1328: 
1329:         Args:
1330:             `child`: the subtree to be connected to `self` as a child
1331:             (starting at the bottom of the subtree).
1332:             `connection_type`: enum indicating what kind of connection is to be
1333:             used to link `self` to `child`.
1334:             `original_correlated_children`: the set of indices of children that
1335:             contain correlated references to the current hybrid tree before
1336:             adding the child.
1337: 
1338:         Returns:
1339:             The index of the newly inserted child (or the index of an existing
1340:             child that matches it).
1341:         """
1342:         for idx, existing_connection in enumerate(self.children):
1343:             if (child == existing_connection.subtree) or (
1344:                 isinstance(self.pipeline[0], HybridPartition)
1345:                 and (child.parent is None)
1346:                 and (len(child.pipeline) == 1)
1347:                 and isinstance(child.pipeline[0], HybridPartitionChild)
1348:             ):
1349:                 connection_type = connection_type.reconcile_connection_types(
1350:                     existing_connection.connection_type
1351:                 )
1352:                 existing_connection.connection_type = connection_type
1353:                 if len(self.correlated_children) > len(original_correlated_children):
1354:                     self._correlated_children = original_correlated_children
1355:                 return idx
1356:         connection: HybridConnection = HybridConnection(
1357:             self, child, connection_type, len(self.pipeline) - 1, {}
1358:         )
1359:         self._children.append(connection)
1360:         return len(self.children) - 1
1361: 
1362:     def add_successor(self, successor: "HybridTree") -> None:
1363:         """
1364:         Marks two hybrid trees in a predecessor-successor relationship.
1365: 
1366:         Args:
1367:             `successor`: the HybridTree to be marked as one level below `self`.
1368:         """
1369:         if self._successor is not None:
1370:             raise Exception("Duplicate successor")
1371:         self._successor = successor
1372:         successor._parent = self
1373:         shifted_expr: HybridExpr | None
1374:         # Shift the aggregation keys and rhs of join keys back by 1 level to
1375:         # account for the fact that the successor must use the same aggregation
1376:         # and join keys as `self`, but they have now become backreferences.
1377:         # Do the same for the general join condition, if one is present.
1378:         if self.agg_keys is not None:
1379:             successor_agg_keys: list[HybridExpr] = []
1380:             for key in self.agg_keys:
1381:                 shifted_expr = key.shift_back(1)
1382:                 assert shifted_expr is not None
1383:                 successor_agg_keys.append(shifted_expr)
1384:             successor.agg_keys = successor_agg_keys
1385:         if self.join_keys is not None:
1386:             successor_join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] = []
1387:             for lhs_key, rhs_key in self.join_keys:
1388:                 shifted_expr = rhs_key.shift_back(1)
1389:                 assert shifted_expr is not None
1390:                 successor_join_keys.append((lhs_key, shifted_expr))
1391:             successor.join_keys = successor_join_keys
1392:         if self.general_join_condition is not None:
1393:             shifted_join_condition: HybridExpr | None = (
1394:                 self.general_join_condition.shift_back(1)
1395:             )
1396:             assert shifted_join_condition is not None
1397:             successor.general_join_condition = shifted_join_condition
1398: 
1399: 
1400: class HybridTranslator:
1401:     """
1402:     Class used to translate PyDough QDAG nodes into the HybridTree structure.
1403:     """
1404: 
1405:     def __init__(self, configs: PyDoughConfigs, dialect: DatabaseDialect):
1406:         self.configs = configs
1407:         # An index used for creating fake column names for aliases
1408:         self.alias_counter: int = 0
1409:         # A stack where each element is a hybrid tree being derived
1410:         # as as subtree of the previous element, and the current tree is
1411:         # being derived as the subtree of the last element.
1412:         self.stack: list[HybridTree] = []
1413:         # If True, rewrites MEDIAN calls into an average of the 1-2 median rows
1414:         # via window functions, otherwise leaves as-is.
1415:         self.rewrite_median: bool = dialect not in {DatabaseDialect.ANSI}
1416: 
1417:     @staticmethod
1418:     def get_join_keys(
1419:         parent_tree: HybridTree,
1420:         subcollection_property: SubcollectionRelationshipMetadata,
1421:         child_node: HybridOperation,
1422:     ) -> list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]]:
1423:         """
1424:         Fetches the list of keys used to join a child node relative to its
1425:         parent node, specifically when the child is a subcollection access.
1426: 
1427:         Args:
1428:             `parent_tree`: the HybridTree corresponding to the parent to access
1429:             from.
1430:             `subcollection_property`: the metadata for the subcollection
1431:             access.
1432:             `child_node`: the HybridOperation node corresponding to the access.
1433: 
1434:         Returns:
1435:             The list of tuples expressions used to join the child, expressed in
1436:             terms of its level, to its parent, where the first tuple element is
1437:             the parent key and the second one is the child key.
1438:         """
1439:         join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] = []
1440:         if isinstance(subcollection_property, SimpleJoinMetadata):
1441:             # If the subcollection is a simple join property, extract the keys.
1442:             for lhs_name in subcollection_property.keys:
1443:                 lhs_key: HybridExpr = (
1444:                     parent_tree.pipeline[-1].terms[lhs_name].make_into_ref(lhs_name)
1445:                 )
1446:                 for rhs_name in subcollection_property.keys[lhs_name]:
1447:                     rhs_key: HybridExpr = child_node.terms[rhs_name].make_into_ref(
1448:                         rhs_name
1449:                     )
1450:                     join_keys.append((lhs_key, rhs_key))
1451:         elif not isinstance(subcollection_property, CartesianProductMetadata):
1452:             raise NotImplementedError(
1453:                 f"Unsupported subcollection property type used for accessing a subcollection: {subcollection_property.__class__.__name__}"
1454:             )
1455:         return join_keys
1456: 
1457:     @staticmethod
1458:     def get_subcollection_join_keys(
1459:         subcollection_property: SubcollectionRelationshipMetadata,
1460:         parent_node: HybridOperation,
1461:         child_node: HybridOperation,
1462:     ) -> list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]]:
1463:         """
1464:         Fetches the list of pairs of keys used to join a parent node onto its
1465:         child node
1466: 
1467:         Args:
1468:             `subcollection_property`: the metadata for the subcollection
1469:             access.
1470:             `parent_node`: the HybridOperation node corresponding to the parent.
1471:             `child_node`: the HybridOperation node corresponding to the access.
1472: 
1473:         Returns:
1474:             A list of tuples in the form `(lhs_key, rhs_key)` where each
1475:             `lhs_key` is the join key from the parent's perspective and each
1476:             `rhs_key` is the join key from the child's perspective.
1477:         """
1478:         join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] = []
1479:         if isinstance(subcollection_property, SimpleJoinMetadata):
1480:             # If the subcollection is a simple join property, extract the keys
1481:             # and build the corresponding (lhs_key == rhs_key) conditions
1482:             for lhs_name in subcollection_property.keys:
1483:                 lhs_key: HybridExpr = parent_node.terms[lhs_name].make_into_ref(
1484:                     lhs_name
1485:                 )
1486:                 for rhs_name in subcollection_property.keys[lhs_name]:
1487:                     rhs_key: HybridExpr = child_node.terms[rhs_name].make_into_ref(
1488:                         rhs_name
1489:                     )
1490:                     join_keys.append((lhs_key, rhs_key))
1491:         elif not isinstance(subcollection_property, CartesianProductMetadata):
1492:             raise NotImplementedError(
1493:                 f"Unsupported subcollection property type used for accessing a subcollection: {subcollection_property.__class__.__name__}"
1494:             )
1495:         return join_keys
1496: 
1497:     @staticmethod
1498:     def identify_connection_types(
1499:         expr: PyDoughExpressionQDAG,
1500:         child_idx: int,
1501:         reference_types: set[ConnectionType],
1502:         inside_aggregation: bool = False,
1503:     ) -> None:
1504:         """
1505:         Recursively identifies what types ways a child collection is referenced
1506:         by its parent context.
1507: 
1508:         Args:
1509:             `expr`: the expression being recursively checked for references
1510:             to the child collection.
1511:             `child_idx`: the index of the child that is being searched for
1512:             references to it.
1513:             `reference_types`: the set of known connection types that the
1514:             are used when referencing the child; the function should mutate
1515:             this set if it finds any new connections.
1516:             `inside_aggregation`: True if `expr` is inside of a call to an
1517:             aggregation function.
1518:         """
1519:         match expr:
1520:             # If `expr` is a reference to the child in question, add
1521:             # a reference that is either singular or aggregation depending
1522:             # on the `inside_aggregation` argument
1523:             case ChildReferenceExpression() if expr.child_idx == child_idx:
1524:                 reference_types.add(
1525:                     ConnectionType.AGGREGATION
1526:                     if inside_aggregation
1527:                     else ConnectionType.SINGULAR
1528:                 )
1529:             case WindowCall():
1530:                 # Otherwise, mutate `reference_types` based on the arguments
1531:                 # to the window call.
1532:                 for window_arg in expr.args:
1533:                     HybridTranslator.identify_connection_types(
1534:                         window_arg, child_idx, reference_types, inside_aggregation
1535:                     )
1536:                 for col in expr.collation_args:
1537:                     HybridTranslator.identify_connection_types(
1538:                         col.expr, child_idx, reference_types, inside_aggregation
1539:                     )
1540:             case ExpressionFunctionCall():
1541:                 # If `expr` is a `HAS` call on the child in question, add a
1542:                 # semi-join connection.
1543:                 if expr.operator == pydop.HAS:
1544:                     arg = expr.args[0]
1545:                     assert isinstance(arg, ChildReferenceCollection)
1546:                     if arg.child_idx == child_idx:
1547:                         reference_types.add(ConnectionType.SEMI)
1548:                 # If `expr` is a `HASNOT` call on the child in question, add a
1549:                 # anti-join connection.
1550:                 elif expr.operator == pydop.HASNOT:
1551:                     arg = expr.args[0]
1552:                     assert isinstance(arg, ChildReferenceCollection)
1553:                     if arg.child_idx == child_idx:
1554:                         reference_types.add(ConnectionType.ANTI)
1555:                 # Otherwise, mutate `reference_types` based on the arguments
1556:                 # to the function call.
1557:                 else:
1558:                     for arg in expr.args:
1559:                         if isinstance(arg, ChildReferenceCollection):
1560:                             # If the argument is a reference to a child,
1561:                             # collection, e.g. `COUNT(X)`, treat as an
1562:                             # aggregation reference if it refers to the child
1563:                             # in question.
1564:                             if arg.child_idx == child_idx:
1565:                                 reference_types.add(ConnectionType.AGGREGATION)
1566:                         else:
1567:                             # Otherwise, recursively check the arguments to the
1568:                             # function, promoting `inside_aggregation` to True
1569:                             # if the function is an aggfunc.
1570:                             assert isinstance(arg, PyDoughExpressionQDAG)
1571:                             inside_aggregation = (
1572:                                 inside_aggregation or expr.operator.is_aggregation
1573:                             )
1574:                             HybridTranslator.identify_connection_types(
1575:                                 arg, child_idx, reference_types, inside_aggregation
1576:                             )
1577:             case _:
1578:                 return
1579: 
1580:     def inject_expression(
1581:         self, hybrid: HybridTree, expr: HybridExpr, create_new_calc: bool
1582:     ) -> HybridExpr:
1583:         """
1584:         Injects a hybrid expression into the HybridTree's terms, returning
1585:         the new name it was injected with.
1586: 
1587:         Args:
1588:             `hybrid`: the base of the HybridTree to inject the expression into.
1589:             `expr`: the expression to be injected.
1590:             `create_new_calc`: if True, injects the expression into a new
1591:             CALCULATE operation. If False, injects the expression into the
1592:             last CALCULATE operation in the pipeline, if there is one at the
1593:             end, otherwise creates a new one.
1594: 
1595:         Returns:
1596:             The HybridExpr corresponding to the injected expression.
1597:         """
1598:         name: str = self.get_internal_name("expr", [hybrid.pipeline[-1].terms])
1599:         if isinstance(hybrid.pipeline[-1], HybridCalculate) and not create_new_calc:
1600:             hybrid.pipeline[-1].terms[name] = expr
1601:             hybrid.pipeline[-1].new_expressions[name] = expr
1602:         else:
1603:             hybrid.pipeline.append(
1604:                 HybridCalculate(
1605:                     hybrid.pipeline[-1],
1606:                     {name: expr},
1607:                     hybrid.pipeline[-1].orderings,
1608:                 )
1609:             )
1610:         return HybridRefExpr(name, expr.typ)
1611: 
1612:     def eject_aggregate_inputs(self, hybrid: HybridTree) -> None:
1613:         """
1614:         Ensures that any inputs to aggregation calls are only references to
1615:         columns from the subtree of the hybrid connection being aggregated.
1616: 
1617:         Args:
1618:             `hybrid`: the base of the HybridTree to eject the aggregate inputs
1619:             from. The ancestors & children of `hybrid` must also be processed.
1620:         """
1621:         if hybrid.parent is not None:
1622:             self.eject_aggregate_inputs(hybrid.parent)
1623:         for child in hybrid.children:
1624:             self.eject_aggregate_inputs(child.subtree)
1625:             create_new_calc: bool = True
1626:             for agg_name, agg_call in sorted(child.aggs.items()):
1627:                 rewritten: bool = False
1628:                 new_args: list[HybridExpr] = []
1629:                 for arg in agg_call.args:
1630:                     if isinstance(arg, HybridRefExpr):
1631:                         new_args.append(arg)
1632:                     else:
1633:                         rewritten = True
1634:                         new_args.append(
1635:                             self.inject_expression(child.subtree, arg, create_new_calc)
1636:                         )
1637:                         create_new_calc = False
1638:                 if rewritten:
1639:                     child.aggs[agg_name] = HybridFunctionExpr(
1640:                         agg_call.operator,
1641:                         new_args,
1642:                         agg_call.typ,
1643:                     )
1644: 
1645:     def run_rewrites(self, hybrid: HybridTree):
1646:         """
1647:         Run any rewrite procedures that must occur after de-correlation, such
1648:         as converting MEDIAN to an average of the 1-2 median rows.
1649: 
1650:         Args:
1651:             `hybrid`: the bottom of the hybrid tree to rewrite.
1652:         """
1653:         # Recursively proceed on the ancestors & children
1654:         if hybrid.parent is not None:
1655:             self.run_rewrites(hybrid.parent)
1656:         for child in hybrid.children:
1657:             self.run_rewrites(child.subtree)
1658: 
1659:         create_new_calc: bool = True
1660:         # Rewrite any MEDIAN calls
1661:         if self.rewrite_median:
1662:             for child in hybrid.children:
1663:                 for agg_name, agg_call in child.aggs.items():
1664:                     if agg_call.operator == pydop.MEDIAN:
1665:                         child.aggs[agg_name] = self.rewrite_median_call(
1666:                             child, agg_call, create_new_calc
1667:                         )
1668:                         create_new_calc = False
1669: 
1670:     def populate_children(
1671:         self,
1672:         hybrid: HybridTree,
1673:         child_operator: ChildOperator,
1674:         child_idx_mapping: dict[int, int],
1675:     ) -> None:
1676:         """
1677:         Helper utility that takes any children of a child operator (CALCULATE,
1678:         WHERE, etc.) and builds the corresponding HybridTree subtree,
1679:         where the parent of the subtree's root is absent instead of the
1680:         current level, and inserts the corresponding HybridConnection node.
1681: 
1682:         Args:
1683:             `hybrid`: the HybridTree having children added to it.
1684:             `child_operator`: the collection QDAG node (CALCULATE, WHERE, etc.)
1685:             containing the children.
1686:             `child_idx_mapping`: a mapping of indices of children of the
1687:             original `child_operator` to the indices of children of the hybrid
1688:             tree level, since the hybrid tree contains the children of all
1689:             pipeline operators of the current level and therefore the indices
1690:             get changes. When the child is inserted, this mapping is mutated
1691:             accordingly so expressions using the child indices know what hybrid
1692:             connection index to use.
1693:         """
1694:         self.stack.append(hybrid)
1695:         for child_idx, child in enumerate(child_operator.children):
1696:             # Infer how the child is used by the current operation based on
1697:             # the expressions that the operator uses.
1698:             reference_types: set[ConnectionType] = set()
1699:             match child_operator:
1700:                 case Where():
1701:                     self.identify_connection_types(
1702:                         child_operator.condition, child_idx, reference_types
1703:                     )
1704:                 case OrderBy():
1705:                     for col in child_operator.collation:
1706:                         self.identify_connection_types(
1707:                             col.expr, child_idx, reference_types
1708:                         )
1709:                 case Calculate():
1710:                     for expr in child_operator.calc_term_values.values():
1711:                         self.identify_connection_types(expr, child_idx, reference_types)
1712:                 case PartitionBy():
1713:                     reference_types.add(ConnectionType.AGGREGATION)
1714:             # Combine the various references to the child to identify the type
1715:             # of connection and add the child. If it already exists, the index
1716:             # of the existing child will be used instead, but the connection
1717:             # type will be updated to reflect the new invocation of the child.
1718:             if len(reference_types) == 0:
1719:                 raise ValueError(
1720:                     f"Bad call to populate_children: child {child_idx} of {child_operator} is never used"
1721:                 )
1722:             connection_type: ConnectionType = reference_types.pop()
1723:             for con_typ in reference_types:
1724:                 connection_type = connection_type.reconcile_connection_types(con_typ)
1725:             # Build the hybrid tree for the child. Before doing so, reset the
1726:             # alias counter to 0 to ensure that identical subtrees are named
1727:             # in the same manner. Afterwards, reset the alias counter to its
1728:             # value within this context.
1729:             snapshot: int = self.alias_counter
1730:             self.alias_counter = 0
1731:             original_correlated_children: set[int] = set(hybrid.correlated_children)
1732:             subtree: HybridTree = self.make_hybrid_tree(
1733:                 child, hybrid, connection_type.is_aggregation
1734:             )
1735:             back_exprs: dict[str, HybridExpr] = {}
1736:             for name in subtree.ancestral_mapping:
1737:                 # Skip adding backrefs for terms that remain part of the
1738:                 # ancestry through the PARTITION, since this creates an
1739:                 # unecessary correlation.
1740:                 if (
1741:                     name in hybrid.ancestral_mapping
1742:                     or name in hybrid.pipeline[-1].terms
1743:                 ):
1744:                     continue
1745:                 hybrid_back_expr = self.make_hybrid_expr(
1746:                     subtree,
1747:                     child.get_expr(name),
1748:                     {},
1749:                     False,
1750:                 )
1751:                 back_exprs[name] = hybrid_back_expr
1752:             if len(back_exprs):
1753:                 subtree.pipeline.append(
1754:                     HybridCalculate(
1755:                         subtree.pipeline[-1],
1756:                         back_exprs,
1757:                         subtree.pipeline[-1].orderings,
1758:                     )
1759:                 )
1760:             self.alias_counter = snapshot
1761:             child_idx_mapping[child_idx] = hybrid.add_child(
1762:                 subtree, connection_type, original_correlated_children
1763:             )
1764:         self.stack.pop()
1765: 
1766:     def postprocess_agg_output(
1767:         self, agg_call: HybridFunctionExpr, agg_ref: HybridExpr, joins_can_nullify: bool
1768:     ) -> HybridExpr:
1769:         """
1770:         Transforms an aggregation function call in any ways that are necessary
1771:         due to configs, such as coalescing the output with zero.
1772: 
1773:         Args:
1774:             `agg_call`: the aggregation call whose reference must be
1775:             transformed if the configs demand it.
1776:             `agg_ref`: the reference to the aggregation call that is
1777:             transformed if the configs demand it.
1778:             `joins_can_nullify`: True if the aggregation is fed into a left
1779:             join, which creates the requirement for some aggregations like
1780:             `COUNT` to have their defaults replaced.
1781: 
1782:         Returns:
1783:             The transformed version of `agg_ref`, if postprocessing is required,
1784:         """
1785:         # If doing a SUM or AVG, and the configs are set to default those
1786:         # functions to zero when there are no values, decorate the result
1787:         # with `DEFAULT_TO(x, 0)`. Also, always does this step with
1788:         # COUNT/NDISTINCT for left joins since the semantics of those functions
1789:         # never allow returning NULL.
1790:         if (
1791:             (agg_call.operator == pydop.SUM and self.configs.sum_default_zero)
1792:             or (agg_call.operator == pydop.AVG and self.configs.avg_default_zero)
1793:             or (
1794:                 agg_call.operator in (pydop.COUNT, pydop.NDISTINCT)
1795:                 and joins_can_nullify
1796:             )
1797:         ):
1798:             agg_ref = HybridFunctionExpr(
1799:                 pydop.DEFAULT_TO,
1800:                 [agg_ref, HybridLiteralExpr(Literal(0, Int64Type()))],
1801:                 agg_call.typ,
1802:             )
1803:         return agg_ref
1804: 
1805:     def gen_agg_name(self, connection: "HybridConnection") -> str:
1806:         """
1807:         Generates a unique name for an aggregation function's output that
1808:         is not already used.
1809: 
1810:         Args:
1811:             `connection`: the HybridConnection in which the aggregation
1812:             is being defined. The name cannot overlap with any other agg
1813:             names or term names of the connection.
1814: 
1815:         Returns:
1816:             The new name to be used.
1817:         """
1818:         return self.get_internal_name(
1819:             "agg", [connection.subtree.pipeline[-1].terms, connection.aggs]
1820:         )
1821: 
1822:     def get_ordering_name(self, hybrid: HybridTree) -> str:
1823:         return self.get_internal_name("ordering", [hybrid.pipeline[-1].terms])
1824: 
1825:     def get_internal_name(
1826:         self, prefix: str, reserved_names: list[Iterable[str]]
1827:     ) -> str:
1828:         """
1829:         Generates a name to be used in the terms of a HybridTree with a
1830:         specified prefix that does not overlap with certain names that have
1831:         already been taken in that context.
1832: 
1833:         Args:
1834:             `prefix`: the prefix that the generated name should start with.
1835:             `reserved_names`: a list of mappings where the keys in each mapping
1836:             are names that cannot be used because they have already been taken.
1837: 
1838:         Returns:
1839:             The string of the name chosen with the corresponding prefix that
1840:             does not overlap with the reserved name.
1841:         """
1842:         name = f"{prefix}_{self.alias_counter}"
1843:         while any(name in s for s in reserved_names):
1844:             self.alias_counter += 1
1845:             name = f"{prefix}_{self.alias_counter}"
1846:         self.alias_counter += 1
1847:         return name
1848: 
1849:     def handle_collection_count(
1850:         self,
1851:         hybrid: HybridTree,
1852:         expr: ExpressionFunctionCall,
1853:         child_ref_mapping: dict[int, int],
1854:     ) -> HybridExpr:
1855:         """
1856:         Special case of `make_hybrid_expr` specifically for expressions that
1857:         are the COUNT of a subcollection.
1858: 
1859:         Args:
1860:             `hybrid`: the hybrid tree that should be used to derive the
1861:             translation of `expr`, as it is the context in which the `expr`
1862:             will live.
1863:             `expr`: the QDAG expression to be converted.
1864:             `child_ref_mapping`: mapping of indices used by child references in
1865:             the original expressions to the index of the child hybrid tree
1866:             relative to the current level.
1867: 
1868:         Returns:
1869:             The HybridExpr node corresponding to `expr`
1870:         """
1871:         assert expr.operator == pydop.COUNT, (
1872:             f"Malformed call to handle_collection_count: {expr}"
1873:         )
1874:         assert len(expr.args) == 1, f"Malformed call to handle_collection_count: {expr}"
1875:         collection_arg = expr.args[0]
1876:         assert isinstance(collection_arg, ChildReferenceCollection), (
1877:             f"Malformed call to handle_collection_count: {expr}"
1878:         )
1879:         count_call: HybridFunctionExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
1880:             pydop.COUNT, [], expr.pydough_type
1881:         )
1882:         child_idx: int = child_ref_mapping[collection_arg.child_idx]
1883:         child_connection: HybridConnection = hybrid.children[child_idx]
1884:         # Generate a unique name for the agg call to push into the child
1885:         # connection. If the call already exists, reuse the existing name.
1886:         agg_name: str
1887:         if count_call in child_connection.aggs.values():
1888:             agg_name = child_connection.fetch_agg_name(count_call)
1889:         else:
1890:             agg_name = self.gen_agg_name(child_connection)
1891:             child_connection.aggs[agg_name] = count_call
1892:         result_ref: HybridExpr = HybridChildRefExpr(
1893:             agg_name, child_idx, expr.pydough_type
1894:         )
1895:         # The null-adding join is not done if this is the root level, since
1896:         # that just means all the aggregations are no-groupby aggregations.
1897:         joins_can_nullify: bool = not (
1898:             isinstance(hybrid.pipeline[0], HybridRoot)
1899:             or child_connection.connection_type.is_semi
1900:         )
1901:         return self.postprocess_agg_output(count_call, result_ref, joins_can_nullify)
1902: 
1903:     def handle_has_hasnot(
1904:         self,
1905:         hybrid: HybridTree,
1906:         expr: ExpressionFunctionCall,
1907:         child_ref_mapping: dict[int, int],
1908:     ) -> HybridExpr:
1909:         """
1910:         Handler function for translating a `HAS` or `HASNOT` expression by
1911:         mutating the referenced HybridConnection so it enforces that predicate,
1912:         then returning an expression indicating that the condition has been
1913:         met.
1914:         """
1915:         assert expr.operator in (
1916:             pydop.HAS,
1917:             pydop.HASNOT,
1918:         ), f"Malformed call to handle_has_hasnot: {expr}"
1919:         assert len(expr.args) == 1, f"Malformed call to handle_has_hasnot: {expr}"
1920:         collection_arg = expr.args[0]
1921:         assert isinstance(collection_arg, ChildReferenceCollection), (
1922:             f"Malformed call to handle_has_hasnot: {expr}"
1923:         )
1924:         # Reconcile the existing connection type with either SEMI or ANTI
1925:         child_idx: int = child_ref_mapping[collection_arg.child_idx]
1926:         child_connection: HybridConnection = hybrid.children[child_idx]
1927:         new_conn_type: ConnectionType = (
1928:             ConnectionType.SEMI if expr.operator == pydop.HAS else ConnectionType.ANTI
1929:         )
1930:         child_connection.connection_type = (
1931:             child_connection.connection_type.reconcile_connection_types(new_conn_type)
1932:         )
1933:         # Since the connection has been mutated to be a semi/anti join, the
1934:         # has / hasnot condition is now known to be true.
1935:         return HybridLiteralExpr(Literal(True, BooleanType()))
1936: 
1937:     def convert_agg_arg(self, expr: HybridExpr, child_indices: set[int]) -> HybridExpr:
1938:         """
1939:         Translates a hybrid expression that is an argument to an aggregation
1940:         (or a subexpression of such an argument) into a form that is expressed
1941:         from the perspective of the child subtree that is being aggregated.
1942: 
1943:         Args:
1944:             `expr`: the expression to be converted.
1945:             `child_indices`: a set that is mutated to contain the indices of
1946:             any children that are referenced by `expr`.
1947: 
1948:         Returns:
1949:             The translated expression.
1950: 
1951:         Raises:
1952:             NotImplementedError if `expr` is an expression that cannot be used
1953:             inside of an aggregation call.
1954:         """
1955:         match expr:
1956:             case HybridLiteralExpr():
1957:                 return expr
1958:             case HybridChildRefExpr():
1959:                 # Child references become regular references because the
1960:                 # expression is phrased as if we were inside the child rather
1961:                 # than the parent.
1962:                 child_indices.add(expr.child_idx)
1963:                 return HybridRefExpr(expr.name, expr.typ)
1964:             case HybridFunctionExpr():
1965:                 return HybridFunctionExpr(
1966:                     expr.operator,
1967:                     [self.convert_agg_arg(arg, child_indices) for arg in expr.args],
1968:                     expr.typ,
1969:                 )
1970:             case HybridBackRefExpr():
1971:                 raise NotImplementedError(
1972:                     "PyDough does yet support aggregations whose arguments mix between subcollection data of the current context and fields of an ancestor of the current context"
1973:                 )
1974:             case HybridRefExpr():
1975:                 raise NotImplementedError(
1976:                     "PyDough does yet support aggregations whose arguments mix between subcollection data of the current context and fields of the context itself"
1977:                 )
1978:             case HybridWindowExpr():
1979:                 raise NotImplementedError(
1980:                     "PyDough does yet support aggregations whose arguments mix between subcollection data of the current context and window functions"
1981:                 )
1982:             case _:
1983:                 raise NotImplementedError(
1984:                     f"TODO: support converting {expr.__class__.__name__} in aggregations"
1985:                 )
1986: 
1987:     def make_agg_call(
1988:         self,
1989:         hybrid: HybridTree,
1990:         expr: ExpressionFunctionCall,
1991:         args: list[HybridExpr],
1992:     ) -> HybridExpr:
1993:         """
1994:         For aggregate function calls, their arguments are translated in a
1995:         manner that identifies what child subtree they correspond too, by
1996:         index, and translates them relative to the subtree. Then, the
1997:         aggregation calls are placed into the `aggs` mapping of the
1998:         corresponding child connection, and the aggregation call becomes a
1999:         child reference (referring to the aggs list), since after translation,
2000:         an aggregated child subtree only has the grouping keys and the
2001:         aggregation calls as opposed to its other terms.
2002: 
2003:         Args:
2004:             `hybrid`: the hybrid tree that should be used to derive the
2005:             translation of the aggregation call.
2006:             `expr`: the aggregation function QDAG expression to be converted.
2007:             `args`: the converted arguments to the aggregation call.
2008:         """
2009:         child_indices: set[int] = set()
2010:         converted_args: list[HybridExpr] = [
2011:             self.convert_agg_arg(arg, child_indices) for arg in args
2012:         ]
2013:         if len(child_indices) != 1:
2014:             raise ValueError(
2015:                 f"Expected aggregation call to contain references to exactly one child collection, but found {len(child_indices)} in {expr}"
2016:             )
2017:         hybrid_call: HybridFunctionExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
2018:             expr.operator, converted_args, expr.pydough_type
2019:         )
2020:         # Identify the child connection that the aggregation call is pushed
2021:         # into.
2022:         child_idx: int = child_indices.pop()
2023:         child_connection: HybridConnection = hybrid.children[child_idx]
2024:         # If the aggregation already exists in the child, use a child reference
2025:         # to it.
2026:         agg_name: str
2027:         if hybrid_call in child_connection.aggs.values():
2028:             agg_name = child_connection.fetch_agg_name(hybrid_call)
2029:         else:
2030:             # Otherwise, Generate a unique name for the agg call to push into the
2031:             # child connection.
2032:             agg_name = self.gen_agg_name(child_connection)
2033:             child_connection.aggs[agg_name] = hybrid_call
2034:         result_ref: HybridExpr = HybridChildRefExpr(
2035:             agg_name, child_idx, expr.pydough_type
2036:         )
2037:         joins_can_nullify: bool = not (
2038:             isinstance(hybrid.pipeline[0], HybridRoot)
2039:             or child_connection.connection_type.is_semi
2040:         )
2041:         return self.postprocess_agg_output(hybrid_call, result_ref, joins_can_nullify)
2042: 
2043:     def rewrite_median_call(
2044:         self,
2045:         child_connection: HybridConnection,
2046:         expr: HybridFunctionExpr,
2047:         create_new_calc: bool,
2048:     ) -> HybridFunctionExpr:
2049:         """
2050:         Transforms a MEDIAN call into an AVG of the 1-2 median rows
2051:         (obtained via window functions). This step must be done after
2052:         de-correlation because it invokes the aggregation keys used for the
2053:         child connection, which may change during de-correlation.
2054: 
2055:         Args:
2056:             `child`: the child connection containing the aggregate call to
2057:             MEDIAN as one of its aggs.
2058:             `expr`: the aggregation function QDAG expression to be converted.
2059:             `create_new_calc`: if True, creates a new CALCULATE when injecting
2060:             the inputs to the AVG call into the child.
2061:         """
2062:         assert expr.operator == pydop.MEDIAN
2063:         # Build an expression that makes all rows null except the 1-2 median
2064:         # rows. The formula to find the kept rows is the following:
2065:         #   ABS((r - 1) - (n - 1) / 2) < 1
2066:         # Where `r` is the row number (sorted by the median column) and `n`
2067:         # is the number of non-null rows of the median column. The window
2068:         # functions are computed with the same partitioning keys that will be
2069:         # used to aggregate the child connection.
2070:         assert len(expr.args) == 1
2071:         data_expr: HybridExpr = expr.args[0]
2072:         one: HybridExpr = HybridLiteralExpr(Literal(1.0, Float64Type()))
2073:         two: HybridExpr = HybridLiteralExpr(Literal(2.0, Float64Type()))
2074:         assert child_connection.subtree.agg_keys is not None
2075:         partition_args: list[HybridExpr] = child_connection.subtree.agg_keys
2076:         order_args: list[HybridCollation] = [HybridCollation(data_expr, False, False)]
2077:         rank: HybridExpr = HybridWindowExpr(
2078:             pydop.RANKING, [], partition_args, order_args, Int64Type(), {}
2079:         )
2080:         rows: HybridExpr = HybridWindowExpr(
2081:             pydop.RELCOUNT, [data_expr], partition_args, [], Int64Type(), {}
2082:         )
2083:         adjusted_rank: HybridExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
2084:             pydop.SUB, [rank, one], Float64Type()
2085:         )
2086:         adjusted_rows: HybridExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
2087:             pydop.SUB, [rows, one], Float64Type()
2088:         )
2089:         centerpoint: HybridExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
2090:             pydop.DIV, [adjusted_rows, two], Float64Type()
2091:         )
2092:         distance_from_center = HybridFunctionExpr(
2093:             pydop.ABS,
2094:             [
2095:                 HybridFunctionExpr(
2096:                     pydop.SUB, [adjusted_rank, centerpoint], Float64Type()
2097:                 )
2098:             ],
2099:             Float64Type(),
2100:         )
2101:         is_median_row: HybridExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
2102:             pydop.LET, [distance_from_center, one], BooleanType()
2103:         )
2104:         median_rows_arg: HybridExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
2105:             pydop.KEEP_IF, [data_expr, is_median_row], data_expr.typ
2106:         )
2107:         # Build a call to AVG on those 1-2 rows.
2108:         median_rows_arg = self.inject_expression(
2109:             child_connection.subtree, median_rows_arg, create_new_calc
2110:         )
2111:         avg_call: HybridFunctionExpr = HybridFunctionExpr(
2112:             pydop.AVG, [median_rows_arg], expr.typ
2113:         )
2114: 
2115:         return avg_call
2116: 
2117:     def make_hybrid_correl_expr(
2118:         self,
2119:         back_expr: BackReferenceExpression,
2120:         collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
2121:         steps_taken_so_far: int,
2122:     ) -> HybridCorrelExpr:
2123:         """
2124:         Converts a BACK reference into a correlated reference when the number
2125:         of BACK levels exceeds the height of the current subtree.
2126: 
2127:         Args:
2128:             `back_expr`: the original BACK reference to be converted.
2129:             `collection`: the collection at the top of the current subtree,
2130:             before we have run out of BACK levels to step up out of.
2131:             `steps_taken_so_far`: the number of steps already taken to step
2132:             up from the BACK node. This is needed so we know how many steps
2133:             still need to be taken upward once we have stepped out of the child
2134:             subtree back into the parent subtree.
2135:         """
2136:         if len(self.stack) == 0:
2137:             raise ValueError("Back reference steps too far back")
2138:         # Identify the parent subtree that the BACK reference is stepping back
2139:         # into, out of the child.
2140:         parent_tree: HybridTree = self.stack.pop()
2141:         remaining_steps_back: int = back_expr.back_levels - steps_taken_so_far - 1
2142:         parent_result: HybridExpr
2143:         new_expr: PyDoughExpressionQDAG
2144:         # Special case: stepping out of the data argument of PARTITION back
2145:         # into its ancestor. For example:
2146:         # TPCH.CALCULATE(x=...).PARTITION(data.WHERE(y > BACK(1).x), ...)
2147:         partition_edge_case: bool = len(parent_tree.pipeline) == 1 and isinstance(
2148:             parent_tree.pipeline[0], HybridPartition
2149:         )
2150:         if partition_edge_case:
2151:             assert parent_tree.parent is not None
2152:             # Treat the partition's parent as the context for the back
2153:             # to step into, as opposed to the partition itself (so the back
2154:             # levels are consistent)
2155:             self.stack.append(parent_tree.parent)
2156:             parent_result = self.make_hybrid_correl_expr(
2157:                 back_expr, collection, steps_taken_so_far
2158:             ).expr
2159:             self.stack.pop()
2160:         elif remaining_steps_back == 0:
2161:             # If there are no more steps back to be made, then the correlated
2162:             # reference is to a reference from the current context.
2163:             if back_expr.term_name in parent_tree.ancestral_mapping:
2164:                 new_expr = BackReferenceExpression(
2165:                     collection,
2166:                     back_expr.term_name,
2167:                     parent_tree.ancestral_mapping[back_expr.term_name],
2168:                 )
2169:                 parent_result = self.make_hybrid_expr(parent_tree, new_expr, {}, False)
2170:             elif back_expr.term_name in parent_tree.pipeline[-1].terms:
2171:                 parent_name: str = parent_tree.pipeline[-1].renamings.get(
2172:                     back_expr.term_name, back_expr.term_name
2173:                 )
2174:                 parent_result = HybridRefExpr(parent_name, back_expr.pydough_type)
2175:             else:
2176:                 raise ValueError(
2177:                     f"Back reference to {back_expr.term_name} not found in parent"
2178:                 )
2179:         else:
2180:             # Otherwise, a back reference needs to be made from the current
2181:             # collection a number of steps back based on how many steps still
2182:             # need to be taken, and it must be recursively converted to a
2183:             # hybrid expression that gets wrapped in a correlated reference.
2184:             new_expr = BackReferenceExpression(
2185:                 collection, back_expr.term_name, remaining_steps_back
2186:             )
2187:             parent_result = self.make_hybrid_expr(parent_tree, new_expr, {}, False)
2188:         if not isinstance(parent_result, HybridCorrelExpr):
2189:             parent_tree.correlated_children.add(len(parent_tree.children))
2190:         # Restore parent_tree back onto the stack, since evaluating `back_expr`
2191:         # does not change the program's current placement in the subtrees.
2192:         self.stack.append(parent_tree)
2193:         # Create the correlated reference to the expression with regards to
2194:         # the parent tree, which could also be a correlated expression.
2195:         return HybridCorrelExpr(parent_tree, parent_result)
2196: 
2197:     def add_unique_terms(
2198:         self,
2199:         hybrid: HybridTree,
2200:         levels_remaining: int,
2201:         levels_so_far: int,
2202:         partition_args: list[HybridExpr],
2203:         child_idx: int | None,
2204:     ) -> None:
2205:         """
2206:         Populates a list of partition keys with the unique terms of an ancestor
2207:         level of the hybrid tree.
2208: 
2209:         Args:
2210:             `hybrid`: the hybrid tree whose ancestor's unique terms are being
2211:             added to the partition keys.
2212:             `levels_remaining`: the number of levels left to step back before
2213:             the unique terms are added to the partition keys.
2214:             `levels_so_far`: the number of levels that have been stepped back
2215:             so far.
2216:             `partition_args`: the list of partition keys that is being
2217:             populated with the unique terms of the ancestor level.
2218:             `child_idx`: the index to use when identifying that a child node
2219:             has become correlated. If not provided, uses the value from the
2220:             top of the stack.
2221:         """
2222:         # When the number of levels remaining to step back is 0, we have
2223:         # reached the targeted ancestor, so we add the unique terms.
2224:         if levels_remaining == 0:
2225:             for unique_term in sorted(hybrid.pipeline[-1].unique_exprs, key=str):
2226:                 shifted_arg: HybridExpr | None = unique_term.shift_back(levels_so_far)
2227:                 assert shifted_arg is not None
2228:                 partition_args.append(shifted_arg)
2229:         elif hybrid.parent is None:
2230:             # If we have not reached the target level yet, but we have reached
2231:             # the top level of the tree, we need to step out of a child subtree
2232:             # back into its parent and make a correlated reference.
2233:             if len(self.stack) == 0:
2234:                 raise ValueError("Window function references too far back")
2235:             prev_hybrid: HybridTree = self.stack.pop()
2236:             correl_args: list[HybridExpr] = []
2237:             self.add_unique_terms(
2238:                 prev_hybrid, levels_remaining - 1, 0, correl_args, child_idx
2239:             )
2240:             join_remapping: dict[HybridExpr, HybridExpr] = dict(
2241:                 hybrid.join_keys if hybrid.join_keys is not None else []
2242:             )
2243:             for arg in correl_args:
2244:                 if arg in join_remapping:
2245:                     # Special case: if the uniqueness key is also a join key
2246:                     # from the LHS, use the equivalent key from the RHS.
2247:                     equivalent_key: HybridExpr | None = join_remapping[arg].shift_back(
2248:                         levels_so_far
2249:                     )
2250:                     assert equivalent_key is not None
2251:                     partition_args.append(equivalent_key)
2252:                 else:
2253:                     # Otherwise, create a correlated reference to the term.
2254:                     if not isinstance(arg, HybridCorrelExpr):
2255:                         if child_idx is not None:
2256:                             prev_hybrid.correlated_children.add(child_idx)
2257:                         else:
2258:                             prev_hybrid.correlated_children.add(
2259:                                 len(prev_hybrid.children)
2260:                             )
2261:                     partition_args.append(HybridCorrelExpr(prev_hybrid, arg))
2262:             self.stack.append(prev_hybrid)
2263:         else:
2264:             # Otherwise, we have to step back further, so we recursively
2265:             # repeat the procedure one level further up in the hybrid tree.
2266:             self.add_unique_terms(
2267:                 hybrid.parent,
2268:                 levels_remaining - 1,
2269:                 levels_so_far + 1,
2270:                 partition_args,
2271:                 child_idx,
2272:             )
2273: 
2274:     def make_hybrid_expr(
2275:         self,
2276:         hybrid: HybridTree,
2277:         expr: PyDoughExpressionQDAG,
2278:         child_ref_mapping: dict[int, int],
2279:         inside_agg: bool,
2280:     ) -> HybridExpr:
2281:         """
2282:         Converts a QDAG expression into a HybridExpr.
2283: 
2284:         Args:
2285:             `hybrid`: the hybrid tree that should be used to derive the
2286:             translation of `expr`, as it is the context in which the `expr`
2287:             will live.
2288:             `expr`: the QDAG expression to be converted.
2289:             `child_ref_mapping`: mapping of indices used by child references in
2290:             the original expressions to the index of the child hybrid tree
2291:             relative to the current level.
2292:             `inside_agg`: True if `expr` is being derived is inside of an
2293:             aggregation call, False otherwise.
2294: 
2295:         Returns:

2514:             a child of.

2699:                         partition_by = (
2700:                             node.child_access.ancestor_context.starting_predecessor

2702:                         assert isinstance(partition_by, PartitionBy)

 28: def merging_doesnt_create_convolution(
 29:     columns_a: dict[str, RelationalExpression],
 30:     columns_b: dict[str, RelationalExpression],
 31: ) -> bool:
 32:     """
 33:     Confirms whether merging two projections results in any complex expressions
 34:     being calculated more than once, ignoring any top-level expressions.
 35:     """
 36:     n_uses: defaultdict[RelationalExpression, int] = defaultdict(int)
 37:     for expr in columns_a.values():
 38:         expr = transpose_expression(expr, columns_b)
 39:         add_expr_uses(expr, n_uses, top_level=True)
 40:     return len(n_uses) == 0 or max(n_uses.values()) == 1
