````python
 68: 
 69:     # For every column, identify which side of the join it references, and add
 70:     # its name to that index of `pushable_columns` if there is exactly one such
 71:     # input side it refers to, thus marking the column expression as pushable
 72:     # into that side.
 73:     join_input_index: int
 74:     for name, expr in project.columns.items():
 75:         finder.reset()
 76:         expr.accept(finder)
 77:         join_input_indices: set[int] = set()
 78:         for input_ref in finder.get_column_references():
 79:             join_input_col: RelationalExpression = join.columns[input_ref.name]
 80:             if not isinstance(join_input_col, ColumnReference):
 81:                 join_input_indices.clear()
 82:                 break
 83:             join_input_indices.add(
 84:                 join.default_input_aliases.index(join_input_col.input_name)
 85:             )
 86:         if len(join_input_indices) == 1:
 87:             join_input_index = join_input_indices.pop()
 88:             # If the corresponding join is an inner join, mark the input as
 89:             # pushable into that side.
 90:             if (
 91:                 join_input_index == 0
 92:                 or join.join_types[join_input_index - 1] == JoinType.INNER
 93:             ):
 94:                 pushable_columns[join_input_index].append((name, expr))
 95: 
 96:     # If not every column can be pushed, abandon the attempt
 97:     if sum(len(columns) for columns in pushable_columns) < len(project.columns):
 98:         return project
 99: 
100:     # Add all input references used in the join condition to a list of columns
101:     # that must be preserved for each join input.
102:     new_input_col_sets: list[dict[str, RelationalExpression]] = [
103:         {} for _ in range(len(join.inputs))
104:     ]
105:     finder.reset()
106:     for cond in join.conditions:
107:         cond.accept(finder)
108:     for input_ref in finder.get_column_references():
109:         join_input_index = join.default_input_aliases.index(input_ref.input_name)
110:         new_input_col_sets[join_input_index][input_ref.name] = ColumnReference(
111:             input_ref.name, input_ref.data_type
112:         )
113: 
114:     # The new columns of the join.
115:     new_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {}
116: 
117:     # For each join input, place all of the columns used from that input into
118:     # a join.
119:     for idx, join_input in enumerate(join.inputs):
120:         input_name: str | None = join.default_input_aliases[idx]
121:         new_input_cols: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = new_input_col_sets[idx]
122:         for name, expr in pushable_columns[idx]:
123:             input_expr_name: str = name
124:             counter: int = 0
125:             # If the name already exists, create a new name for the column
126:             # expression in the new projection that will be part of the input.
127:             while input_expr_name in new_input_cols:
128:                 if expr == new_input_cols[name]:
129:                     break
130:                 input_expr_name += f"_{counter}"
131:                 counter += 1
132:             # Add the expression to the projection for the referenced input,
133:             # and a reference to the new column in the join's columns.
134:             new_input_cols[input_expr_name] = transpose_expression(expr, join.columns)
135:             new_columns[name] = ColumnReference(
136:                 input_expr_name, expr.data_type, input_name=input_name
137:             )
138:         # Create the projection on top of the join's input, unless the
139:         # projection would be a no-op
140:         if new_input_cols != join_input.columns:
141:             join.inputs[idx] = Project(join_input, new_input_cols)
142: 
143:     # Replace the original columns with the new columns.
144:     join._columns = new_columns
145:     return join
146: 
147: 
148: def merge_adjacent_projects(node: RelationalRoot | Project) -> RelationalNode:
149:     """
150:     Attempts to merge the projection input of a root/projection node into it,
151:     repeatedly if possible, or returns the original node if not possible. At
152:     the end, if the node is a project on top of a scan that only does
153:     column pruning/renaming, it is pushed into the scan.
154: 
155:     Args:
156:         `node`: The current node of the relational tree, which must be a root
157:         or projection.
158: 
159:     Returns:
160:         The transformed version of `node` with the projection input merged into
161:         it, or the original node if the merging is not possible.
162:     """
163:     expr: RelationalExpression
164:     new_expr: RelationalExpression
165:     # Repeatedly attempt the merging protocol until the input of the node is
166:     # no longer a projection.
167:     while isinstance(node.input, Project):
168:         child_project: Project = node.input
169:         if isinstance(node, RelationalRoot):
170:             # The columns of the projection can be sucked into the root
171:             # above it if they are all pass-through/renamings, or if there
172:             # is no convolution created (only allowed if there are no
173:             # ordering expressions).
174:             if all(
175:                 isinstance(expr, ColumnReference)
176:                 for expr in child_project.columns.values()
177:             ) or (
178:                 len(node.orderings) == 0
179:                 and merging_doesnt_create_convolution(
180:                     node.columns, child_project.columns
181:                 )
182:             ):
183:                 # Replace all column references in the root's columns with
184:                 # the expressions from the child projection..
185:                 for idx, (name, expr) in enumerate(node.ordered_columns):
186:                     new_expr = transpose_expression(expr, child_project.columns)
187:                     node.columns[name] = new_expr
188:                     node.ordered_columns[idx] = (name, new_expr)
189:                 # Do the same with the sort expressions.
190:                 for idx, sort_info in enumerate(node.orderings):
191:                     new_expr = transpose_expression(
192:                         sort_info.expr, child_project.columns
193:                     )
194:                     node.orderings[idx] = ExpressionSortInfo(
195:                         new_expr, sort_info.ascending, sort_info.nulls_first
196:                     )
197:                 # Delete the child projection from the tree, replacing it
198:                 # with its input.
199:                 node._input = child_project.input
200:             else:
201:                 # Otherwise, halt the merging process since it is no longer
202:                 # possible to merge the children of this root into it.
203:                 break
204:         elif isinstance(node, Project):
205:             # The columns of the projection can be sucked into the
206:             # projection above it if they are all pass-through/renamings
207:             # or if there is no convolution created.
208:             if all(
209:                 isinstance(expr, ColumnReference)
210:                 for expr in child_project.columns.values()
211:             ) or merging_doesnt_create_convolution(node.columns, child_project.columns):
212:                 for name, expr in node.columns.items():
213:                     new_expr = transpose_expression(expr, child_project.columns)
214:                     node.columns[name] = new_expr
215:                 # Delete the child projection from the tree, replacing it
216:                 # with its input.
217:                 node._input = child_project.input
218:             else:
219:                 # Otherwise, halt the merging process since it is no longer
220:                 # possible to merge the children of this project into it.
221:                 break
222:     # Final round: if there is a project on top of a scan that only does
223:     # column pruning/renaming, just push it into the scan.
224:     if (
225:         isinstance(node, Project)
226:         and isinstance(node.input, Scan)
227:         and all(isinstance(expr, ColumnReference) for expr in node.columns.values())
228:     ):
229:         return node.input.copy(
230:             columns={
231:                 name: transpose_expression(expr, node.input.columns)
232:                 for name, expr in node.columns.items()
233:             },
234:         )
235:     return node
236: 
237: 
238: def merge_projects(node: RelationalNode) -> RelationalNode:
239:     """
240:     Merge adjacent projections when beneficial.
241: 
242:     Args:
243:         `node`: The current node of the relational tree.
244: 
245:     Returns:
246:         The transformed version of `node` with adjacent projections merged
247:         into one when the top project never references nodes from the bottom
248:         more than once.
249:     """
250:     # If there is a project on top of a join, attempt to push it down into the
251:     # inputs of the join.
252:     if isinstance(node, Project) and isinstance(node.input, Join):
253:         node = project_join_transpose(node)
254: 
255:     # Recursively invoke the procedure on all inputs to the node.
256:     node = node.copy(inputs=[merge_projects(input) for input in node.inputs])
257: 
258:     # Invoke the main merging step if the current node is a root/projection,
259:     # potentially multiple times if the projection below it that gets deleted
260:     # reveals another projection below it.
261:     if isinstance(node, (RelationalRoot, Project)):
262:         node = merge_adjacent_projects(node)
263: 
264:     return node
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/conversion/README.md
````markdown
 1: # Conversion
 2: 
 3: This subdirectory of the PyDough directory deals with the conversion of PyDough expressions into various intermediate representations.
 4: 
 5: The conversion module provides functionality to convert qualified DAG (QDAG) nodes into hybrid nodes and then into relational nodes.
 6: 
 7: ## Hybrid Tree
 8: 
 9: The `HybridTree` is an intermediate representation used to bridge the gap between QDAG nodes and relational nodes. The components of this structure, and the process to convert QDAG nodes into it, are defined in [hybrid_tree.py](hybrid_tree.py)
10: 
11: 
12: Hybrid tree instances are structured as a linear chain linked to one another as predecessors/successors, and each hybrid tree instance is composed of a pipeline of hybrid operation instances. Each hybrid operation builds on the previous one, and the first one in the pipeline builds on the result from the last element in the pipeline of the predecessor. Steps from one hybrid tree down to its successor correspond to moving into a child context, whereas operations in the same pipeline operate on the same context by augmenting it.
13: 
14: ### Hybrid Expressions
15: 
16: Hybrid expressions are used to represent various types of expressions within the hybrid tree. Some notable classes include:
17: 
18: - `HybridLiteralExpr`: Represents a literal value.
19: - `HybridColumnExpr`: Represents a column reference.
20: - `HybridFunctionExpr`: Represents a regular or aggregate function call.
21: - `HybridWindowExpr`: represents a window function call.
22: - `HybridRefExpr`: Represents a reference to another expression.
23: - `HybridBackRefExpr`: Represents a reference to another hybrid expression that exists in one of the successors of the current hybrid tree.
24: - `HybridChildRefExpr`: Represents a reference to another hybrid expression that exists in one of the child connections of the current hybrid tree.
25: - `HybridCorrelExpr`: Represents a reference to another hybrid expression that exists in the parent hybrid tree containing the current hybrid tree as a child subtree. These references are correlated because they mean that one side of a join will depend on logic from the other side.
26: 
27: ### Hybrid Connections
28: 
29: Hybrid connections represent the relationships between different parts of the hybrid tree. They are used to handle subcollection accesses and aggregations. Its fields are as follows:
30: 
31: - `parent`: The `HybridTree` that the connection exists within.
32: - `subtree`: The `HybridTree` corresponding to the child itself, starting from the bottom.
33: - `connection_type`: An enum indicating which connection type is being used.
34: - `required_steps`: An index indicating which step in the pipeline must be completed before the child can be defined.
35: - `aggs`: A mapping of aggregation calls made onto expressions relative to the context of `subtree`.
36: 
37: The `ConnectionType` eEnum describes how a hybrid tree is connected to a child tree. It has the following values:
38: 
39: - `SINGULAR`: The child should be 1:1 with regards to the parent.
40: - `AGGREGATION`: The child is being accessed for the purposes of aggregating its columns.
41: - `NDISTINCT`: The child is being accessed for the purposes of counting how many distinct elements it has.
42: - `SEMI`: The child is being used as a semi-join.
43: - `SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH`: A variant of `SINGULAR` that can use an INNER join instead of a LEFT join.
44: - `AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH`: A variant of `AGGREGATION` that can use an INNER join instead of a LEFT join.
45: - `NDISTINCT_ONLY_MATCH`: A variant of `NDISTINCT` that can use an INNER join instead of a LEFT join.
46: - `ANTI`: The child is being used as an anti-join.
47: - `NO_MATCH_SINGULAR`: A variant of `SINGULAR` that replaces all of the child references with NULL.
48: - `NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION`: A variant of `AGGREGATION` that replaces all of the aggregation outputs with NULL.
49: - `NO_MATCH_NDISTINCT`: A variant of `NDISTINCT` that replaces the NDISTINCT output with 0.
50: 
51: ### Hybrid Operations
52: 
53: Hybrid operations represent the various operations that can be performed within the hybrid tree. Some notable classes include:
54: 
55: - `HybridOperation`: Base class for all hybrid operations.
56: - `HybridRoot`: Represents the root context.
57: - `HybridCollectionAccess`: Represents accessing a collection.
58: - `HybridFilter`: Represents a filter operation.
59: - `HybridCalc`: Represents a calculation operation.
60: - `HybridLimit`: Represents a limit operation.
61: - `HybridPartition`: Represents a partition operation.
62: - `HybridPartitionChild`: Represents accessing the data of a partition as a child.
63: - `HybridNoop`: Represents a do-nothing operation that propagates all of the data from the previous operation without any change.
64: - `HybridChildPullup`: Represents an operation that accesses all of the data from a child hybrid tree as if one of its levels were the current level and its ancestors were the current levels ancestors, while the bottom level remain as child references.
65: 
66: ## Hybrid De-Correlation
67: 
68: The file [hybrid_decorrelater.py](hybrid_decorrelater.py) contains the logic used to hunt for `HybridCorrelExpr` outside of a semi/anti join and de-correlates them by snapshotting the hybrid tree and attaching the snapshot copy to the top of the child subtree, thus turning the correlated reference into a back reference. Also, for only-match patterns, replaces the original logic that was snapshotted with a single `HybridChildPullup` to avoid re-computing the same logic twice.
69: 
70: ## Relational Conversion
71: 
72: The methodology for converting hybrid nodes into relational nodes is implemented in [relational_converter.py](relational_converter.py). The main steps involved in this process are:
73: 
74: 1. **Preprocessing**: The QDAG node is preprocessed to ensure that all necessary terms are included in the final output.
75: 2. **Hybrid Conversion**: The QDAG node is converted into a hybrid tree structure.
76: 3. **Relational Translation**: The hybrid nodes are recursively converted into relational nodes by starting at the last pipeline operator of the bottom of the hybrid tree, working backwards, and building onto the previous result. The accumulated result is both the relational tree of the answer so far and a mapping of hybrid expressions to the corresponding column in the answer that corresponds to their value. Operations such as filter or limit just wrap the previous result in another relational node, but several other translations have more steps:
77:    - When stepping down from one level of the HybridTree to the next level, e.g. by accessing a subcollection, the result of the previous level is inner joined to reach the new level, and all expressions from the previous level are back-shifted up by 1.
78:    - All child references are resolved by calculating the relational translation of the child and joining it onto the current result so that its expressions are accessible as child expressions. The type of join depends on the type of `HybridConnection`, but the result is that every row in the current relation matches to at most 1 row in the child relational tree, either because it is already guaranteed to be singular or because it has been aggregated in a manner that ensures so.
79: 4. **Finalization**: The final relational structure is created, and extra optimizations are run such as filter pushdown and column pruning.
80: 
81: ## Hybrid De-Correlation
82: 
83: The file [filter_pushdown.py](filter_pushdown.py) contains the logic used to push filters further down into the relational tree.
````

````python
 122:     def make_null_column(self, relation: RelationalNode) -> ColumnReference:

 141:                 isinstance(existing_val, LiteralExpression)
 142:                 and existing_val.value is None

 287:         into a relational expression. The columns from the RHS are assumed to
 288:         be ordinary references/back-references within the condition expr, while
 289:         columns from the LHS are assumed to be `HybridSidedRefExpr`, denoting
 290:         that they come from the parent.
 291: 
 292:         Args:
 293:             `condition`: the condition to be converted.
 294:             `lhs_result`: the TranslationOutput for the LHS of the join.
 295:             `rhs_result`: the TranslationOutput for the RHS of the join.
 296:             `lhs_alias`: the alias used to refer to the LHS of the join.
 297:             `rhs_alias`: the alias used to refer to the RHS of the join.
 298: 
 299:         Returns:
 300:             The converted relational expression for the join condition.
 301:         """
 302:         result: RelationalExpression
 303:         inputs: list[RelationalExpression]
 304:         partition_inputs: list[RelationalExpression]
 305:         order_inputs: list[ExpressionSortInfo]
 306:         match condition:
 307:             case HybridSidedRefExpr():
 308:                 # For sided references, access the referenced expression from
 309:                 # the lhs output.
 310:                 result = self.translate_expression(
 311:                     HybridRefExpr(condition.name, condition.typ), lhs_result
 312:                 )
 313:                 return self.rename_inputs(result, lhs_alias)
 314:             case HybridFunctionExpr():
 315:                 # For function calls, recursively convert the arguments, then
 316:                 # build a relational function call expression.
 317:                 inputs = [
 318:                     self.build_general_join_condition(
 319:                         arg, lhs_result, rhs_result, lhs_alias, rhs_alias
 320:                     )
 321:                     for arg in condition.args
 322:                 ]
 323:                 return CallExpression(condition.operator, condition.typ, inputs)
 324:             case HybridWindowExpr():
 325:                 # For window function calls, do the same as regular funcitons
 326:                 # but also convert the partition/order inputs.
 327:                 inputs = [
 328:                     self.build_general_join_condition(
 329:                         arg, lhs_result, rhs_result, lhs_alias, rhs_alias
 330:                     )
 331:                     for arg in condition.args
 332:                 ]
 333:                 partition_inputs = [
 334:                     self.build_general_join_condition(
 335:                         arg, lhs_result, rhs_result, lhs_alias, rhs_alias
 336:                     )
 337:                     for arg in condition.partition_args
 338:                 ]
 339:                 order_inputs = [
 340:                     ExpressionSortInfo(
 341:                         self.build_general_join_condition(
 342:                             order_arg.expr, lhs_result, rhs_result, lhs_alias, rhs_alias
 343:                         ),
 344:                         order_arg.asc,
 345:                         order_arg.na_first,
 346:                     )
 347:                     for order_arg in condition.order_args
 348:                 ]
 349:                 return WindowCallExpression(
 350:                     condition.window_func,
 351:                     condition.typ,
 352:                     inputs,
 353:                     partition_inputs,
 354:                     order_inputs,
 355:                     condition.kwargs,
 356:                 )
 357:             case _:
 358:                 # For all other expressions, convert regularly using the RHS
 359:                 # as the context to pull columns from.
 360:                 result = self.translate_expression(condition, rhs_result)
 361:                 return self.rename_inputs(result, rhs_alias)
 362: 
 363:     def rename_inputs(
 364:         self, expr: RelationalExpression, alias: str | None
 365:     ) -> RelationalExpression:
 366:         """
 367:         Recursively transforms a relational expression and any of its contents
 368:         so that all column references have an input alias added to them.
 369: 
 370:         Args:
 371:             `expr`: the expression to be transformed.
 372:             `alias`: the alias to be added to the column references.
 373: 
 374:         Returns:
 375:             The transformed expression with the input alias added to all
 376:             column references.
 377:         """
 378:         inputs: list[RelationalExpression]
 379:         partition_inputs: list[RelationalExpression]
 380:         order_inputs: list[ExpressionSortInfo]
 381:         match expr:
 382:             case WindowCallExpression():
 383:                 inputs = [self.rename_inputs(arg, alias) for arg in expr.inputs]
 384:                 partition_inputs = [
 385:                     self.rename_inputs(arg, alias) for arg in expr.partition_inputs
 386:                 ]
 387:                 order_inputs = [
 388:                     ExpressionSortInfo(
 389:                         self.rename_inputs(order_arg.expr, alias),
 390:                         order_arg.ascending,
 391:                         order_arg.nulls_first,
 392:                     )
 393:                     for order_arg in expr.order_inputs
 394:                 ]
 395:                 return WindowCallExpression(
 396:                     expr.op,
 397:                     expr.data_type,
 398:                     inputs,
 399:                     partition_inputs,
 400:                     order_inputs,
 401:                     expr.kwargs,
 402:                 )
 403:             case CallExpression():
 404:                 return CallExpression(
 405:                     expr.op,
 406:                     expr.data_type,
 407:                     [self.rename_inputs(arg, alias) for arg in expr.inputs],
 408:                 )
 409:             case ColumnReference():
 410:                 return ColumnReference(expr.name, expr.data_type, alias)
 411:             case LiteralExpression() | CorrelatedReference():
 412:                 return expr
 413:             case _:
 414:                 raise NotImplementedError(
 415:                     f"Unrecognized expression type: {expr.__class__.__name__}"
 416:                 )
 417: 
 418:     def join_outputs(
 419:         self,
 420:         lhs_result: TranslationOutput,
 421:         rhs_result: TranslationOutput,
 422:         join_type: JoinType,
 423:         join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] | None,
 424:         join_cond: HybridExpr | None,
 425:         child_idx: int | None,
 426:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 427:         """
 428:         Handles the joining of a parent context onto a child context.
 429: 
 430:         Args:
 431:             `lhs_result`: the TranslationOutput payload storing containing the
 432:             relational structure for the parent context.
 433:             `rhs_result`: the TranslationOutput payload storing containing the
 434:             relational structure for the child context.
 435:             `join_type` the type of join to be used to connect `lhs_result`
 436:             onto `rhs_result`.
 437:             `join_keys`: a list of tuples in the form `(lhs_key, rhs_key)` that
 438:             represent the equi-join keys used for the join from either side.
 439:             This can be None if the `join_cond` is provided instead.
 440:             `join_cond`: a generic join condition that can be used to join the
 441:             lhs and rhs, where correlated references refer to terms from the
 442:             lhs. This can be None if the `join_keys` is provided instead.
 443:             `child_idx`: if None, means that the join is being used to step
 444:             down from a parent into its child. If non-none, it means the join
 445:             is being used to bring a child's elements into the same context as
 446:             the parent, and the `child_idx` is the index of that child.
 447: 
 448:         Returns:
 449:             The TranslationOutput payload containing the relational structure
 450:             created by joining `lhs_result` and `lhs_result` in the manner
 451:             described.
 452:         """
 453:         out_columns: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference] = {}
 454:         join_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {}
 455: 
 456:         assert (join_keys is None) != (join_cond is None)
 457: 
 458:         # Special case: if the lhs is an EmptySingleton, just return the RHS,
 459:         # decorated if needed.
 460:         if isinstance(lhs_result.relational_node, EmptySingleton):
 461:             if child_idx is None:
 462:                 return rhs_result
 463:             else:
 464:                 for expr, col_ref in rhs_result.expressions.items():
 465:                     if isinstance(expr, HybridRefExpr):
 466:                         child_ref: HybridExpr = HybridChildRefExpr(
 467:                             expr.name, child_idx, expr.typ
 468:                         )
 469:                         out_columns[child_ref] = col_ref
 470:                 return TranslationOutput(rhs_result.relational_node, out_columns)
 471: 
 472:         # Create the join node so we know what aliases it uses, but leave
 473:         # the condition as always-True and the output columns empty for now.
 474:         # The condition & output columns will be filled in later.
 475:         out_rel: Join = Join(
 476:             [lhs_result.relational_node, rhs_result.relational_node],
 477:             [LiteralExpression(True, BooleanType())],
 478:             [join_type],
 479:             join_columns,
 480:             correl_name=lhs_result.correlated_name,
 481:         )
 482:         input_aliases: list[str | None] = out_rel.default_input_aliases
 483: 
 484:         # Build the corresponding (lhs_key == rhs_key) conditions
 485:         cond_terms: list[RelationalExpression] = []
 486:         if join_keys is not None:
 487:             for lhs_key, rhs_key in join_keys:
 488:                 lhs_key_column: ColumnReference = lhs_result.expressions[
 489:                     lhs_key
 490:                 ].with_input(input_aliases[0])
 491:                 rhs_key_column: ColumnReference = rhs_result.expressions[
 492:                     rhs_key
 493:                 ].with_input(input_aliases[1])
 494:                 cond: RelationalExpression = CallExpression(
 495:                     pydop.EQU, BooleanType(), [lhs_key_column, rhs_key_column]
 496:                 )
 497:                 cond_terms.append(cond)
 498:             out_rel.conditions[0] = RelationalExpression.form_conjunction(cond_terms)
 499:         else:
 500:             assert join_cond is not None
 501:             out_rel.conditions[0] = self.build_general_join_condition(
 502:                 join_cond, lhs_result, rhs_result, input_aliases[0], input_aliases[1]
 503:             )
 504: 
 505:         # Propagate all of the references from the left hand side. If the join
 506:         # is being done to step down from a parent into a child then promote
 507:         # the back levels of the reference by 1. If the join is being done to
 508:         # pull elements from the child context into the current context, then
 509:         # maintain them as-is.
 510:         for expr in lhs_result.expressions:
 511:             existing_ref: ColumnReference = lhs_result.expressions[expr]
 512:             join_columns[existing_ref.name] = existing_ref.with_input(input_aliases[0])
 513:             if child_idx is None:
 514:                 shifted_expr: HybridExpr | None = expr.shift_back(1)
 515:                 if shifted_expr is not None:
 516:                     out_columns[shifted_expr] = existing_ref
 517:             else:
 518:                 out_columns[expr] = existing_ref
 519: 
 520:         # Skip the following steps for semi/anti joins
 521:         if join_type not in (JoinType.SEMI, JoinType.ANTI):
 522:             # Add all of the new references from the right hand side (in
 523:             # alphabetical order).
 524:             expr_refs: list[tuple[HybridExpr, ColumnReference]] = list(
 525:                 rhs_result.expressions.items()
 526:             )
 527:             expr_refs.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1].name)
 528:             for expr, old_reference in expr_refs:
 529:                 # If the join is being done to pull elements from the child context
 530:                 # into the current context, then promote the references to child
 531:                 # references.
 532:                 if child_idx is not None:
 533:                     if not isinstance(expr, HybridRefExpr):
 534:                         continue
 535:                     expr = HybridChildRefExpr(expr.name, child_idx, expr.typ)
 536:                 # Names from the LHS are maintained as-is, so if there is a
 537:                 # an overlapping name in the RHS, a new name must be found.
 538:                 old_name: str = old_reference.name
 539:                 new_name: str = old_name
 540:                 while new_name in join_columns:
 541:                     new_name = f"{old_name}_{self.dummy_idx}"
 542:                     self.dummy_idx += 1
 543:                 new_reference: ColumnReference = ColumnReference(
 544:                     new_name, old_reference.data_type
 545:                 )
 546:                 join_columns[new_name] = old_reference.with_input(input_aliases[1])
 547:                 out_columns[expr] = new_reference
 548: 
 549:         return TranslationOutput(out_rel, out_columns)
 550: 
 551:     def apply_aggregations(
 552:         self,
 553:         connection: HybridConnection,
 554:         context: TranslationOutput,
 555:         agg_keys: list[HybridExpr],
 556:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 557:         """
 558:         Transforms the TranslationOutput payload from translating the
 559:         subtree of HyrbidConnection by grouping it using the specified
 560:         aggregation keys then deriving the aggregations in the `aggs` mapping
 561:         of the HybridAggregation.
 562: 
 563:         Args:
 564:             `connection`: the HybridConnection whose subtree is being derived.
 565:             This connection must be of an aggregation type.
 566:             `context`: the TranslationOutput being augmented.
 567:             `agg_keys`: the list of expressions corresponding to the keys
 568:             that should be used to aggregate `context`.
 569: 
 570:         Returns:
 571:             The TranslationOutput payload for `context` wrapped in an
 572:             aggregation.
 573:         """
 574:         assert connection.connection_type in (
 575:             ConnectionType.AGGREGATION,
 576:             ConnectionType.AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH,
 577:             ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION,
 578:         )
 579:         out_columns: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference] = {}
 580:         keys: dict[str, ColumnReference] = {}
 581:         aggregations: dict[str, CallExpression] = {}
 582:         used_names: set[str] = set()
 583:         # First, propagate all key columns into the output, and add them to
 584:         # the keys mapping of the aggregate.
 585:         for agg_key in agg_keys:
 586:             agg_key_expr = self.translate_expression(agg_key, context)
 587:             assert isinstance(agg_key_expr, ColumnReference)
 588:             out_columns[agg_key] = agg_key_expr
 589:             keys[agg_key_expr.name] = agg_key_expr
 590:             used_names.add(agg_key_expr.name)
 591:         # Then, add all of the agg calls to the aggregations mapping of the
 592:         # the aggregate, and add references to the corresponding dummy-names
 593:         # to the output.
 594:         for agg_name, agg_func in connection.aggs.items():
 595:             # Ensure there is no name conflict
 596:             in_agg_name: str = agg_name
 597:             if agg_name in keys:
 598:                 agg_name = self.get_column_name(agg_name, used_names)
 599:             used_names.add(agg_name)
 600:             col_ref: ColumnReference = ColumnReference(agg_name, agg_func.typ)
 601:             hybrid_expr: HybridExpr = HybridRefExpr(in_agg_name, agg_func.typ)
 602:             out_columns[hybrid_expr] = col_ref
 603:             args: list[RelationalExpression] = [
 604:                 self.translate_expression(arg, context) for arg in agg_func.args
 605:             ]
 606:             aggregations[agg_name] = CallExpression(
 607:                 agg_func.operator, agg_func.typ, args
 608:             )
 609:         out_rel: RelationalNode = Aggregate(context.relational_node, keys, aggregations)
 610:         return TranslationOutput(out_rel, out_columns)
 611: 
 612:     def handle_children(
 613:         self,
 614:         context: TranslationOutput,
 615:         hybrid: HybridTree,
 616:         pipeline_idx: int,
 617:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 618:         """
 619:         Post-processes a TranslationOutput payload by finding any children of
 620:         the current hybrid tree level that are newly able to be defined, and
 621:         bringing them into context via the handler.
 622: 
 623:         Args:
 624:             `context`: the TranslationOutput being augmented, if one exists.
 625:             `hybrid`: the current level of the HybridTree.
 626:             `pipeline_idx`: the index of the element in the pipeline of
 627:             `hybrid` that has just been defined, meaning any children that
 628:             depend on it can now also be defined.
 629:             `partition_child`: if True, only translate the input argument for
 630:             a partition, not any other children.
 631: 
 632:         Returns:
 633:             The augmented version of `context` with any children that are
 634:             possible to define brought into context.
 635:         """
 636:         for child_idx, child in enumerate(hybrid.children):
 637:             if (
 638:                 isinstance(hybrid.pipeline[0], HybridChildPullUp)
 639:                 and hybrid.pipeline[0].child_idx == child_idx
 640:             ):
 641:                 continue
 642:             if child.required_steps == pipeline_idx:
 643:                 self.stack.append(context)
 644:                 child_output = self.rel_translation(
 645:                     child.subtree, len(child.subtree.pipeline) - 1
 646:                 )
 647:                 self.stack.pop()
 648:                 child_expr: HybridExpr
 649:                 match child.connection_type:
 650:                     case (
 651:                         ConnectionType.SINGULAR
 652:                         | ConnectionType.SINGULAR_ONLY_MATCH
 653:                         | ConnectionType.AGGREGATION
 654:                         | ConnectionType.AGGREGATION_ONLY_MATCH
 655:                         | ConnectionType.SEMI
 656:                         | ConnectionType.ANTI
 657:                     ):
 658:                         if child.connection_type.is_aggregation:
 659:                             assert child.subtree.agg_keys is not None
 660:                             child_output = self.apply_aggregations(
 661:                                 child, child_output, child.subtree.agg_keys
 662:                             )
 663:                         context = self.join_outputs(
 664:                             context,
 665:                             child_output,
 666:                             child.connection_type.join_type,
 667:                             child.subtree.join_keys,
 668:                             child.subtree.general_join_condition,
 669:                             child_idx,
 670:                         )
 671:                     case (
 672:                         ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_SINGULAR
 673:                         | ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION
 674:                     ):
 675:                         assert child_idx is not None
 676:                         context = self.join_outputs(
 677:                             context,
 678:                             child_output,
 679:                             child.connection_type.join_type,
 680:                             child.subtree.join_keys,
 681:                             child.subtree.general_join_condition,
 682:                             child_idx,
 683:                         )
 684:                         # Map every child_idx reference from child_output to null
 685:                         null_column: ColumnReference = self.make_null_column(
 686:                             context.relational_node
 687:                         )
 688:                         for expr in child_output.expressions:
 689:                             if isinstance(expr, HybridRefExpr):
 690:                                 child_expr = HybridChildRefExpr(
 691:                                     expr.name, child_idx, expr.typ
 692:                                 )
 693:                                 context.expressions[child_expr] = null_column
 694:                         # For aggregations, map every child_idx reference to the
 695:                         # `aggs` list to null
 696:                         if child.connection_type == ConnectionType.NO_MATCH_AGGREGATION:
 697:                             for agg_name, agg_expr in child.aggs.items():
 698:                                 child_expr = HybridChildRefExpr(
 699:                                     agg_name, child_idx, agg_expr.typ
 700:                                 )
 701:                                 context.expressions[child_expr] = null_column
 702:                     case conn_type:
 703:                         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported connection type {conn_type}")
 704:             # If handling the data for a partition, pull every aggregation key
 705:             # into the current context since it is now accessible as a normal
 706:             # ref instead of a child ref.
 707:             if isinstance(hybrid.pipeline[pipeline_idx], HybridPartition):
 708:                 partition = hybrid.pipeline[pipeline_idx]
 709:                 assert isinstance(partition, HybridPartition)
 710:                 for key_name in partition.key_names:
 711:                     key_expr = partition.terms[key_name]
 712:                     assert isinstance(key_expr, HybridChildRefExpr)
 713:                     hybrid_ref: HybridRefExpr = HybridRefExpr(
 714:                         key_expr.name, key_expr.typ
 715:                     )
 716:                     context.expressions[hybrid_ref] = context.expressions[key_expr]
 717:         return context
 718: 
 719:     def build_simple_table_scan(
 720:         self, node: HybridCollectionAccess
 721:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 722:         """
 723:         Converts an access of a collection into a table scan.
 724: 
 725:         Args:
 726:             `node`: the node corresponding to accessing a collection
 727:             (could be a standalone table collection or subcollection access).
 728: 
 729:         Returns:
 730:             The TranslationOutput payload containing the table scan as well
 731:             as the expression mappings so future references know how to
 732:             access the table columns.
 733:         """
 734:         out_columns: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference] = {}
 735:         scan_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {}
 736:         for expr_name in node.terms:
 737:             hybrid_expr: HybridExpr = node.terms[expr_name]
 738:             scan_ref: RelationalExpression = self.translate_expression(
 739:                 hybrid_expr, None
 740:             )
 741:             assert isinstance(scan_ref, ColumnReference)
 742:             scan_columns[expr_name] = scan_ref
 743:             hybrid_ref: HybridRefExpr = HybridRefExpr(expr_name, hybrid_expr.typ)
 744:             out_ref: ColumnReference = ColumnReference(expr_name, hybrid_expr.typ)
 745:             out_columns[hybrid_ref] = out_ref
 746:         assert isinstance(node.collection.collection, SimpleTableMetadata), (
 747:             f"Expected table collection to correspond to an instance of simple table metadata, found: {node.collection.collection.__class__.__name__}"
 748:         )
 749:         uniqueness: set[frozenset[str]] = set()
 750:         for unique_set in node.collection.collection.unique_properties:
 751:             names: list[str] = (
 752:                 [unique_set] if isinstance(unique_set, str) else unique_set
 753:             )
 754:             real_names: set[str] = set()
 755:             for name in names:
 756:                 expr = scan_columns[name]
 757:                 assert isinstance(expr, ColumnReference)
 758:                 real_names.add(expr.name)
 759:             uniqueness.add(frozenset(real_names))
 760:         answer = Scan(node.collection.collection.table_path, scan_columns, uniqueness)
 761:         return TranslationOutput(answer, out_columns)
 762: 
 763:     def translate_sub_collection(
 764:         self,
 765:         node: HybridCollectionAccess,
 766:         parent: HybridTree,
 767:         context: TranslationOutput,
 768:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 769:         """
 770:         Converts a subcollection access into a join from the parent onto
 771:         a scan of the child.
 772: 
 773:         Args:
 774:             `node`: the node corresponding to the subcollection access.
 775:             `parent`: the hybrid tree of the previous layer that the access
 776:             steps down from.
 777:             `context`: the data structure storing information used by the
 778:             conversion, such as bindings of already translated terms from
 779:             preceding contexts.
 780: 
 781:         Returns:
 782:             The TranslationOutput payload containing an INNER join of the
 783:             relational node for the parent and the table scan of the child.
 784:         """
 785: 
 786:         # First, build the table scan for the collection being stepped into.
 787:         collection_access: CollectionAccess = node.collection
 788:         assert isinstance(collection_access, SubCollection)
 789:         assert isinstance(collection_access.collection, SimpleTableMetadata), (
 790:             f"Expected table collection to correspond to an instance of simple table metadata, found: {collection_access.collection.__class__.__name__}"
 791:         )
 792:         rhs_output: TranslationOutput = self.build_simple_table_scan(node)
 793: 
 794:         join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] | None = None
 795:         join_cond: HybridExpr | None = None
 796:         match collection_access.subcollection_property:
 797:             case SimpleJoinMetadata():
 798:                 join_keys = HybridTranslator.get_subcollection_join_keys(
 799:                     collection_access.subcollection_property,
 800:                     parent.pipeline[-1],
 801:                     node,
 802:                 )
 803:             case GeneralJoinMetadata():
 804:                 assert node.general_condition is not None
 805:                 join_cond = node.general_condition
 806: 
 807:         return self.join_outputs(
 808:             context,
 809:             rhs_output,
 810:             JoinType.INNER,
 811:             join_keys,
 812:             join_cond,
 813:             None,
 814:         )
 815: 
 816:     def translate_child_sub_collection(
 817:         self, node: HybridCollectionAccess
 818:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 819:         """
 820:         Converts a subcollection access, used as the root of a child subtree,
 821:         into a table scan.
 822: 
 823:         Args:
 824:             `connection`: the HybridConnection linking the parent context
 825:             to the child subtree.
 826:             `node`: the collection access that is the root of the child
 827:             subtree.
 828: 
 829:         Returns:
 830:             The TranslationOutput payload corresponding to the access of the
 831:             child collection.
 832:         """
 833:         # First, build the table scan for the collection being stepped into.
 834:         collection_access: CollectionAccess = node.collection
 835:         assert isinstance(collection_access, SubCollection)
 836:         assert isinstance(collection_access.collection, SimpleTableMetadata), (
 837:             f"Expected table collection to correspond to an instance of simple table metadata, found: {collection_access.collection.__class__.__name__}"
 838:         )
 839:         result: TranslationOutput = self.build_simple_table_scan(node)
 840:         return result
 841: 
 842:     def translate_partition(
 843:         self,
 844:         node: HybridPartition,
 845:         context: TranslationOutput,
 846:         hybrid: HybridTree,
 847:         pipeline_idx: int,
 848:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 849:         """
 850:         Converts a partition into the correct context with access to the
 851:         aggregated child inputs.
 852: 
 853:         Args:
 854:             `node`: the node corresponding to the partition being derived.
 855:             `context`: the data structure storing information used by the
 856:             conversion, such as bindings of already translated terms from
 857:             preceding contexts.
 858:             `hybrid`: the current level of the hybrid tree to be derived,
 859:             including all levels before it.
 860:             `pipeline_idx`: the index of the operation in the pipeline of the
 861:             current level that is to be derived, as well as all operations
 862:             preceding it in the pipeline.
 863: 
 864:         Returns:
 865:             The TranslationOutput payload containing access to the aggregated
 866:             child corresponding to the partition data.
 867:         """
 868:         expressions: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference] = {}
 869:         # Account for the fact that the PARTITION is stepping down a level,
 870:         # without actually joining.
 871:         for expr, ref in context.expressions.items():
 872:             shifted_expr: HybridExpr | None = expr.shift_back(1)
 873:             if shifted_expr is not None:
 874:                 expressions[shifted_expr] = ref
 875:         # Return the input data, which will be wrapped in an aggregation when
 876:         # handle_children is called on the output
 877:         result: TranslationOutput = TranslationOutput(
 878:             context.relational_node, expressions
 879:         )
 880:         return result
 881: 
 882:     def translate_filter(
 883:         self,
 884:         node: HybridFilter,
 885:         context: TranslationOutput,
 886:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 887:         """
 888:         Converts a filter into a relational Filter node on top of its child.
 889: 
 890:         Args:
 891:             `node`: the node corresponding to the filter being derived.
 892:             `context`: the data structure storing information used by the
 893:             conversion, such as bindings of already translated terms from
 894:             preceding contexts.
 895: 
 896:         Returns:
 897:             The TranslationOutput payload containing a FILTER on top of
 898:             the relational node for the parent to derive any additional terms.
 899:         """
 900:         # Keep all existing columns.
 901:         kept_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {
 902:             name: ColumnReference(name, context.relational_node.columns[name].data_type)
 903:             for name in context.relational_node.columns
 904:         }
 905:         condition: RelationalExpression = self.translate_expression(
 906:             node.condition, context
 907:         )
 908:         out_rel: Filter = Filter(context.relational_node, condition, kept_columns)
 909:         return TranslationOutput(out_rel, context.expressions)
 910: 
 911:     def translate_limit(
 912:         self,
 913:         node: HybridLimit,
 914:         context: TranslationOutput,
 915:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 916:         """
 917:         Converts a HybridLimit into a relational Limit node on top of its child.
 918: 
 919:         Args:
 920:             `node`: the node corresponding to the limit being derived.
 921:             `context`: the data structure storing information used by the
 922:             conversion, such as bindings of already translated terms from
 923:             preceding contexts. Can be omitted in certain contexts, such as
 924:             when deriving a table scan or literal.
 925: 
 926:         Returns:
 927:             The TranslationOutput payload containing a Limit on top of
 928:             the relational node for the parent to derive any additional terms.
 929:         """
 930:         # Keep all existing columns.
 931:         kept_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {
 932:             name: ColumnReference(name, context.relational_node.columns[name].data_type)
 933:             for name in context.relational_node.columns
 934:         }
 935:         limit_expr: LiteralExpression = LiteralExpression(
 936:             node.records_to_keep, Int64Type()
 937:         )
 938:         orderings: list[ExpressionSortInfo] = make_relational_ordering(
 939:             node.orderings, context.expressions
 940:         )
 941:         out_rel: Limit = Limit(
 942:             context.relational_node, limit_expr, kept_columns, orderings
 943:         )
 944:         return TranslationOutput(out_rel, context.expressions)
 945: 
 946:     def translate_calculate(
 947:         self,
 948:         node: HybridCalculate,
 949:         context: TranslationOutput,
 950:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 951:         """
 952:         Converts a CALCULATE into a project on top of its child to derive
 953:         additional terms.
 954: 
 955:         Args:
 956:             `node`: the node corresponding to the CALCULATE being derived.
 957:             `context`: the data structure storing information used by the
 958:             conversion, such as bindings of already translated terms from
 959:             preceding contexts and the corresponding relational node.
 960: 
 961:         Returns:
 962:             The TranslationOutput payload containing a PROJECT that propagates
 963:             any existing terms top of
 964:             the relational node for the parent to derive any additional terms.
 965:         """
 966:         proj_columns: dict[str, RelationalExpression] = {}
 967:         out_columns: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference] = {}
 968:         # Propagate all of the existing columns.
 969:         for name in context.relational_node.columns:
 970:             proj_columns[name] = ColumnReference(
 971:                 name, context.relational_node.columns[name].data_type
 972:             )
 973:         for expr in context.expressions:
 974:             out_columns[expr] = context.expressions[expr].with_input(None)
 975:         # Populate every expression into the project's columns by translating
 976:         # it relative to the input context.
 977:         for name in node.new_expressions:
 978:             name = node.renamings.get(name, name)
 979:             hybrid_expr: HybridExpr = node.terms[name]
 980:             ref_expr: HybridRefExpr = HybridRefExpr(name, hybrid_expr.typ)
 981:             rel_expr: RelationalExpression = self.translate_expression(
 982:                 hybrid_expr, context
 983:             )
 984:             # Ensure the name of the new column is not already being used. If
 985:             # it is, choose a new name. The new name will be the original name
 986:             # with a numerical index appended to it.
 987:             if name in proj_columns and proj_columns[name] != rel_expr:
 988:                 name = self.get_column_name(name, proj_columns)
 989:             proj_columns[name] = rel_expr
 990:             out_columns[ref_expr] = ColumnReference(name, rel_expr.data_type)
 991:         out_rel: Project = Project(context.relational_node, proj_columns)
 992:         return TranslationOutput(out_rel, out_columns)
 993: 
 994:     def translate_partition_child(
 995:         self,
 996:         node: HybridPartitionChild,
 997:         context: TranslationOutput | None,
 998:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
 999:         """
1000:         Converts a step into the child of a PARTITION node into a join between
1001:         the aggregated partitions versus the data that was originally being
1002:         partitioned.
1003: 
1004:         Args:
1005:             `node`: the node corresponding to the partition child access.
1006:             `context`: the data structure storing information used by the
1007:             conversion, such as bindings of already translated terms from
1008:             preceding contexts.
1009: 
1010:         Returns:
1011:             The TranslationOutput payload containing expressions for both the
1012:             aggregated partitions and the original partitioned data.
1013:         """
1014:         child_output: TranslationOutput = self.rel_translation(
1015:             node.subtree, len(node.subtree.pipeline) - 1
1016:         )
1017: 
1018:         if context is None:
1019:             return child_output
1020: 
1021:         # Special case: when the context is the just-partitioned data, just
1022:         # return the child without bothering to join them.
1023:         if (
1024:             isinstance(context.relational_node, Aggregate)
1025:             and len(context.relational_node.aggregations) == 0
1026:         ):
1027:             new_expressions: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference] = dict(
1028:                 child_output.expressions
1029:             )
1030:             for expr, column_ref in child_output.expressions.items():
1031:                 shifted_expr: HybridExpr | None = expr.shift_back(1)
1032:                 if shifted_expr is not None:
1033:                     new_expressions[shifted_expr] = column_ref
1034:             return TranslationOutput(child_output.relational_node, new_expressions)
1035: 
1036:         join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] = []
1037:         assert node.subtree.agg_keys is not None
1038:         for agg_key in sorted(node.subtree.agg_keys, key=str):
1039:             join_keys.append((agg_key, agg_key))
1040: 
1041:         result = self.join_outputs(
1042:             context,
1043:             child_output,
1044:             JoinType.INNER,
1045:             join_keys,
1046:             None,
1047:             None,
1048:         )
1049:         return result
1050: 
1051:     def translate_child_pullup(self, node: HybridChildPullUp) -> TranslationOutput:
1052:         """
1053:         Converts a HybridChildPullUp node into the relational tree for the
1054:         child it is pulling up, with a change in expressions to reflect the
1055:         different perspective in what each column means.
1056:         """
1057:         # First, translate the child being pulled up
1058:         subtree: HybridTree = node.child.subtree
1059:         child_result: TranslationOutput = self.rel_translation(
1060:             subtree, len(subtree.pipeline) - 1
1061:         )
1062: 
1063:         # Define the new expressions list differently depending on whether the
1064:         # child being pulled up was being aggregating or not.
1065:         new_expressions: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference] = {}
1066:         local_ref: HybridExpr
1067:         child_ref: HybridExpr
1068:         if node.child.connection_type.is_aggregation:
1069:             # If aggregating, first wrap the child relational node in an
1070:             # aggregate, then rephrase all of the aggregation calls to be child
1071:             # references.
1072:             assert node.child.subtree.agg_keys is not None
1073:             child_result = self.apply_aggregations(
1074:                 node.child, child_result, node.child.subtree.agg_keys
1075:             )
1076:             for agg_name, agg_call in node.child.aggs.items():
1077:                 child_ref = HybridChildRefExpr(agg_name, node.child_idx, agg_call.typ)
1078:                 local_ref = HybridRefExpr(agg_name, agg_call.typ)
1079:                 new_expressions[child_ref] = child_result.expressions[local_ref]
1080:         else:
1081:             # Otherwise, just rephrase all of the columns to be child references.
1082:             for child_name, child_term in node.child.subtree.pipeline[-1].terms.items():
1083:                 local_ref = HybridChildRefExpr(
1084:                     child_name, node.child_idx, child_term.typ
1085:                 )
1086:                 child_ref = HybridRefExpr(child_name, child_term.typ)
1087:                 new_expressions[local_ref] = child_result.expressions[child_ref]
1088: 
1089:         # For each expression that is being defined via pullup, map it to the
1090:         # corresponding expression within the child.
1091:         for local_ref, child_ref in node.pullup_remapping.items():
1092:             new_expressions[local_ref] = child_result.expressions[child_ref]
1093: 
1094:         # Build the new output with the child relational tree and the new
1095:         # expressions mapping
1096:         return TranslationOutput(child_result.relational_node, new_expressions)
1097: 
1098:     def rel_translation(
1099:         self,
1100:         hybrid: HybridTree,
1101:         pipeline_idx: int,
1102:     ) -> TranslationOutput:
1103:         """
1104:         The recursive procedure for converting a prefix of the hybrid tree
1105:         into a TranslationOutput payload.
1106: 
1107:         Args:
1108:             `hybrid`: the current level of the hybrid tree to be derived,
1109:             including all levels before it.
1110:             `pipeline_idx`: the index of the operation in the pipeline of the
1111:             current level that is to be derived, as well as all operations
1112:             preceding it in the pipeline.
1113: 
1114:         Returns:
1115:             The TranslationOutput payload corresponding to the relational
1116:             node to derive the prefix of the hybrid tree up to the level of
1117:             `hybrid` from all pipeline operators up to and including the
1118:             value of `pipeline_idx`.
1119:         """
1120:         assert pipeline_idx < len(hybrid.pipeline), (
1121:             f"Pipeline index {pipeline_idx} is too big for hybrid tree:\n{hybrid}"
1122:         )
1123: 
1124:         # Identify the operation that will be computed at this stage, and the
1125:         # previous stage on the current level of the hybrid tree, or the last
1126:         # operation from the preceding level if we are at the start of the
1127:         # current level. However, one may not exist, in which case the current
1128:         # stage must be defined as the first step.
1129:         operation: HybridOperation = hybrid.pipeline[pipeline_idx]
1130:         result: TranslationOutput
1131:         preceding_hybrid: tuple[HybridTree, int] | None = None
1132:         if pipeline_idx > 0:
1133:             preceding_hybrid = (hybrid, pipeline_idx - 1)
1134:         elif hybrid.parent is not None:
1135:             preceding_hybrid = (hybrid.parent, len(hybrid.parent.pipeline) - 1)
1136: 
1137:         # First, recursively fetch the TranslationOutput of the preceding
1138:         # stage, if valid.
1139:         context: TranslationOutput | None
1140:         if preceding_hybrid is None:
1141:             context = None
1142:         elif isinstance(preceding_hybrid[0].pipeline[preceding_hybrid[1]], HybridRoot):
1143:             # If at the true root, set the starting context to just be a dummy
1144:             # VALUES clause.
1145:             context = TranslationOutput(EmptySingleton(), {})
1146:             context = self.handle_children(context, *preceding_hybrid)
1147:         else:
1148:             context = self.rel_translation(*preceding_hybrid)
1149: 
1150:         # Then, dispatch onto the logic to transform from the context into the
1151:         # new translation output.
1152:         match operation:
1153:             case HybridCollectionAccess():
1154:                 if isinstance(operation.collection, TableCollection):
1155:                     result = self.build_simple_table_scan(operation)
1156:                     if context is not None:
1157:                         # If the collection access is the child of something
1158:                         # else, join it onto that something else. Use the
1159:                         # uniqueness keys of the ancestor, which should also be
1160:                         # present in the collection (e.g. joining a partition
1161:                         # onto the original data using the partition keys).
1162:                         assert preceding_hybrid is not None
1163:                         join_keys: list[tuple[HybridExpr, HybridExpr]] = []
1164:                         for unique_column in sorted(
1165:                             preceding_hybrid[0].pipeline[0].unique_exprs, key=str
1166:                         ):
1167:                             if unique_column not in result.expressions:
1168:                                 raise ValueError(
1169:                                     f"Cannot connect parent context to child {operation.collection} because {unique_column} is not in the child's expressions."
1170:                                 )
1171:                             join_keys.append((unique_column, unique_column))
1172:                         result = self.join_outputs(
1173:                             context,
1174:                             result,
1175:                             JoinType.INNER,
1176:                             join_keys,
1177:                             None,
1178:                             None,
1179:                         )
1180:                 else:
1181:                     # For subcollection accesses, the access is either a step
1182:                     # from a parent into a child (if the parent exists), or the
1183:                     # root of a child subtree (if the parent does not exist).
1184:                     if hybrid.parent is not None:
1185:                         assert context is not None, "Malformed HybridTree pattern."
1186:                         result = self.translate_sub_collection(
1187:                             operation, hybrid.parent, context
1188:                         )
1189:                     else:
1190:                         result = self.build_simple_table_scan(operation)
1191:             case HybridPartitionChild():
1192:                 result = self.translate_partition_child(operation, context)
1193:             case HybridCalculate():
1194:                 assert context is not None, "Malformed HybridTree pattern."
1195:                 result = self.translate_calculate(operation, context)
1196:             case HybridFilter():
1197:                 assert context is not None, "Malformed HybridTree pattern."
1198:                 result = self.translate_filter(operation, context)
1199:             case HybridPartition():
1200:                 if context is None:
1201:                     context = TranslationOutput(EmptySingleton(), {})
1202:                 result = self.translate_partition(
1203:                     operation, context, hybrid, pipeline_idx
1204:                 )
1205:             case HybridLimit():
1206:                 assert context is not None, "Malformed HybridTree pattern."
1207:                 result = self.translate_limit(operation, context)
1208:             case HybridChildPullUp():
1209:                 assert context is None, "Malformed HybridTree pattern."
1210:                 result = self.translate_child_pullup(operation)
1211:             case HybridNoop():
1212:                 assert context is not None, "Malformed HybridTree pattern."
1213:                 result = context
1214:             case _:
1215:                 raise NotImplementedError(
1216:                     f"TODO: support relational conversion on {operation.__class__.__name__}"
1217:                 )
1218:         result = self.handle_children(result, hybrid, pipeline_idx)
1219:         return result
1220: 
1221:     @staticmethod
1222:     def preprocess_root(
1223:         node: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
1224:         output_cols: list[tuple[str, str]] | None,
1225:     ) -> PyDoughCollectionQDAG:
1226:         """
1227:         Transforms the final PyDough collection by appending it with an extra
1228:         CALCULATE containing all of the columns that are output.
1229:         """
1230:         # Fetch all of the expressions that should be kept in the final output
1231:         final_terms: list[tuple[str, PyDoughExpressionQDAG]] = []
1232:         if output_cols is None:
1233:             for name in node.calc_terms:
1234:                 final_terms.append((name, Reference(node, name)))
1235:             final_terms.sort(key=lambda term: node.get_expression_position(term[0]))
1236:         else:
1237:             for _, column in output_cols:
1238:                 final_terms.append((column, Reference(node, column)))
1239:         children: list[PyDoughCollectionQDAG] = []
1240:         final_calc: Calculate = Calculate(node, children).with_terms(final_terms)
1241:         return final_calc
1242: 
1243: 
1244: def make_relational_ordering(
1245:     collation: list[HybridCollation],
1246:     expressions: dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference],
1247: ) -> list[ExpressionSortInfo]:
1248:     """
1249:     Converts a list of collation expressions into a list of ExpressionSortInfo.
1250: 
1251:     Args:
1252:         collation (list[CollationExpression]): The list of collation
1253:             expressions to convert.
1254:         expressions (dict[HybridExpr, ColumnReference]): The dictionary of
1255:             expressions to use for the relational ordering.
1256: 
1257:     Returns:
1258:         list[ExpressionSortInfo]: The ordering expressions converted into
1259:         ExpressionSortInfo.
1260:     """
1261:     orderings: list[ExpressionSortInfo] = []
1262:     for col_expr in collation:
1263:         relational_expr: ColumnReference = expressions[col_expr.expr]
1264:         collation_expr: ExpressionSortInfo = ExpressionSortInfo(
1265:             relational_expr, col_expr.asc, col_expr.na_first
1266:         )
1267:         orderings.append(collation_expr)
1268:     return orderings
1269: 
1270: 
1271: def postprocess_root(
1272:     node: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
1273:     columns: list[tuple[str, str]] | None,
1274:     hybrid: HybridTree,
1275:     relational_translation: TranslationOutput,
1276: ) -> RelationalRoot:
1277:     """
1278:     Run several postprocessing steps after the relational conversion step to
1279:     build the relational root for the QDAG node.
1280: 
1281:     Args:
1282:         `node`: the PyDough QDAG collection node to be translated.
1283:         `columns`: a list of tuples in the form `(alias, column)`
1284:         describing every column that should be in the output, in the order
1285:         they should appear, and the alias they should be given. If None, uses
1286:         the most recent CALCULATE in the node to determine the columns.
1287:         `hybrid`: the hybrid tree that `node` was translated into.
1288:         `relational_translation`: the TranslationOutput for the relational
1289:         node that `hybrid` was turned into.
1290:     """
1291: 
1292:     ordered_columns: list[tuple[str, RelationalExpression]] = []
1293:     orderings: list[ExpressionSortInfo] | None = None
1294:     renamings: dict[str, str] = hybrid.pipeline[-1].renamings
1295:     hybrid_expr: HybridExpr
1296:     rel_expr: RelationalExpression
1297:     name: str
1298:     original_name: str
1299:     if columns is None:
1300:         for original_name in node.calc_terms:
1301:             name = renamings.get(original_name, original_name)
1302:             hybrid_expr = hybrid.pipeline[-1].terms[name]
1303:             rel_expr = relational_translation.expressions[hybrid_expr]
1304:             ordered_columns.append((original_name, rel_expr))
1305:         ordered_columns.sort(key=lambda col: node.get_expression_position(col[0]))
1306:     else:
1307:         for alias, column in columns:
1308:             hybrid_expr = hybrid.pipeline[-1].terms[column]
1309:             rel_expr = relational_translation.expressions[hybrid_expr]
1310:             ordered_columns.append((alias, rel_expr))
1311:     hybrid_orderings: list[HybridCollation] = hybrid.pipeline[-1].orderings
1312:     if hybrid_orderings:
1313:         orderings = make_relational_ordering(
1314:             hybrid_orderings, relational_translation.expressions
1315:         )
1316:     return RelationalRoot(
1317:         relational_translation.relational_node, ordered_columns, orderings
1318:     )
1319: 
1320: 
1321: def confirm_root(node: RelationalNode) -> RelationalRoot:
1322:     """
1323:     Verify that the node is a RelationalRoot so it can be typed as such.
1324:     """
1325:     assert isinstance(node, RelationalRoot)
1326:     return node
1327: 
1328: 
1329: def optimize_relational_tree(
1330:     root: RelationalRoot, configs: PyDoughConfigs
1331: ) -> RelationalRoot:
1332:     """
1333:     Runs optimize on the relational tree, including pushing down filters and
1334:     pruning columns.
1335: 
1336:     Args:
1337:         `root`: the relational root to optimize.
1338:         `configs`: the configuration settings to use during optimization.
1339: 
1340:     Returns:
1341:         The optimized relational root.
1342:     """
1343: 
1344:     # Step 1: push filters down as far as possible
1345:     root._input = push_filters(root.input, set())
1346: 
1347:     # Step 2: merge adjacent projections, unless it would result in excessive
1348:     # duplicate subexpression computations.
1349:     root = confirm_root(merge_projects(root))
1350: 
1351:     # Step 3: split aggregations on top of joins so part of the aggregate
1352:     # happens underneath the join.
1353:     root = confirm_root(split_partial_aggregates(root, configs))
1354: 
1355:     # Step 4: re-run projection merging.
1356:     root = confirm_root(merge_projects(root))
1357: 
1358:     # Step 5: delete aggregations that are inferred to be redundant due to
1359:     # operating on already unique data.
1360:     root = remove_redundant_aggs(root)
1361: 
1362:     # Step 6: re-run projection merging.
1363:     root = confirm_root(merge_projects(root))
1364: 
1365:     # Step 7: prune unused columns
1366:     root = ColumnPruner().prune_unused_columns(root)
1367: 
1368:     # Step 3: merge adjacent projections, unless it would result in excessive
1369:     # duplicate subexpression computations.
1370:     merged_root = merge_projects(root)
1371:     assert isinstance(merged_root, RelationalRoot)
1372:     root = merged_root
1373: 
1374:     return root
1375: 
1376: 
1377: def convert_ast_to_relational(
1378:     node: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
1379:     columns: list[tuple[str, str]] | None,
1380:     configs: PyDoughConfigs,
1381:     dialect: DatabaseDialect = DatabaseDialect.ANSI,
1382: ) -> RelationalRoot:
1383:     """
1384:     Main API for converting from the collection QDAG form into relational
1385:     nodes.
1386: 
1387:     Args:
1388:         `node`: the PyDough QDAG collection node to be translated.
1389:         `columns`: a list of tuples in the form `(alias, column)`
1390:         describing every column that should be in the output, in the order
1391:         they should appear, and the alias they should be given. If None, uses
1392:         the most recent CALCULATE in the node to determine the columns.
1393:         `configs`: the configuration settings to use during translation.
1394:         `dialect`: the database dialect being used.
1395: 
1396:     Returns:
1397:         The RelationalRoot for the entire PyDough calculation that the
1398:         collection node corresponds to. Ensures that the desired output columns
1399:         of `node` are included in the root in the correct order, and if it
1400:         has an ordering then the relational root stores that information.
1401:     """
1402:     # Pre-process the QDAG node so the final CALCULATE includes any ordering
1403:     # keys.
1404:     rel_translator: RelTranslation = RelTranslation()
1405:     node = rel_translator.preprocess_root(node, columns)
1406: 
1407:     # Convert the QDAG node to the hybrid form and run a series of
1408:     # transformations:
1409:     # 1. Eject any arguments from the aggregate inputs
1410:     # 2. Run the de-correlation procedure
1411:     # 3. Run any final rewrites, such as turning MEDIAN into an average of the
1412:     #    1-2 median rows, that must happen after de-correlation.
1413:     hybrid_translator: HybridTranslator = HybridTranslator(configs, dialect)
1414:     hybrid: HybridTree = hybrid_translator.make_hybrid_tree(node, None)
1415:     hybrid_translator.eject_aggregate_inputs(hybrid)
1416:     run_hybrid_decorrelation(hybrid)
1417:     hybrid_translator.run_rewrites(hybrid)
1418: 
1419:     # Then, invoke relational conversion procedure. The first element in the
1420:     # returned list is the final relational tree.
1421:     output: TranslationOutput = rel_translator.rel_translation(
1422:         hybrid, len(hybrid.pipeline) - 1
1423:     )
1424: 
1425:     # Extract the relevant expressions for the final columns and ordering keys
1426:     # so that the root node can be built from them.
1427:     raw_result: RelationalRoot = postprocess_root(node, columns, hybrid, output)
1428: 
1429:     # Invoke the optimization procedures on the result to clean up the tree.
1430:     optimized_result: RelationalRoot = optimize_relational_tree(raw_result, configs)
1431: 
1432:     return optimized_result
````
