## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/back_reference_expression.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes that reference an expression of an ancestor
 3: context.
 4: """
 5: 
 6: __all__ = ["BackReferenceExpression"]
 7: from pydough.qdag.collections.collection_qdag import PyDoughCollectionQDAG
 8: from pydough.qdag.errors import PyDoughQDAGException
 9: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
10: 
11: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
12: from .reference import Reference
13: 
14: 
15: class BackReferenceExpression(Reference):
16:     """
17:     The QDAG node implementation class representing a reference to a term in
18:     the ancestor context.
19:     """
20: 
21:     def __init__(
22:         self, collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG, term_name: str, back_levels: int
23:     ):
24:         if not (isinstance(back_levels, int) and back_levels > 0):
25:             raise PyDoughQDAGException(
26:                 f"Expected number of levels in BACK to be a positive integer, received {back_levels!r}"
27:             )
28:         self._collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG = collection
29:         self._term_name: str = term_name
30:         self._back_levels: int = back_levels
31:         self._ancestor: PyDoughCollectionQDAG = collection
32:         for _ in range(back_levels):
33:             ancestor = self._ancestor.ancestor_context
34:             if ancestor is None:
35:                 msg: str = "1 level" if back_levels == 1 else f"{back_levels} levels"
36:                 raise PyDoughQDAGException(
37:                     f"Cannot reference back {msg} above {collection!r}"
38:                 )
39:             self._ancestor = ancestor
40:         self._expression = self._ancestor.get_expr(term_name)
41: 
42:     @property
43:     def back_levels(self) -> int:
44:         """
45:         The number of levels upward that the backreference refers to.
46:         """
47:         return self._back_levels
48: 
49:     @property
50:     def ancestor(self) -> PyDoughCollectionQDAG:
51:         """
52:         The specific ancestor collection that the ancestor refers to.
53:         """
54:         return self._ancestor
55: 
56:     @property
57:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
58:         return self.expression.pydough_type
59: 
60:     @property
61:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
62:         return self.expression.is_aggregation
63: 
64:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: PyDoughExpressionQDAG) -> bool:
65:         return False
66: 
67:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
68:         return self.term_name
69: 
70:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
71:         return (
72:             super().equals(other)
73:             and isinstance(other, BackReferenceExpression)
74:             and self.ancestor.equals(other.ancestor)
75:         )
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/child_reference_expression.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes for referencing expressions from a child
 3: collection of a child operator, e.g. `orders.order_date` in
 4: `customers.CALCULATE(most_recent_order=MAX(orders.order_date))`.
 5: """
 6: 
 7: __all__ = ["ChildReferenceExpression"]
 8: 
 9: from functools import cache
10: 
11: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
12: from pydough.qdag.collections.collection_qdag import PyDoughCollectionQDAG
13: from pydough.qdag.errors import PyDoughQDAGException
14: 
15: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
16: from .reference import Reference
17: 
18: 
19: class ChildReferenceExpression(Reference):
20:     """
21:     The QDAG node implementation class representing a reference to a term in
22:     a child collection of a CALCULATE or similar child operator node.
23:     """
24: 
25:     def __init__(
26:         self, collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG, child_idx: int, term_name: str
27:     ):
28:         self._collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG = collection
29:         self._child_idx: int = child_idx
30:         self._term_name: str = term_name
31:         self._expression: PyDoughExpressionQDAG = self._collection.get_expr(term_name)
32:         if not self.expression.is_singular(collection.starting_predecessor):
33:             raise PyDoughQDAGException(
34:                 f"Cannot reference plural expression {self.expression} from {self.collection}"
35:             )
36: 
37:     @property
38:     def child_idx(self) -> int:
39:         """
40:         The integer index of the child from the child operator that the
41:         ChildReferenceExpression refers to.
42:         """
43:         return self._child_idx
44: 
45:     @cache
46:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
47:         # Child reference expressions are already known to be singular relative
48:         # to the child collection to the via their construction, so they are
49:         # singular relative to the context if and only if their child collection
50:         # is singular relative to the context.
51:         assert isinstance(context, PyDoughCollectionQDAG)
52:         return self.collection.is_singular(context)
53: 
54:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
55:         if tree_form:
56:             return f"${self.child_idx + 1}.{self.term_name}"
57:         else:
58:             return f"{self.collection.to_string()}.{self.term_name}"
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/collation_expression.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes used to wrap another expression node in
 3: ordering information so the expression can be used as an ordering key.
 4: """
 5: 
 6: __all__ = ["CollationExpression"]
 7: 
 8: 
 9: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
10: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
11: 
12: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
13: 
14: 
15: class CollationExpression(PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
16:     """
17:     The wrapper class around expressions to denote how to use them as an
18:     ordering key.
19:     """
20: 
21:     def __init__(self, expr: PyDoughExpressionQDAG, asc: bool, na_last: bool):
22:         self._expr: PyDoughExpressionQDAG = expr
23:         self._asc: bool = asc
24:         self._na_last: bool = na_last
25: 
26:     @property
27:     def expr(self) -> PyDoughExpressionQDAG:
28:         """
29:         The expression being used as a collation.
30:         """
31:         return self._expr
32: 
33:     @property
34:     def asc(self) -> bool:
35:         """
36:         Whether the collation key is ascending or descending.
37:         """
38:         return self._asc
39: 
40:     @property
41:     def na_last(self) -> bool:
42:         """
43:         Whether the collation key places nulls at the end.
44:         """
45:         return self._na_last
46: 
47:     @property
48:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
49:         return self.expr.pydough_type
50: 
51:     @property
52:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
53:         return self.expr.is_aggregation
54: 
55:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
56:         # Collation expressions inherit their singular-or-plural nature from
57:         # their underlying expression.
58:         return self.expr.is_singular(context)
59: 
60:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
61:         expr_string: str = self.expr.to_string(tree_form)
62:         if self.expr.requires_enclosing_parens(self):
63:             expr_string = f"({expr_string})"
64:         suffix = "ASC" if self.asc else "DESC"
65:         kwarg = "'last'" if self.na_last else "'first'"
66:         return f"{expr_string}.{suffix}(na_pos={kwarg})"
67: 
68:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: "PyDoughExpressionQDAG") -> bool:
69:         return False
70: 
71:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
72:         if isinstance(other, CollationExpression):
73:             return (
74:                 self.expr.equals(other.expr)
75:                 and self.asc == other.asc
76:                 and self.na_last == other.na_last
77:             )
78:         else:
79:             return self.expr.equals(other)
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/expression_function_call.py
````python
  1: """
  2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes for function calls that return expressions.
  3: """
  4: 
  5: __all__ = ["ExpressionFunctionCall"]
  6: 
  7: 
  8: from pydough.pydough_operators.expression_operators.expression_operator import (
  9:     PyDoughExpressionOperator,
 10: )
 11: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
 12: from pydough.qdag.collections.collection_qdag import PyDoughCollectionQDAG
 13: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
 14: 
 15: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
 16: 
 17: 
 18: class ExpressionFunctionCall(PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
 19:     """
 20:     The QDAG node implementation class representing a call to a function
 21:     that returns an expression.
 22:     """
 23: 
 24:     def __init__(
 25:         self,
 26:         operator: PyDoughExpressionOperator,
 27:         args: list[PyDoughQDAG],
 28:     ):
 29:         operator.verify_allows_args(args)
 30:         self._operator: PyDoughExpressionOperator = operator
 31:         self._args: list[PyDoughQDAG] = args
 32:         self._data_type: PyDoughType = operator.infer_return_type(args)
 33: 
 34:     @property
 35:     def operator(self) -> PyDoughExpressionOperator:
 36:         """
 37:         The expression-returning PyDough operator corresponding to the
 38:         function call.
 39:         """
 40:         return self._operator
 41: 
 42:     @property
 43:     def args(self) -> list[PyDoughQDAG]:
 44:         """
 45:         The list of arguments to the function call.
 46:         """
 47:         return self._args
 48: 
 49:     @property
 50:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
 51:         return self._data_type
 52: 
 53:     @property
 54:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
 55:         return self.operator.is_aggregation
 56: 
 57:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
 58:         # Function calls are singular if they are aggregations or if all of
 59:         # their operands are also singular.
 60:         assert isinstance(context, PyDoughCollectionQDAG)
 61:         if self.is_aggregation:
 62:             return True
 63:         for arg in self.args:
 64:             if isinstance(
 65:                 arg, (PyDoughExpressionQDAG, PyDoughCollectionQDAG)
 66:             ) and not arg.is_singular(context):
 67:                 return False
 68:         return True
 69: 
 70:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: PyDoughExpressionQDAG) -> bool:
 71:         return self.operator.requires_enclosing_parens(parent)
 72: 
 73:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
 74:         from pydough.qdag.collections.child_reference_collection import (
 75:             ChildReferenceCollection,
 76:         )
 77: 
 78:         arg_strings: list[str] = []
 79:         for arg in self.args:
 80:             arg_string: str
 81:             if isinstance(arg, PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
 82:                 arg_string = arg.to_string(tree_form)
 83:                 if arg.requires_enclosing_parens(self):
 84:                     arg_string = f"({arg_string})"
 85:             elif isinstance(arg, PyDoughCollectionQDAG):
 86:                 if tree_form:
 87:                     assert isinstance(arg, ChildReferenceCollection), (
 88:                         f"Unexpected argument to function call {arg}: expected an expression, or reference to a collection"
 89:                     )
 90:                     arg_string = arg.tree_item_string
 91:                 else:
 92:                     arg_string = arg.to_string()
 93:             else:
 94:                 arg_string = str(arg)
 95:             arg_strings.append(arg_string)
 96:         return self.operator.to_string(arg_strings)
 97: 
 98:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
 99:         return (
100:             isinstance(other, ExpressionFunctionCall)
101:             and (self.operator == other.operator)
102:             and (self.args == other.args)
103:         )
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/expression_qdag.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Base definition of PyDough expression QDAG nodes.
 3: """
 4: 
 5: __all__ = ["PyDoughExpressionQDAG"]
 6: 
 7: from abc import abstractmethod
 8: 
 9: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
10: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
11: 
12: 
13: class PyDoughExpressionQDAG(PyDoughQDAG):
14:     """
15:     The base class for QDAG nodes that represent expressions.
16:     """
17: 
18:     def __repr__(self):
19:         return self.to_string()
20: 
21:     @property
22:     @abstractmethod
23:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
24:         """
25:         The PyDough type of the expression.
26:         """
27: 
28:     @property
29:     @abstractmethod
30:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
31:         """
32:         Whether the expression corresponds to an aggregation that
33:         can collapse multiple records into a scalar value.
34:         """
35: 
36:     @abstractmethod
37:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
38:         """
39:         Returns whether the expression is singular with regards to a
40:         context collection.
41: 
42:         Args:
43:             `context`: the collection that the singular/plural status of the
44:             current expression is being checked against. Note: despite the
45:             annotation, this must be a collection.
46: 
47:         Returns:
48:             True if there is at most a single record of the current expression
49:             for each record of the context, and False otherwise.
50:         """
51: 
52:     @property
53:     def key(self) -> str:
54:         return self.to_string()
55: 
56:     @abstractmethod
57:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
58:         """
59:         Returns a PyDough expression QDAG converted into a single-line string
60:         structured so it can be placed in the tree-like string representation
61:         of a collection QDAG.
62: 
63:         Args:
64:             `tree_form`: indicates that the string conversion is happening
65:             inside of a tree string (default False).
66: 
67:         Returns:
68:             The single-line string representation of `self`.
69:         """
70: 
71:     @abstractmethod
72:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: "PyDoughExpressionQDAG") -> bool:
73:         """
74:         Identifies whether an expression converted to a string must be wrapped
75:         in parenthesis before being inserted into it's parent's string
76:         representation. This depends on what exactly the parent is.
77: 
78:         Args:
79:             `parent`: the parent expression QDAG that contains this expression
80:             QDAG as a child.
81: 
82:         Returns:
83:             True if the string representation of `parent` should enclose
84:             parenthesis around the string representation of `self`.
85:         """
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/partition_key.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes used to wrap certain expressions to denote them
 3: as keys of a PARTITION BY clause.
 4: """
 5: 
 6: __all__ = ["PartitionKey"]
 7: 
 8: 
 9: from functools import cache
10: 
11: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
12: from pydough.qdag.collections.collection_qdag import PyDoughCollectionQDAG
13: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
14: 
15: from .child_reference_expression import ChildReferenceExpression
16: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
17: 
18: 
19: class PartitionKey(PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
20:     """
21:     The wrapper class around expressions to denote that an expression
22:     is a key used for partitioning. Currently only allows the expression to be
23:     a reference to an expression from the partition data.
24:     """
25: 
26:     def __init__(
27:         self, collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG, expr: ChildReferenceExpression
28:     ):
29:         self._collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG = collection
30:         self._expr: ChildReferenceExpression = expr
31: 
32:     @property
33:     def collection(self) -> PyDoughCollectionQDAG:
34:         """
35:         The PARTITION BY collection that the expression is being used as a key
36:         for.
37:         """
38:         return self._collection
39: 
40:     @property
41:     def expr(self) -> ChildReferenceExpression:
42:         """
43:         The expression being used as a partition key.
44:         """
45:         return self._expr
46: 
47:     @property
48:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
49:         return self.expr.pydough_type
50: 
51:     @property
52:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
53:         return self.expr.is_aggregation
54: 
55:     @cache
56:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
57:         # A partition key is singular with regards to a context if and only
58:         # if the PARTITION BY clause it corresponds to is also singular with
59:         # regards to that context (or the PARTITION BY clause is the context).
60:         assert isinstance(context, PyDoughCollectionQDAG)
61:         return (context == self.collection) or self.collection.is_singular(context)
62: 
63:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
64:         return self.expr.to_string(tree_form)
65: 
66:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: "PyDoughExpressionQDAG") -> bool:
67:         return self.expr.requires_enclosing_parens(parent)
68: 
69:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
70:         if isinstance(other, PartitionKey):
71:             return self.expr.equals(other.expr)
72:         else:
73:             return self.expr.equals(other)
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/README.md
````markdown
 1: # PyDough QDAG Expressions Module
 2: 
 3: This module defines the various expression types used in the QDAG (Qualified Directed Acyclic Graph) structure of PyDough. These expressions represent different ways of accessing and manipulating data within the graph.
 4: 
 5: ## Available Classes
 6: 
 7: ### Base Class
 8: 
 9: `PyDoughExpressionQDAG` is the base class for all QDAG expression nodes. It provides a common interface for all expression types. That interface includes the following APIs, in addition to the base QDAG interface:
10: 
11: - `pydough_type`: a property indicating what type an expression returns.
12: - `is_aggregation`: a property indicating whether an expression collapses multiple records into a single value.
13: - `is_singular`: a method that takes in a collection as a context and returns whether the expression is singular with regards to that context (e.g. there is only one value of `name` or `region.name` for each record of `Nations`, but several values of `nations.name` for each value of `Regions`).
14: - `to_string`: converts the expression to a string. The string conversion can be different depending on whether the `tree_form` argument is True or False.
15: - `requires_enclosing_parens`: takes in a parent expression and returns whether the current expression should be placed inside parenthesis when converting it into a string that goes inside the string representation of the parent.
16: 
17: ### Expression Implementation Classes
18: 
19: - `Literal`: Represents a literal value in the QDAG.
20: - `ColumnProperty`: Represents a column property of a collection.
21: - `ExpressionFunctionCall`: Represents a function call expression. Contains a PyDough operator that returns an expression, as well as a list of QDAG nodes (collections or expressions).
22: - `WindowCall`: Represents a window function call expression. Contains a PyDough operator for a window function that returns an expression, as well as the QDAG nodes for the window ordering, the number of ancestor levels that the window is relative to, and any additional keyword arguments.
23: - `Reference`: Represents a reference to an expression in a preceding context.
24: - `ChildReferenceExpression`: Represents a reference to an expression in a child collection.
25: - `BackReferenceExpression`: Represents a reference to an expression in an ancestor collection.
26: - `HiddenBackReferenceExpression`: Represents a regular reference expression that is actually a back reference because the ancestor it refers to is hidden by a compound relationship (e.g. accessing `availqty` from `supply_records` in `parts.suppliers_of_part` where that relationship is an alias for `parts.supply_records.supplier`).
27: - `CollationExpression`: Wraps another expression QDAG node in information about how to use it to order a collection by (e.g. ascending vs descending, nulls first vs last).
28: - `PartitionKey`: Wraps another expression QDAG node to indicate that it is used as a key to partition by (should only wrap a child reference to an expression from the partition data).
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/reference.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes for expression references to another expression
 3: in a preceding context.
 4: """
 5: 
 6: __all__ = ["Reference"]
 7: 
 8: 
 9: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
10: from pydough.qdag.collections.collection_qdag import PyDoughCollectionQDAG
11: from pydough.qdag.errors import PyDoughQDAGException
12: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
13: 
14: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
15: 
16: 
17: class Reference(PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
18:     """
19:     The QDAG node implementation class representing a reference to a term in
20:     a preceding collection.
21:     """
22: 
23:     def __init__(self, collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG, term_name: str):
24:         self._collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG = collection
25:         self._term_name: str = term_name
26:         self._expression: PyDoughExpressionQDAG = collection.get_expr(term_name)
27:         if not self.expression.is_singular(collection.starting_predecessor):
28:             raise PyDoughQDAGException(
29:                 f"Cannot reference plural expression {self.expression} from {self.collection}"
30:             )
31: 
32:     @property
33:     def collection(self) -> PyDoughCollectionQDAG:
34:         """
35:         The collection that the Reference term comes from.
36:         """
37:         return self._collection
38: 
39:     @property
40:     def term_name(self) -> str:
41:         """
42:         The name of the term that the Reference refers to.
43:         """
44:         return self._term_name
45: 
46:     @property
47:     def expression(self) -> PyDoughExpressionQDAG:
48:         """
49:         The original expression that the reference refers to.
50:         """
51:         return self._expression
52: 
53:     @property
54:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
55:         return self.expression.pydough_type
56: 
57:     @property
58:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
59:         return self.expression.is_aggregation
60: 
61:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
62:         # References are already known to be singular via their construction.
63:         return True
64: 
65:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: PyDoughExpressionQDAG) -> bool:
66:         return False
67: 
68:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
69:         return self.term_name
70: 
71:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
72:         return (
73:             isinstance(other, Reference)
74:             and self.term_name == other.term_name
75:             and self.collection.equals(other.collection)
76:         )
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/sided_reference.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes for expression references to another expression
 3: in a preceding context.
 4: """
 5: 
 6: __all__ = ["SidedReference"]
 7: 
 8: 
 9: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
10: from pydough.qdag.collections.collection_qdag import PyDoughCollectionQDAG
11: from pydough.qdag.errors import PyDoughQDAGException
12: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
13: 
14: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
15: 
16: 
17: class SidedReference(PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
18:     """
19:     The QDAG node implementation class representing a reference to a term from
20:     one of two sides of connection between a parent collection and a child
21:     connection. This type of expression node is only allowed to exist inside of
22:     a general join condition.
23:     """
24: 
25:     def __init__(
26:         self, term_name: str, collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG, is_parent: bool
27:     ):
28:         self._collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG = collection
29:         self._term_name: str = term_name
30:         base_collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG
31:         if is_parent:
32:             assert collection.ancestor_context is not None
33:             base_collection = collection.ancestor_context.starting_predecessor
34:         else:
35:             base_collection = collection.starting_predecessor
36:         self._expression: PyDoughExpressionQDAG = base_collection.get_expr(term_name)
37:         if not self.expression.is_singular(collection.starting_predecessor):
38:             raise PyDoughQDAGException(
39:                 f"Cannot reference plural expression {self.expression} from {self.collection}"
40:             )
41:         self._is_parent: bool = is_parent
42: 
43:     @property
44:     def collection(self) -> PyDoughCollectionQDAG:
45:         """
46:         The collection that the Reference term comes from.
47:         """
48:         return self._collection
49: 
50:     @property
51:     def term_name(self) -> str:
52:         """
53:         The name of the term that the Reference refers to.
54:         """
55:         return self._term_name
56: 
57:     @property
58:     def expression(self) -> PyDoughExpressionQDAG:
59:         """
60:         The original expression that the reference refers to.
61:         """
62:         return self._expression
63: 
64:     @property
65:     def is_parent(self) -> bool:
66:         """
67:         Whether the reference is to the parent side of the connection.
68:         """
69:         return self._is_parent
70: 
71:     @property
72:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
73:         return self.expression.pydough_type
74: 
75:     @property
76:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
77:         return self.expression.is_aggregation
78: 
79:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
80:         # References are already known to be singular via their construction.
81:         return True
82: 
83:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: PyDoughExpressionQDAG) -> bool:
84:         return False
85: 
86:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
87:         prefix: str = "PARENT" if self.is_parent else "CHILD"
88:         return f"{prefix}.{self.term_name}"
89: 
90:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
91:         return (
92:             isinstance(other, SidedReference)
93:             and self.term_name == other.term_name
94:             and self.is_parent == other.is_parent
95:             and self.collection.equals(other.collection)
96:         )
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/expressions/window_call.py
````python
  1: """
  2: Definition of PyDough QDAG nodes for window function calls that return
  3: expressions.
  4: """
  5: 
  6: __all__ = ["WindowCall"]
  7: 
  8: 
  9: from pydough.pydough_operators.expression_operators import (
 10:     ExpressionWindowOperator,
 11: )
 12: from pydough.qdag.abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
 13: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
 14: 
 15: from .collation_expression import CollationExpression
 16: from .expression_qdag import PyDoughExpressionQDAG
 17: 
 18: 
 19: class WindowCall(PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
 20:     """
 21:     The QDAG node implementation class representing window operations that
 22:     return expressions.
 23:     """
 24: 
 25:     def __init__(
 26:         self,
 27:         window_operator: ExpressionWindowOperator,
 28:         args: list[PyDoughExpressionQDAG],
 29:         collation_args: list[CollationExpression],
 30:         levels: int | None,
 31:         kwargs: dict[str, object],
 32:     ):
 33:         window_operator.verify_allows_args(args)
 34:         self._window_operator: ExpressionWindowOperator = window_operator
 35:         self._args: list[PyDoughExpressionQDAG] = args
 36:         self._collation_args: list[CollationExpression] = collation_args
 37:         self._levels: int | None = levels
 38:         self._kwargs: dict[str, object] = kwargs
 39: 
 40:     @property
 41:     def window_operator(self) -> ExpressionWindowOperator:
 42:         """
 43:         The window operator that is being applied.
 44:         """
 45:         return self._window_operator
 46: 
 47:     @property
 48:     def args(self) -> list[PyDoughExpressionQDAG]:
 49:         """
 50:         The list of arguments used to as inputs to the window function.
 51:         """
 52:         return self._args
 53: 
 54:     @property
 55:     def collation_args(self) -> list[CollationExpression]:
 56:         """
 57:         The list of collation arguments used to order to the window function.
 58:         """
 59:         return self._collation_args
 60: 
 61:     @property
 62:     def levels(self) -> int | None:
 63:         """
 64:         The number of ancestor levels the window function is being computed
 65:         relative to. None indicates that the computation is global.
 66:         """
 67:         return self._levels
 68: 
 69:     @property
 70:     def kwargs(self) -> dict[str, object]:
 71:         """
 72:         Any additional keyword arguments to window functions. For example, for
 73:         `RANKING`, whether to allow ties in the ranking (True) or not (False).
 74:         """
 75:         return self._kwargs
 76: 
 77:     @property
 78:     def pydough_type(self) -> PyDoughType:
 79:         return self.window_operator.infer_return_type(self.args)
 80: 
 81:     @property
 82:     def is_aggregation(self) -> bool:
 83:         return False
 84: 
 85:     def is_singular(self, context: PyDoughQDAG) -> bool:
 86:         # Window function calls are singular if all of their arguments and
 87:         # collation arguments are singular
 88:         for arg in self.args:
 89:             if not arg.is_singular(context):
 90:                 return False
 91:         for order_arg in self.collation_args:
 92:             if not order_arg.expr.is_singular(context):
 93:                 return False
 94:         return True
 95: 
 96:     def requires_enclosing_parens(self, parent: PyDoughExpressionQDAG) -> bool:
 97:         return False
 98: 
 99:     def to_string(self, tree_form: bool = False) -> str:
100:         arg_strings: list[str] = [f"{arg.to_string(tree_form)}, " for arg in self.args]
101:         collation_arg_strings: list[str] = [
102:             arg.to_string(tree_form) for arg in self.collation_args
103:         ]
104:         suffix: str = ""
105:         if self.levels is not None:
106:             suffix += f", levels={self.levels}"
107:         for kwarg in self.kwargs:
108:             suffix += f", {kwarg}={self.kwargs.get(kwarg)!r}"
109:         return f"{self.window_operator.function_name}({''.join(arg_strings)}by=({', '.join(collation_arg_strings)}){suffix})"
110: 
111:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
112:         return (
113:             isinstance(other, WindowCall)
114:             and (self.window_operator == other.window_operator)
115:             and (self.args == other.args)
116:             and (self.collation_args == other.collation_args)
117:             and (self.levels == other.levels)
118:             and (repr(self.kwargs) == repr(other.kwargs))
119:         )
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/abstract_pydough_qdag.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Base class for all PyDough QDAG nodes, collection or expression.
 3: """
 4: 
 5: __all__ = ["PyDoughQDAG"]
 6: 
 7: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
 8: from hashlib import sha256
 9: 
10: 
11: class PyDoughQDAG(ABC):
12:     """
13:     Base class used for PyDough collection and expression nodes.
14:     Mostly exists for isinstance checks & type annotation.
15:     """
16: 
17:     def __eq__(self, other):
18:         return self.equals(other)
19: 
20:     def __hash__(self):
21:         # TODO: investigate whether this is too slow, and if so find something
22:         # faster that has the same benefits (good hash function, possibly
23:         # consistent)
24:         return int(sha256(self.key.encode()).hexdigest(), base=16)
25: 
26:     @property
27:     @abstractmethod
28:     def key(self) -> str:
29:         """
30:         An string used to distinguish `self` to hash on so that QDAG nodes can
31:         have cached methods. This key string is not necessarily unique for
32:         objects even if they are not equal.
33:         """
34: 
35:     @abstractmethod
36:     def equals(self, other: object) -> bool:
37:         """
38:         Returns true if two PyDoughQDAG objects are equal.
39: 
40:         Args:
41:             `other`: the candidate object being compared to `self`.
42: 
43:         Returns:
44:             Whether `other` is equal to `self`.
45:         """
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/has_hasnot_rewrite.py
````python
 1: """
 2: Definition of the PyDough QDAG expression rewrite step that handles HAS and
 3: HASNOT.
 4: """
 5: 
 6: __all__ = ["has_hasnot_rewrite"]
 7: 
 8: 
 9: from pydough.types import Int64Type
10: 
11: from .abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
12: from .expressions import (
13:     ExpressionFunctionCall,
14:     Literal,
15:     PyDoughExpressionQDAG,
16: )
17: 
18: 
19: def has_hasnot_rewrite(
20:     exp: PyDoughExpressionQDAG, allow_has_hasnot: bool
21: ) -> PyDoughExpressionQDAG:
22:     """
23:     Recursively transforms a PyDough expression QDAG node to achieve the
24:     following goals:
25:     - Flatten all conjunctions, e.g. `(x & y) & (a & b) -> (x & y & a & b)`
26:     - Rewrite all `HAS(X)` as `COUNT(X) > 0` unless in the conjunction of a
27:     `WHERE` clause.
28:     - Rewrite all `HASNOT(X)` as `COUNT(X) == 0` unless in the conjunction of a
29:     `WHERE` clause.
30: 
31:     Args:
32:         - `exp`: the PyDough expression node being transformed.
33:         - `allow_has_hasnot`: whether the call is being done in the conjunction
34:         of a `WHERE` clause, meaning that `HAS` and `HASNOT` should not be
35:         rewritten. This should only be True when the original callsite is a
36:         `WHERE` clause.
37: 
38:     Returns:
39:         The transformed PyDough expression QDAG node.
40:     """
41:     from pydough.pydough_operators import (
42:         BAN,
43:         COUNT,
44:         EQU,
45:         GRT,
46:         HAS,
47:         HASNOT,
48:     )
49: 
50:     if isinstance(exp, ExpressionFunctionCall):
51:         new_args: list[PyDoughQDAG] = []
52:         if exp.operator in (HAS, HASNOT) and not allow_has_hasnot:
53:             # Rewrite HAS and HASNOT into COUNT comparisons unless we are
54:             # still in the conjunction of a WHERE clause
55:             cmp_op = GRT if exp.operator == HAS else EQU
56:             return ExpressionFunctionCall(
57:                 cmp_op,
58:                 [ExpressionFunctionCall(COUNT, exp.args), Literal(0, Int64Type())],
59:             )
60:         elif exp.operator == BAN:
61:             # When processing an AND call, flatten its children that are also
62:             # AND calls, and process their arguments as if we were still in a
63:             # conjunction.
64:             for arg in exp.args:
65:                 arg = (
66:                     has_hasnot_rewrite(arg, allow_has_hasnot)
67:                     if isinstance(arg, PyDoughExpressionQDAG)
68:                     else arg
69:                 )
70:                 if isinstance(arg, ExpressionFunctionCall) and arg.operator == BAN:
71:                     new_args.extend(arg.args)
72:                 else:
73:                     new_args.append(arg)
74:             return ExpressionFunctionCall(BAN, new_args)
75:         else:
76:             # For any other function call, just recursively transform any
77:             # arguments that are expressions, but disable HAS/HASNOT since the
78:             # function call means we are no longer inside of a conjunction.
79:             for arg in exp.args:
80:                 if isinstance(arg, PyDoughExpressionQDAG):
81:                     new_args.append(has_hasnot_rewrite(arg, False))
82:                 else:
83:                     new_args.append(arg)
84:             return ExpressionFunctionCall(exp.operator, new_args)
85:     else:
86:         # Anything except a function call is un-transformed.
87:         return exp
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/node_builder.py
````python
  1: """
  2: Definitions of utilities used to build PyDough QDAG nodes.
  3: """
  4: 
  5: __all__ = ["AstNodeBuilder"]
  6: 
  7: 
  8: from pydough.metadata import (
  9:     CollectionMetadata,
 10:     GraphMetadata,
 11:     PropertyMetadata,
 12:     PyDoughMetadataException,
 13:     TableColumnMetadata,
 14: )
 15: from pydough.pydough_operators import (
 16:     ExpressionWindowOperator,
 17:     PyDoughExpressionOperator,
 18:     PyDoughOperator,
 19:     builtin_registered_operators,
 20: )
 21: from pydough.types import PyDoughType
 22: 
 23: from .abstract_pydough_qdag import PyDoughQDAG
 24: from .collections import (
 25:     Calculate,
 26:     ChildAccess,
 27:     ChildReferenceCollection,
 28:     GlobalContext,
 29:     OrderBy,
 30:     PartitionBy,
 31:     PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
 32:     Singular,
 33:     TopK,
 34:     Where,
 35: )
 36: from .errors import PyDoughQDAGException
 37: from .expressions import (
 38:     BackReferenceExpression,
 39:     ChildReferenceExpression,
 40:     CollationExpression,
 41:     ColumnProperty,
 42:     ExpressionFunctionCall,
 43:     Literal,
 44:     PyDoughExpressionQDAG,
 45:     Reference,
 46:     WindowCall,
 47: )
 48: 
 49: 
 50: class AstNodeBuilder:
 51:     """
 52:     Class used in testing to build QDAG nodes
 53:     """
 54: 
 55:     def __init__(self, graph: GraphMetadata):
 56:         self._graph: GraphMetadata = graph
 57:         self._operators: dict[str, PyDoughOperator] = builtin_registered_operators()
 58: 
 59:     @property
 60:     def graph(self) -> GraphMetadata:
 61:         """
 62:         The graph used by the node builder.
 63:         """
 64:         return self._graph
 65: 
 66:     @property
 67:     def operators(self) -> dict[str, PyDoughOperator]:
 68:         """
 69:         The operators that the builder has access to.
 70:         """
 71:         return self._operators
 72: 
 73:     def build_literal(self, value: object, data_type: PyDoughType) -> Literal:
 74:         """
 75:         Creates a new literal of the specified PyDough type using a passed-in
 76:         literal value.
 77: 
 78:         Args:
 79:             `value`: the literal value to be stored.
 80:             `data_type`: the PyDough type of the literal.
 81: 
 82:         Returns:
 83:             The newly created PyDough literal.
 84: 
 85:         Raises:
 86:             `PyDoughQDAGException`: if the literal cannot be created.
 87:         """
 88:         return Literal(value, data_type)
 89: 
 90:     def build_column(self, collection_name: str, property_name: str) -> ColumnProperty:
 91:         """
 92:         Creates a new column property node by accessing a specific property of
 93:         a collection in the graph by name.
 94: 
 95:         Args:
 96:             `value`: the literal value to be stored.
 97:             `data_type`: the PyDough type of the literal.
 98: 
 99:         Returns:
100:             The newly created PyDough literal.
101: 
102:         Raises:
103:             `PyDoughMetadataException`: if the property does not exist or is
104:             not a table column.
105:         """
106:         collection = self.graph.get_collection(collection_name)
107:         assert isinstance(collection, CollectionMetadata)
108:         property = collection.get_property(property_name)
109:         assert isinstance(property, PropertyMetadata)
110:         if not isinstance(property, TableColumnMetadata):
111:             raise PyDoughMetadataException(
112:                 f"Expected {property.error_name} to be a table column property"
113:             )
114:         return ColumnProperty(property)
115: 
116:     def build_expression_function_call(
117:         self, operator: PyDoughExpressionOperator, args: list[PyDoughQDAG]
118:     ) -> ExpressionFunctionCall:
119:         """
120:         Creates a new expression function call.
121: 
122:         Args:
123:             `operator`: the operator to be called.
124:             `args`: the arguments to the operator.
125: 
126:         Returns:
127:             The newly created PyDough expression function call.
128:         """
129:         return ExpressionFunctionCall(operator, args)
130: 
131:     def build_window_call(
132:         self,
133:         window_operator: ExpressionWindowOperator,
134:         qualified_args: list[PyDoughExpressionQDAG],
135:         collation_args: list[CollationExpression],
136:         levels: int | None,
137:         kwargs: dict[str, object],
138:     ) -> WindowCall:
139:         """
140:         Creates a new window function call that returns an expression.
141: 
142:         Args:
143:             `window_operator`: the operator for the window function called.
144:             `collation_args`: the orderings used by the window function.
145:             `levels`: which ancestor the window function partitions relative to
146:             (None is the same thing as the furthest ancestor).
147:             `kwargs`: any additional arguments to the function, such as whether
148:             ranking allows ties or is dense.
149:             are ties.
150: 
151:         Returns:
152:             The window function call as a QDAG expression node.
153:         """
154:         return WindowCall(
155:             window_operator, qualified_args, collation_args, levels, kwargs
156:         )
157: 
158:     def build_reference(
159:         self, collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG, name: str
160:     ) -> Reference:
161:         """
162:         Creates a new reference to an expression from a preceding collection.
163: 
164:         Args:
165:             `collection`: the collection that the reference comes from.
166:             `name`: the name of the expression being referenced.
167: 
168:         Returns:
169:             The newly created PyDough Reference.
170: 
171:         Raises:
172:             `PyDoughQDAGException`: if `name` does not refer to an expression in
173:             the collection.
174:         """
175:         return Reference(collection, name)
176: 
177:     def build_child_reference_expression(
178:         self,
179:         children: list[PyDoughCollectionQDAG],
180:         child_idx: int,
181:         name: str,
182:     ) -> Reference:
183:         """
184:         Creates a new reference to an expression from a child collection of a
185:         CALCULATE or similar operator.
186: 
187:         Args:
188:             `children`: the child collections that the reference accesses.
189:             `child_idx`: the index of the child collection being referenced.
190:             `name`: the name of the expression being referenced.
191: 
192:         Returns:
193:             The newly created PyDough Child Reference.
194: 
195:         Raises:
196:             `PyDoughQDAGException`: if `name` does not refer to an expression in
197:             the collection, or `child_idx` is not a valid index for `children`.
198:         """
199:         if child_idx not in range(len(children)):
200:             raise PyDoughQDAGException(
201:                 f"Invalid child reference index {child_idx} with {len(children)} children"
202:             )
203:         return ChildReferenceExpression(children[child_idx], child_idx, name)
204: 
205:     def build_back_reference_expression(
206:         self, collection: PyDoughCollectionQDAG, name: str, levels: int
207:     ) -> Reference:
208:         """
209:         Creates a new reference to an expression from an ancestor collection.
210: 
211:         Args:
212:             `collection`: the collection that the back reference comes from.
213:             `name`: the name of the expression being referenced.
214:             `levels`: the number of levels back from `collection` the reference
215:             refers to.
216: 
217:         Returns:
218:             The newly created PyDough Back Reference.
219: 
220:         Raises:
221:             `PyDoughQDAGException`: if `name` does not refer to an expression in
222:             the ancestor collection, or the collection does not have `levels`
223:             many ancestors.
224:         """
225:         return BackReferenceExpression(collection, name, levels)
226: 
227:     def build_global_context(self) -> GlobalContext:
228:         """
229:         Creates a new global context for the graph.
230: 
231:         Returns:
232:             The newly created PyDough GlobalContext.
233:         """
234:         return GlobalContext(self.graph)
235: 
236:     def build_child_access(
237:         self, name: str, preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG
238:     ) -> ChildAccess:
239:         """
240:         Creates a new child access QDAG node.
241: 
242:         Args:
243:             `name`: the name of the collection being referenced.
244:             `preceding_context`: the collection node from which the
245:             child access is being fetched.
246: 
247:         Returns:
248:             The newly created PyDough ChildAccess.
249: 
250:         Raises:
251:             `PyDoughMetadataException`: if `name` does not refer to a
252:             collection that `preceding_context` has access to.
253:         """
254:         term = preceding_context.get_collection(name)
255:         assert isinstance(term, ChildAccess)
256:         return term
257: 
258:     def build_calculate(
259:         self,
260:         preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
261:         children: list[PyDoughCollectionQDAG],
262:     ) -> Calculate:
263:         """
264:         Creates a CALCULATE instance, but `with_terms` still needs to be called on
265:         the output.
266: 
267:         Args:
268:             `preceding_context`: the preceding collection.
269:             `children`: the child collections accessed by the CALCULATE term.
270: 
271:         Returns:
272:             The newly created PyDough CALCULATE term.
273:         """
274:         return Calculate(preceding_context, children)
275: 
276:     def build_where(
277:         self,
278:         preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
279:         children: list[PyDoughCollectionQDAG],
280:     ) -> Where:
281:         """
282:         Creates a WHERE instance, but `with_condition` still needs to be called on
283:         the output.
284: 
285:         Args:
286:             `preceding_context`: the preceding collection.
287:             `children`: the child collections accessed by the WHERE term.
288: 
289:         Returns:
290:             The newly created PyDough WHERE instance.
291:         """
292:         return Where(preceding_context, children)
293: 
294:     def build_order(
295:         self,
296:         preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
297:         children: list[PyDoughCollectionQDAG],
298:     ) -> OrderBy:
299:         """
300:         Creates a ORDERBY instance, but `with_collation` still needs to be called on
301:         the output.
302: 
303:         Args:
304:             `preceding_context`: the preceding collection.
305:             `children`: the child collections accessed by the ORDERBY term.
306: 
307:         Returns:
308:             The newly created PyDough ORDERBY instance.
309:         """
310:         return OrderBy(preceding_context, children)
311: 
312:     def build_top_k(
313:         self,
314:         preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
315:         children: list[PyDoughCollectionQDAG],
316:         records_to_keep: int,
317:     ) -> TopK:
318:         """
319:         Creates a TOP K instance, but `with_collation` still needs to be called on
320:         the output.
321: 
322:         Args:
323:             `preceding_context`: the preceding collection.
324:             `children`: the child collections accessed by the ORDERBY term.
325:             `records_to_keep`: the `K` value in the TOP K.
326: 
327:         Returns:
328:             The newly created PyDough TOP K instance.
329:         """
330:         return TopK(preceding_context, children, records_to_keep)
331: 
332:     def build_partition(
333:         self,
334:         preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
335:         child: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
336:         name: str,
337:     ) -> PartitionBy:
338:         """
339:         Creates a PARTITION BY instance, but `with_keys` still needs to be called on
340:         the output.
341: 
342:         Args:
343:             `preceding_context`: the preceding collection.
344:             `child`: the child that is the input to the PARTITION BY term.
345:             `name`: the name that is used to refer to the partitioned data.
346: 
347:         Returns:
348:             The newly created PyDough PARTITION BY instance.
349:         """
350:         return PartitionBy(preceding_context, child, name)
351: 
352:     def build_child_reference_collection(
353:         self,
354:         preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
355:         children: list[PyDoughCollectionQDAG],
356:         child_idx: int,
357:     ) -> ChildReferenceCollection:
358:         """
359:         Creates a new reference to a collection from a child collection of a
360:         CALCULATE or other child operator.
361: 
362:         Args:
363:             `preceding_context`: the preceding collection.
364:             `children`: the child collections that the reference accesses.
365:             `child_idx`: the index of the child collection being referenced.
366: 
367:         Returns:
368:             The newly created PyDough Child Reference.
369: 
370:         Raises:
371:             `PyDoughQDAGException`: if `child_idx` is not a valid index for `children`.
372:         """
373:         if child_idx not in range(len(children)):
374:             raise PyDoughQDAGException(
375:                 f"Invalid child reference index {child_idx} with {len(children)} children"
376:             )
377:         return ChildReferenceCollection(
378:             preceding_context, children[child_idx], child_idx
379:         )
380: 
381:     def build_singular(
382:         self,
383:         preceding_context: PyDoughCollectionQDAG,
384:     ) -> Singular:
385:         """
386:         Creates a SINGULAR instance.
387: 
388:         Args:
389:             `preceding_context`: the preceding collection.
390: 
391:         Returns:
392:             The newly created PyDough SINGULAR instance.
393:         """
394:         return Singular(preceding_context)
````

## File: PyDough-5ff410e3bbe246a24b52fd56934c7b6c23da3fb0/pydough/qdag/README.md
````markdown
  1: # PyDough QDAG Module
  2: 
  3: This module deals with the qualified DAG (QDAG) structure used as an intermediary representation after unqualified nodes and before the relational tree. The QDAG nodes represent collections and expressions in a structured manner that can be further processed and transformed.
  4: 
  5: ## Available APIs
  6: 
  7: The QDAG module provides the following notable APIs:
  8: 
  9: ### Base Classes
 10: 
 11: - `PyDoughQDAG`: Base class for all QDAG nodes, including collections and expressions. Contains information about how to compare QDAG nodes for equality & place them in hash sets.
 12: 
 13: ### [Collection Nodes](collections/README.md)
 14: 
 15: The sub-module of the PyDough QDAG module class definitions for collections.
 16: 
 17: ### [Expression Nodes](expressions/README.md)
 18: 
 19: The sub-module of the PyDough QDAG module class definitions for expressions.
 20: 
 21: ### Errors
 22: 
 23: - `PyDoughQDAGException`: Exception class for errors related to QDAG nodes.
 24: 
 25: ### Node Builder
 26: 
 27: - `AstNodeBuilder`: Utility class for building QDAG nodes.
 28: 
 29: ## Usage
 30: 
 31: ### Building QDAG Nodes
 32: 
 33: To build QDAG nodes, use the `AstNodeBuilder` class. These APIs are only intended for internal use when the qualifier converts unqualified nodes into QDAG nodes.
 34: 
 35: Examples of how to use the node builder to construct QDAG nodes:
 36: 
 37: ```python
 38: from pydough.qdag import AstNodeBuilder, ChildOperatorChildAccess
 39: from pydough.metadata import parse_json_metadata_from_file
 40: from pydough.types import Int64Type, StringType
 41: 
 42: # Define the graph metadata & create a node builder
 43: graph = parse_json_metadata_from_file(...)
 44: builder = AstNodeBuilder(graph)
 45: 
 46: # Build a literal node
 47: # Equivalent PyDough code: `1`
 48: literal_node = builder.build_literal(1, Int64Type())
 49: 
 50: # Build a column property node
 51: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Orders.order_date`
 52: column_node = builder.build_column("Orders", "order_date")
 53: 
 54: # Build a back reference expression node
 55: # Equivalent PyDough code: `BACK(1).region_key`
 56: back_reference_node = builder.build_back_reference_expression(table_collection, "region_key", 1)
 57: 
 58: # Build a global context node
 59: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TCPH`
 60: global_context_node = builder.build_global_context()
 61: 
 62: # Build a table collection access
 63: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Nations`
 64: table_collection = builder.build_child_access("Nations", global_context_node)
 65: 
 66: # Build a reference node
 67: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Nations.name`
 68: reference_node = builder.build_reference(table_collection, "name")
 69: 
 70: # Build an expression function call node
 71: # Equivalent PyDough code: `LOWER(TPCH.Nations.name)`
 72: function_call_node = builder.build_expression_function_call("LOWER", [reference_node])
 73: 
 74: # Build a child reference expression node
 75: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Nations.region.name`
 76: sub_collection = builder.build_child_access("region", table_collection)
 77: child_collection = ChildOperatorChildAccess(sub_collection)
 78: child_reference_node = builder.build_child_reference_expression([child_collection], 0, "name")
 79: 
 80: # Build a CALCULATE node
 81: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Nations.CALCULATE(region_name=region.name)`
 82: calculate_node = builder.build_calc(table_collection, [child_collection])
 83: calculate_node = calculate_node.with_terms([("region_name", child_reference_node)])
 84: 
 85: # Build a WHERE node
 86: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Nations.WHERE(region.name == "ASIA")`
 87: condition = builder.build_expression_function_call(
 88:     "EQU",
 89:     [child_reference_node, builder.build_literal("ASIA", StringType())]
 90: )
 91: where_node = builder.build_where(table_collection, [child_collection])
 92: where_node = where_node.with_condition(condition)
 93: 
 94: # Build a SINGULAR node
 95: # Equivalent PyDough code: `Regions.CALCULATE(n_4_nation=nations.WHERE(key == 4).SINGULAR().name)`
 96: # Build base Regions collection
 97: global_context_node = builder.build_global_context()
 98: regions_collection = builder.build_child_access("Regions", global_context_node)
 99: # Access nations sub-collection
100: nations_sub_collection = builder.build_child_access("nations", regions_collection)
101: # Create WHERE(key == 4) condition
102: key_ref = builder.build_reference(nations_sub_collection, "key")
103: literal_4 = builder.build_literal(4, Int64Type())
104: condition = builder.build_expression_function_call("EQU", [key_ref, literal_4])
105: # Build WHERE node with condition
106: where_node = builder.build_where(nations_sub_collection, [])
107: where_node = where_node.with_condition(condition)
108: # Create SINGULAR node from filtered result
109: singular_node = builder.build_singular(where_node)
110: # Build reference node for name
111: reference_node = builder.build_reference(singular_node, "name")
112: # Build CALCULATE node with calculated term
113: calculate_node = builder.build_calc(regions_collection, [nations_sub_collection])
114: calculate_node = calculate_node.with_terms([("n_4_nation", reference_node)])
115: 
116: 
117: # Build an ORDER BY node
118: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Nations.ORDER_BY(name.ASC(na_pos='first'))`
119: collation_expression = builder.build_collation_expression(
120:     reference_node, True, False
121: )
122: order_by_node = builder.build_order(table_collection, [])
123: order_by_node = order_by_node.with_collation([collation_expression])
124: 
125: # Build a TOP K node
126: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.Nations.TOP_K(5, by=name.ASC(na_pos='first'))`
127: top_k_node = builder.build_top_k(table_collection, [], 5)
128: top_k_node = top_k_node.with_collation([collation_expression])
129: 
130: # Build a PARTITION BY node
131: # Equivalent PyDough code: `TPCH.PARTITION(Parts, name="p", by=part_type)`
132: part_collection = builder.build_child_access("Parts", global_context_node)
133: partition_key = builder.build_reference(part_collection, "part_type")
134: partition_by_node = builder.build_partition(part_collection, child_collection, "p")
135: partition_by_node = partition_by_node.with_keys([partition_key])
136: 
137: # Build a child reference collection node
138: # Equivalent PyDough code: `Nations.CALCULATE(n_customers=COUNT(customers))`
139: customers_sub_collection = builder.build_child_access("customers", table_collection)
140: customers_child = ChildOperatorChildAccess(customers_sub_collection)
141: child_reference_collection_node = builder.build_child_reference_collection(
142:     table_collection, [customers_subcollection], 0
143: )
144: child_collection = 
145: count_call = builder.build_expression_function_call(
146:     "COUNT",
147:     [child_reference_collection_node]
148: )
149: calculate_node = builder.build_calc(table_collection, [customers_child])
150: calculate_node = calculate_node.with_terms([("n_customers", count_call)])
151: 
152: # Build a window function call node
153: # Equivalent PyDough code: `RANKING(by=TPCH.Nations.name, levels=1, allow_ties=True)`
154: from pydough.operators import RANKING
155: window_call_node = builder.build_window_call(RANKING, [reference_node], 1, {"allow_ties": True})
156: ```
157: 
158: ### HAS/HASNOT Rewrite
159: 
160: The `has_hasnot_rewrite` function is used to transform `HAS` and `HASNOT` expressions in the QDAG. It is used in the `with_terms`, `with_condition`, and `with_collation` calls of the various child operator classes to rewrite all `HAS(x)` into `COUNT(X) > 0` and all `HASNOT(X)` into `COUNT(X) == 0` unless they are in the conjunction of a `WHERE` clause.
161: 
162: Below are some examples of PyDough snippets that are/aren't affected by the rewrite.
163: 
164: 
165: ```python
166: # Will be rewritten to `Customers.CALCULATE(name, has_orders=COUNT(orders) > 0)`
167: Customers.CALCULATE(name, has_orders=HAS(orders))
168: 
169: # Will be rewritten to `Customers.CALCULATE(name, never_made_order=COUNT(orders) == 0)`
170: Customers.CALCULATE(name, never_made_order=HASNOT(orders))
171: 
172: # Will not be rewritten
173: Customers.WHERE(HAS(orders) & (nation.region.name == "EUROPE"))
174: 
175: # Will not be rewritten
176: Customers.WHERE(HASNOT(orders))
177: 
178: # Will be rewritten to
179: # `Customers.WHERE((COUNT(orders) > 0) | (nation.region.name == "EUROPE"))`
180: Customers.WHERE(HAS(orders) | (nation.region.name == "EUROPE"))
181: 
182: # Will be rewritten to
183: # `Customers.WHERE((COUNT(orders) == 0) | (acct_bal < 0))`
184: Customers.WHERE(HASNOT(orders) | (acct_bal < 0))
185: ```
````
